SATIN-ACCT-001.text: - `SATIN-ACCT-001` Data size MUST count the byte table of [History Gas and the History Allowance](history-gas.md) (`SATIN-HIST-002`), plus two items that pay no history gas: an EIP-7708 transfer log, counted as `TRANSFER_LOG_SIZE` bytes ([EIP-7708 Transfer Logs](transfer-logs.md)), and an Oracle hint's input, counted by its length ([Oracle](../system-contracts/oracle.md)).

SATIN-ACCT-003.text: - `SATIN-ACCT-003` A deposit's data size MUST be counted as any transaction's, and a deposit that fails MUST keep what it counted: its body and the hints it admitted.

SATIN-ACCT-004.text:
- `SATIN-ACCT-004` A write record MUST be one account or storage write the transaction keeps.
  A storage slot's record MUST exist while the slot's value differs from its original value in the transaction: the slot's first change makes it, and writing the slot back to its original value takes it back.
  An account's record MUST exist while the account's nonce, balance or code differs from what the transaction loaded — its information at its first load in the transaction: a write that changes an unchanged account makes the record, a write that returns a changed account to what was loaded takes it back, and a write to an account that already differs adds nothing.

SATIN-ACCT-005.text:
- `SATIN-ACCT-005` These writes MUST be held to `SATIN-ACCT-004`: a value transfer's sender and recipient, on the balances the transfer leaves them; a creation's created account, which the creation leaves changed by its nonce, and the creator's nonce it bumps; a `SELFDESTRUCT`'s beneficiary and the account it clears; an applied EIP-7702 authority; and the transaction's value recipient or created account.
  A created account is no exception: an address the transaction changed before a creation lands on it — a value transfer funded it, or a `SELFDESTRUCT` paid it — differs already, and the creation adds no record for it.

SATIN-ACCT-006.text:
- `SATIN-ACCT-006` A record MUST be made where the write is, and taken back where a write returns the account or slot: a value transfer that returns an account to what the transaction loaded takes the record back in the frame the transfer starts, with its data size, and its history gas comes back to the caller once that frame returned with its start kept (`SATIN-HIST-009`); a `SELFDESTRUCT` whose move returns an account takes the record back where the opcode completed; a slot written back to its original value gives its record back.
  N value transfers from one frame to the same recipient keep one record for the recipient and one for the sender; a transfer and its exact return keep none; a recipient that passes on exactly what it received keeps none of its own; a frame that funds an address and then creates at it keeps two records, its own and the address's.

SATIN-ACCT-007.text: - `SATIN-ACCT-007` A value-transferring `CALLCODE`, which moves the value from the calling account to that same account, and a value-transferring `CALL` to the calling account itself MUST change no account and record none.

SATIN-ACCT-008.text: - `SATIN-ACCT-008` The sender's account is one of the body's fixed records (`SATIN-HIST-003`), which are data size and history bytes only and MUST NOT count as KV updates, and it MUST NOT be recorded again: validation changes it before execution, by its fee and a call's nonce, and a creation transaction's first frame by its nonce, so no write execution makes to it — a frame running as the sender, a value transfer or a `SELFDESTRUCT` that moves value to it, a keyless deployment whose signer is the sender — changes it from what the transaction loaded.

SATIN-ACCT-009.text: - `SATIN-ACCT-009` An applied EIP-7702 authority is changed by its nonce and its delegation when it is applied: a write to it afterwards, the transaction's own value to it included, MUST add no record.

SATIN-ACCT-010.text: - `SATIN-ACCT-010` The four fee accounts are in the body only for the fee credits the settlement makes, and are unchanged until execution writes them: a write execution makes to a fee account that is not the sender — a value transfer to it, a `SELFDESTRUCT` that moves a balance to it, an applied EIP-7702 authority that is one of them — MUST be recorded like a write to any other account.

SATIN-ACCT-011.text: - `SATIN-ACCT-011` A successful frame's records and bytes MUST merge into its caller's; a failed frame's MUST be discarded, the records it took back standing again, except that a creator's nonce record is the creating frame's and survives the creation's failure (`SATIN-LIM-008`).

SATIN-ACCT-012.text:
- `SATIN-ACCT-012` The KV count MUST be the write-record count, held to `TX_KV_UPDATE_LIMIT`; the five fixed records of the body (`SATIN-HIST-003`) are not in it.
  Every record MUST weigh `WRITE_RECORD_SIZE` bytes of data size, counted and taken back with it, so `KV × WRITE_RECORD_SIZE ≤ data size` at every point.
  The KV check MUST be made although, at these constants, `TX_KV_UPDATE_LIMIT` records weigh more than `TX_DATA_LIMIT` bytes; a record taken back cannot cross it.
  Logs, deployed code, transfer logs and Oracle hints are not records.

SATIN-ACCT-013.text: - `SATIN-ACCT-013` State growth MUST be the net count of new accounts and new storage slots the transaction keeps: each rise is one unit at an account-leaf or fresh-slot state charge site ([State Gas and SALT Pricing](state-gas.md)), not one unit per byte of deployed code or of a delegation indicator, whose bytes state gas still prices.

SATIN-ACCT-015.text:
- `SATIN-ACCT-015` An account that is not empty under EIP-161 MUST NOT be a rise, an authority whose account the state holds MUST NOT be one either, and neither MUST a `CALLCODE`, a value call to the calling account itself, deployed code, or a delegation indicator.
  An account whose leaf is in the state but is empty under EIP-161 is a rise or not by the predicate of its site (`SATIN-STATE-011`).

SATIN-ACCT-016.text:
- `SATIN-ACCT-016` An `SSTORE` MUST change state growth at the transitions of `SATIN-STATE-008` alone, read from the slot's original value in the transaction, its present value and the value written: +1 where that rule charges fresh-slot state gas (original zero, present zero, new non-zero), −1 where it gives it back (original zero, present non-zero, new zero), and nothing on every other transition.
  A slot written from zero to a non-zero value and then to another non-zero value rose once; written from zero to non-zero and back to zero, its net is zero; written from zero to non-zero, back to zero and to non-zero again, it rose, fell and rose.
  While its account is marked for deletion, an `SSTORE` of its slots changes nothing ([SELFDESTRUCT and the Destruction Table](selfdestruct.md)).

SATIN-ACCT-017.text: - `SATIN-ACCT-017` The fee credits the settlement writes MUST NOT be rises and are not EIP-8037 charge sites.

SATIN-ACCT-018.text:
- `SATIN-ACCT-018` A fall MUST happen at the opcode that restores the state, and a fall cannot cross a limit.
  The only slot fall is the −1 transition of `SATIN-ACCT-016`; the other falls are the destruction table's ([SELFDESTRUCT and the Destruction Table](selfdestruct.md)).

SATIN-ACCT-019.text: - `SATIN-ACCT-019` A rise that would take the signed net past the transaction limit or the frame budget is the crossing, and that rise MUST NOT be kept ([Limit Stops](limit-stops.md)).

SATIN-ACCT-020.text:
- `SATIN-ACCT-020` A failed deposit whose caller was empty under EIP-161 when the deposit was executed MUST count that account as one unit of state growth on the transaction's reported usage and on the block's counter, MUST NOT be charged state gas for it, and MUST NOT be stopped by the limit, the deposit having already failed ([Deposit Transactions](../block/deposits.md)).
  A deposit that runs to a success or a revert and creates its caller makes the ordinary charged rise of one, and a stop of its first frame keeps that account ([Limit Stops](limit-stops.md)).

SATIN-ACT-001.text:
- `SATIN-ACT-001` Satin follows Rex6 on the spec ladder.
  A node MUST execute every block whose timestamp is at or after `satinTime` under Satin, and every earlier block under the spec its timestamp resolves to.
  The block in which Satin activates is the block whose timestamp is at or after `satinTime` and whose parent's timestamp is before it (see [Base Layer](../base-layer.md), `SATIN-BASE-007`).

SATIN-ACT-002.text:
- `SATIN-ACT-002` A chain configuration's `config` object MUST schedule Satin by one key, `satinTime`, whose value is the activation timestamp: an unsigned integer of at most `MAX_TIMESTAMP`, given as a JSON number.
  Satin carries no parameter of its own: no key names a limit, a detention cap or a price, and the SequencerRegistry's bootstrap values are the keys the Rex era introduced (see [SequencerRegistry](../system-contracts/sequencer-registry.md), `SATIN-REG-009`).
  A node MUST refuse a configuration that carries a key starting with `satin`, in any ASCII letter case, that is not exactly `satinTime`, whether or not it also carries `satinTime`.
  A key given twice MUST be read as its last copy.

SATIN-ACT-003.text: - `SATIN-ACT-003` Every base fork Satin runs on — the Ethereum forks from Shanghai to Osaka and the Optimism forks from Regolith to Karst — MUST be active at `satinTime`, and a node MUST refuse a configuration that schedules Satin and leaves one of them inactive at `satinTime`.

SATIN-ACT-004.text: - `SATIN-ACT-004` The block in which Satin activates MUST admit only deposits (`SATIN-BASE-006`), and MUST make the factory check of `SATIN-ACT-005` as the third step of its pre-block sequence, before the system contracts are deployed and before its first transaction (see [System Calls and the Pre-Block Sequence](system-calls.md)).

SATIN-ACT-005.text:
- `SATIN-ACT-005` The factory check MUST read the [EIP-7997](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7997) `CREATE2` factory at `CREATE2_FACTORY_ADDRESS`, which MUST hold an account whose code hash is `CREATE2_FACTORY_CODE_HASH`; its nonce, balance and storage are not checked.
  An address with no account, an account without code, or any other code MUST make the block invalid.
  The check writes nothing: the account it reads is a read-only entry of the activation block's pre-block states (see [The Stateless Witness](stateless-witness.md)).
  No other block reads the factory before its transactions.
  The system contracts are not checked: every block, the activation block included, deploys them (`SATIN-SYSC-003`).

SATIN-ACT-006.text: - `SATIN-ACT-006` Retired, replaced by `SATIN-SYSC-003` and `SATIN-REG-008`: every block deploys the system contracts, as Rex6 does, and the activation block checks only the factory (`SATIN-ACT-005`).

SATIN-ACT-007.text: - `SATIN-ACT-007` Satin MUST NOT upgrade or write the L1 block contract: it runs on the contract the chain holds, which on a chain coming from the Rex era is OP's L1Block version 1.6.0 (Isthmus), whose data-availability footprint gas scalar and operator fee scalars are zero until the contract is upgraded and the scalars are set.

SATIN-ACT-008.text:
- `SATIN-ACT-008` Satin MUST NOT change how a block before `satinTime` executes: a node replaying history MUST resolve each block's spec from its timestamp and apply that spec's rules.
  From `satinTime` on, every account, contract and slot the earlier blocks left MUST be executed under Satin's rules: accounts, code and storage carry over unchanged and run under Satin's prices, pools and limits.
  A contract deployed under an earlier spec is not promised the outcome it had under that spec for the same gas: a gas budget fixed for Rex prices — a gas argument, a stored per-call limit, a signed gas limit — can be too small under Satin's prices — by about five times for a call that writes a fresh slot or creates an account without a reservoir — or larger than needed, as for deployed code, whose price per byte fell ([Two-Pool Gas](../evm/gas-model.md), [State Gas and SALT Pricing](../evm/state-gas.md)).

SATIN-ACT-009.text:
- `SATIN-ACT-009` Part of the execution configuration is fixed by the spec, whatever a node supplies: the Satin gas schedule and the byte prices of state and history gas; EIP-8037, EIP-2780 and EIP-7708 on; the execution cap; the chain-id check on; the code and initcode size limits; the per-transaction limits, the per-frame share and the detention caps; and the block's packing budgets.
  A node MUST execute every Satin block on these values and on no value its configuration or a block names, and a node that reads the configuration before it executes — to estimate gas against the execution cap, for one — MUST read these values.
  The values are those of the pages that state the rules: [Gas Schedule and Intrinsic Gas](../evm/gas-schedule.md), [State Gas and SALT Pricing](../evm/state-gas.md), [History Gas](../evm/history-gas.md), [Two-Pool Gas](../evm/gas-model.md), [Contract Size Limits](../evm/contract-limits.md), [Resource Limits](../evm/resource-limits.md), [Gas Detention](../evm/gas-detention.md), [Transaction Validation and Refusals](transaction-validation.md) and [Block Limits and Packing](block-limits.md).

SATIN-ACT-010.text:
- `SATIN-ACT-010` A node MUST work out, for every block it builds or validates, whether the block admits only deposits (`SATIN-BASE-006`) and whether Satin activates in it, from the chain configuration and the parent block's timestamp, and MUST execute the block accordingly; neither may be left to an input a caller can omit.
  The two differ: an Optimism fork's activation block admits only deposits and checks no factory.

SATIN-ACT-011.text:
- `SATIN-ACT-011` A chain configuration that schedules Satin MUST schedule every Mega spec below it on the spec ladder — MiniRex, Rex, Rex1, Rex2, Rex3, Rex4, Rex5 and Rex6 — each at or before the timestamp of the spec above it, and MAY omit only the alias specs MiniRex1 and MiniRex2, which carry no setup of their own.
  A Satin block deploys every system contract whatever earlier specs the configuration scheduled (`SATIN-SYSC-003`), so what a block sets up before its transactions follows from its place on the ladder.

SATIN-ACT-012.text:
- `SATIN-ACT-012` Satin MAY be active from genesis, `satinTime` at or before the genesis block's timestamp, as Rex6 may be.
  Such a chain has no block in which Satin activates: none of its blocks admits only deposits for Satin's sake or checks the factory, and the pre-block sequence of its first block installs every system contract the genesis state does not hold and seeds a SequencerRegistry it does not hold from the configuration's bootstrap values (`SATIN-SYSC-003`, `SATIN-REG-008`, `SATIN-REG-009`); the genesis block itself makes no EIP-2935 or EIP-4788 call (`SATIN-PBLK-003`).

SATIN-AUTH-001.text:
- `SATIN-AUTH-001` Before the first frame of an EIP-7702 transaction, a node MUST decide its authorization list by simulating EIP-7702 application in list order, whatever the length of the list.
  A node MUST NOT omit the simulation for a list too short to cross either limit.
  The simulation MUST write nothing and warm nothing.

SATIN-AUTH-002.text: - `SATIN-AUTH-002` An entry whose chain id is neither zero nor the chain's, whose nonce is `2^64 − 1`, or whose signature does not recover an authority MUST be skipped, and its authority's account MUST NOT be read.

SATIN-AUTH-003.text:
- `SATIN-AUTH-003` Every other entry MUST load its authority's account with its code.
  An authority whose account holds code other than an EIP-7702 delegation indicator MUST be skipped, and its simulated nonce MUST NOT be bumped.

SATIN-AUTH-005.text:
- `SATIN-AUTH-005` The simulation MUST walk the whole list and MUST NOT stop at the first entry that would cross a limit.
  Each distinct authority whose entry passed the chain-id, nonce and signature gates of `SATIN-AUTH-002` MUST be loaded once, and a later entry for that authority MUST use the simulated nonce and the code already loaded.
  Every authority so loaded is in the block's witness, whether or not the list is applied ([The Stateless Witness](../block/stateless-witness.md)).

SATIN-AUTH-006.text:
- `SATIN-AUTH-006` A failure to read an authority the simulation consults is a fault of the transaction's execution, reported as `SATIN-VAL-010` classifies it ([Transaction Validation and Refusals](../block/transaction-validation.md)).
  The block MUST NOT be refused for the limit instead, also when an earlier prefix of the list would already have crossed.

SATIN-AUTH-007.text: - `SATIN-AUTH-007` The simulation MUST charge no gas, a cold access included; the intrinsic `PER_AUTH_BASE_COST` of every entry is already charged by validation, applied or not ([Gas Schedule and Intrinsic Gas](gas-schedule.md)).

SATIN-AUTH-009.text:
- `SATIN-AUTH-009` Delegation-indicator state gas MUST be charged at most once per authority, and only when an accepted authorization writes a non-zero delegation designator, the authority holds no delegation indicator at the start of the transaction, and no earlier authorization in the list set one for it.
  An authority that holds an indicator at the start of the transaction is charged none, a clear and a later non-zero authorization included; a clear charges none and gives back none, an indicator an earlier authorization of the list set and paid for included; two accepted non-zero authorizations for an authority that holds none at the start charge it once.
  An authorization with a zero delegation target still bumps the nonce and can create the account, and charges no indicator.
  The indicator is not a unit of state growth.

SATIN-AUTH-010.section: Specification > A list that does not fit
SATIN-AUTH-010.text:
- `SATIN-AUTH-010` If the list's KV or state-growth total would exceed the transaction's KV-update or state-growth limit, given what the body and the counts before it left ([Resource Limits](resource-limits.md)), the node MUST apply none of the list, MUST charge none of its authorities' state gas or record history, and MUST stop the transaction's own frame before it runs, with `MegaLimitExceeded` of the crossed kind and that transaction limit ([Limit Stops](limit-stops.md)).
  No frame budget exists yet, so the stop names the transaction limit; when both would be crossed the kind is 1.
  Data size cannot be crossed here, since validation refuses a body that, with `WRITE_RECORD_SIZE` bytes for each authorization entry, exceeds the data-size limit ([Transaction Validation and Refusals](../block/transaction-validation.md)), and compute does not apply.

SATIN-AUTH-011.section: Specification > A list that does not fit
SATIN-AUTH-011.text:
- `SATIN-AUTH-011` A skipped list MUST keep no authority account, no authority write record, no authority state gas and no authority history; no delegation is written, and no authority nonce is bumped beyond the sender's validation bump.
  The intrinsic regular gas, the body's history gas and the body's data size stay.

SATIN-AUTH-012.section: Specification > A list that does not fit
SATIN-AUTH-012.text: - `SATIN-AUTH-012` On a skip the authorities the simulation consulted MUST NOT be made warm, except one already warm from the transaction's start: the sender, the recipient of a call, the block beneficiary, an access-list address or a precompile ([Gas Schedule and Intrinsic Gas](gas-schedule.md)).

SATIN-AUTH-013.section: Specification > A list that does not fit
SATIN-AUTH-013.text: - `SATIN-AUTH-013` The skip MUST be all or nothing, including an authority that would have fitted by itself, and MUST be settled as a revert-class stop of the transaction's own frame, which settles as `SATIN-STOP-009` states ([Limit Stops](limit-stops.md)).

SATIN-AUTH-014.text: - `SATIN-AUTH-014` A list that fits MUST be applied as EIP-7702 applies it, which warms every authority whose account the application loads: an entry skipped for its chain id, for a nonce of `2^64 − 1` or for a signature that does not recover an authority is not loaded and is not warmed; an entry skipped because its authority's code is not a delegation, or because its nonce does not match, is loaded before that check, and its authority is warmed.

SATIN-AUTH-015.text:
- `SATIN-AUTH-015` The authorities' state gas, their `ACCOUNT_WRITE` ([Gas Schedule and Intrinsic Gas](gas-schedule.md)) and the history of their write records MUST be charged when the list is applied, in the order of `SATIN-SCHED-008`, and reduce what the first frame is given.
  `ACCOUNT_WRITE` MUST be charged only for an authority whose account write the transaction has not paid already: not for the sender, not for the recipient of a transaction that carries a non-zero value, and not for an authority an earlier applied authorization wrote.
  An EIP-7702 transaction from A that sends 1 wei to an existing B, with empty calldata and access list, whose one authorization by B carries B's current nonce and a zero delegation target, therefore costs 68,504 gas before its first frame — 21,000 of intrinsic base and value cost, 7,816 for the entry, and `(310 + 101 + 40) × 88` of history for the body, the entry and B's one write record, which the value to B does not make again (`SATIN-ACCT-009`) — and no `ACCOUNT_WRITE`, no indicator and no new-account state gas.
  If one of those charges cannot be paid, the transaction MUST take the pre-frame out-of-gas path of `SATIN-SCHED-009`: the authorizations are taken back, and for a transaction other than a deposit this is an out-of-gas halt, not a limit stop.
  The limit is decided before those charges, so a list that does not fit never takes that path.

SATIN-AUTH-016.text: - `SATIN-AUTH-016` When the list fits, a later stop or revert of the first frame MUST keep the authorizations, with their state gas, their write records and the history those records cost (`SATIN-STOP-011`).

SATIN-AUTH-017.text: - `SATIN-AUTH-017` The caller account a deposit creates is not an authorization and MUST NOT be held to the list rule of this page; it is created, charged and counted as `SATIN-DEP-003` specifies ([Deposit Transactions](../block/deposits.md)).

SATIN-AUTH-018.text: - `SATIN-AUTH-018` The list rule MUST be decided during execution, where the authorities are read; it is not a rejection a transaction pool can make before inclusion.

SATIN-BASE-001.text:
- `SATIN-BASE-001` Every standard EVM, transaction and block rule that the Satin section does not override MUST be Optimism Karst's, including the Optimism changes of Jovian and Karst and the Ethereum changes of Osaka (for example `CLZ` of [EIP-7939](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7939)).
  Satin follows the Optimism forks it requires — Karst, Jovian and their predecessors — with their whole transaction and block rule set, the data-availability footprint gas scalar, the blob gas used a block reports and the fee rules among them, and not rule by rule.
  Where a page of the Satin section states a rule, that rule MUST be applied in place of the base layer's.

SATIN-BASE-002.text:
- `SATIN-BASE-002` A node MUST NOT apply the per-transaction gas limit cap of [EIP-7825](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7825).
  A transaction's gas limit MUST be bounded by what its block's gas limit has left (see [Block Limits and Packing](block/block-limits.md)); its regular gas is bounded by the execution cap (see [Two-Pool Gas](evm/gas-model.md)).
  A block builder MAY refuse a larger declared gas limit as building policy, which a node validating a block MUST NOT apply (see [Block Limits and Packing](block/block-limits.md)).

SATIN-BASE-003.text: - `SATIN-BASE-003` A node MUST NOT apply the [EIP-8037](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8037) per-transaction cap `TX_MAX_TOTAL_GAS_LIMIT` on a transaction's total gas.

SATIN-BASE-004.text: - `SATIN-BASE-004` A node MUST enable `DUPN` (`DUPN_OPCODE`), `SWAPN` (`SWAPN_OPCODE`) and `EXCHANGE` (`EXCHANGE_OPCODE`) as [EIP-8024](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8024) as of [commit `34b49095ca`](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/commit/34b49095ca5f7343045da279f04e7ecd1e451393) (10 June 2026) defines them, the revision current when the EIP-8037 profile was frozen (see [Two-Pool Gas](evm/gas-model.md)).

SATIN-BASE-005.text:
- `SATIN-BASE-005` A node MUST enable `SLOTNUM` (`SLOTNUM_OPCODE`) of [EIP-7843](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7843) as of [commit `e44e1960a9`](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/commit/e44e1960a9328282af8dd884837c2302f6a45c3d) (17 September 2026), and `SLOTNUM` MUST push zero in every block.
  `SLOTNUM` is a read of the block environment: it is a volatile read for [gas detention](evm/gas-detention.md), and a frame whose volatile-data access is off is refused it (see [MegaAccessControl](system-contracts/mega-access-control.md)).

SATIN-BASE-006.text:
- `SATIN-BASE-006` A block in which Satin activates, or in which an Optimism fork at or after Jovian in the Optimism fork order activates, MUST contain only deposit transactions.
  A non-deposit transaction in such a block MUST make the block invalid.
  The rule covers Jovian, Karst and every later Optimism fork the chain configuration schedules.

SATIN-BASE-007.text:
- `SATIN-BASE-007` A fork MUST be taken to activate in a block when the chain configuration schedules it, it is active at the block's timestamp, and it is not active at the parent block's timestamp.
  A fork the chain configuration does not schedule MUST NOT be taken to activate in any block.

SATIN-BASE-008.text:
- `SATIN-BASE-008` A Mega System Transaction is a legacy transaction, so a block that admits only deposits MUST NOT contain one either.
  The block in which Satin activates therefore carries no Mega System Transaction, and no Oracle read in it asks the oracle service (see [Oracle](system-contracts/oracle.md), `SATIN-ORCL-005`).
  A deposit can still write the Oracle in that block through code running at the live system address, as the Oracle's bytecode allows (`SATIN-ORCL-011`).

SATIN-BASE-009.text:
- `SATIN-BASE-009` A non-deposit transaction's data-availability footprint MUST be its estimated compressed size, as the Optimism Fjord specification estimates it, times the data-availability footprint gas scalar the L1 block contract (`L1_BLOCK_ADDRESS`) holds when the transaction is about to run; with no contract or no scalar in state the scalar MUST be taken as zero.
  A Mega System Transaction is a non-deposit transaction and has a footprint; a deposit has none.
  The footprints of a block's non-deposit transactions MUST accumulate against the block's gas limit: the sum MUST NOT exceed the block's gas limit, and the block MUST report the sum as its blob gas used.
  A transaction whose footprint does not fit in what the block's gas limit has left for footprints MUST NOT be included in the block (see [Block Limits and Packing](block/block-limits.md)).

SATIN-BASE-010.section: Specification > Pricing against the L1 block information
SATIN-BASE-010.text:
- `SATIN-BASE-010` Every non-deposit transaction that pays an L1 fee — every non-deposit transaction but a Mega System Transaction, which pays no fee (`SATIN-MST-005`) — MUST be priced against the L1 block information the block's own L1 attributes deposit wrote.
  That information MUST be what the L1 block contract holds on the state left by the transactions before the block's first non-deposit transaction other than a Mega System Transaction, and it MUST hold for every later transaction of the block.
  The data-availability footprint gas scalar is the exception: it MUST be read from the contract again before each non-deposit transaction, a Mega System Transaction included.
  The contract's slots are read as the base layer's fee computation and footprint read them, when they need them; that every slot either read makes is in the block's witness is specified in [The Stateless Witness](block/stateless-witness.md) (`SATIN-WIT-011`).

SATIN-BASE-011.text:
- `SATIN-BASE-011` A state from which a transaction's execution reaches a value transfer that would push the recipient's balance above 2^256 − 1 is an invalid prestate, and the execution of such a transaction lies outside this specification, whatever it would do next.
  This holds for every value transfer: a transaction's value, a deposit's included, a `CALL`'s value, a `SELFDESTRUCT`'s balance sent to its beneficiary, and a creation's endowment of the account it creates.
  A deposit's mint that would overflow its sender's balance is the same case, stated in [Deposit Transactions](block/deposits.md) (`SATIN-DEP-011`).

SATIN-BLK-001.text: - `SATIN-BLK-001` A block MUST count, for each transaction it includes, the transaction's regular gas as `max(regular, floor)`, its state gas, its history gas, its history bytes (`SATIN-HIST-022`), its data size, its KV updates and its state growth, as the transaction reports them (see [Two-Pool Gas](../evm/gas-model.md), [History Gas](../evm/history-gas.md) and [Resource Accounting](../evm/resource-accounting.md)).

SATIN-BLK-002.text: - `SATIN-BLK-002` Three of those counts are limited, each checked before the next transaction runs: data size against `BLOCK_DATA_LIMIT`, KV updates (write records) against `BLOCK_KV_UPDATE_LIMIT`, and state growth (new accounts and new slots) against `BLOCK_STATE_GROWTH_LIMIT`.

SATIN-BLK-003.text:
- `SATIN-BLK-003` A block reaches a limit when its counter is at or above it.
  The transaction that moves a counter from below its limit to the limit, or past it, MUST be included; once a limit is reached, every later transaction that is not a deposit MUST be skipped before it runs, a Mega System Transaction included.
  When more than one limit is reached, a node MAY report the skip in the order data size, KV updates, state growth; two nodes need not name the same one, and a skip leaves no field in the block.

SATIN-BLK-004.text:
- `SATIN-BLK-004` A builder that executes several candidate transactions before it commits one MUST hold each candidate, when it commits it, to the block's packing budgets, the block gas limit and the data-availability footprint again, on the block as it then stands; a candidate that no longer fits MUST NOT be committed.
  A validator commits every transaction before it executes the next, so for it the second check finds what the first found.

SATIN-BLK-005.text:
- `SATIN-BLK-005` Such a builder MUST NOT commit a candidate whose sender's nonce or balance — the system address's, for a Mega System Transaction — another commit changed after the candidate executed; the refusal is a fault of the builder's ordering, neither a verdict on the block nor on the transaction, which the builder executes again.
  Any other state a candidate read and a later commit changed is the builder's to account for, by executing the candidate again; a candidate that read the Oracle before a Mega System Transaction that writes it, and is committed after that transaction, commits the value it read.

SATIN-BLK-006.text: - `SATIN-BLK-006` A deposit (a transaction whose envelope is a deposit) MUST NOT be refused by any of the three budgets, nor by any building policy, and MUST count toward each; the block decides this from the transaction's envelope, before the transaction runs.

SATIN-BLK-007.text: - `SATIN-BLK-007` A Mega System Transaction MUST be held to the three packing budgets, to building policy, to the block gas limit and, its envelope being legacy, to the block's data-availability footprint (see [Base Layer](../base-layer.md)), as any other non-deposit transaction is, and MUST count toward each.

SATIN-BLK-008.text: - `SATIN-BLK-008` Execution gas, state gas and history gas MUST have no block limit beyond the block gas limit, and history bytes MUST be reported and not limited.

SATIN-BLK-009.section: Specification > The block gas limit and skipping
SATIN-BLK-009.text: - `SATIN-BLK-009` A transaction's declared gas limit MUST fit in what the block's gas limit has left, as the base layer defines it.

SATIN-BLK-010.text: - `SATIN-BLK-010` The three packing budgets are protocol values fixed by the spec, the same on every chain; no chain configuration carries them, and a node validating a block MUST hold the block to these values and to no other.

SATIN-BLK-011.text:
- `SATIN-BLK-011` A block builder MAY pack tighter than these rules, as building policy: it MAY refuse a transaction for its declared gas limit, its encoded size or its data-availability size, hold the block to an encoded-size or data-availability budget, and hold any of the three packing budgets below the protocol's value, never above it; and it MAY pack fewer transactions than the budgets allow by not selecting them.
  A building policy MUST NOT refuse a deposit: none of its per-transaction limits or budgets applies to one, and a policy's cap on a packing budget does not; it applies to a Mega System Transaction as to any other non-deposit transaction.
  A deposit counts toward the block's encoded size and not toward its data-availability size; a Mega System Transaction counts toward both.
  A node validating a block MUST NOT apply a building policy, and a block is not invalid for a transaction a building policy would have skipped.

SATIN-BLK-012.text: - `SATIN-BLK-012` A transaction's and a block's encoded size MUST NOT be limited by these rules; a block-size rule of the base layer, where a chain adopts one, is the node's to apply and is not one of these limits.

SATIN-BLK-013.section: Specification > The block gas limit and skipping

SATIN-DEP-001.section: Specification > What a deposit pays and is held to
SATIN-DEP-001.text: - `SATIN-DEP-001` That a deposit pays history gas as any transaction does — for its body, its calldata, its logs, its write records and its deposited code — is the rule `SATIN-HIST-016` (see [History Gas](../evm/history-gas.md)); a deposit whose gas limit cannot pay its intrinsic regular gas and its body's history gas fails validation, and so is a failed deposit (`SATIN-VAL-002`, `SATIN-DEP-004`).

SATIN-DEP-002.section: Specification > What a deposit pays and is held to
SATIN-DEP-002.text: - `SATIN-DEP-002` That a deposit which is not system-originated is priced by the SALT bucket its state lands in, held to every per-transaction limit and frame budget, and detained after a read of volatile data, as any transaction is, is the rule of `SATIN-STATE-009`, `SATIN-LIM-001` and `SATIN-DET-026`; which deposits are system-originated is `SATIN-MST-010` (see [Mega System Transactions](../system-contracts/system-tx.md)).

SATIN-DEP-003.section: Specification > What a deposit pays and is held to
SATIN-DEP-003.text:
- `SATIN-DEP-003` A deposit — or a Mega System Transaction, which executes as one — whose caller is empty under EIP-161 when the deposit is executed (no account, or nonce zero, zero balance and no code: `SATIN-STATE-011`) MUST be charged that account's new-account state gas exactly once, before its first frame, as the first charge of `SATIN-SCHED-008`, priced at the caller's bucket (at `m = 1` for a system-originated one).
  The account MUST always be created and kept, whatever the deposit then does, and it MUST count as one unit of state growth; being one account, it cannot by itself cross the state-growth limit.

SATIN-DEP-004.text:
- `SATIN-DEP-004` A deposit MUST become a failed deposit when it fails a validation check (see [Transaction Validation and Refusals](transaction-validation.md)), when it cannot pay a charge made before its first frame (the state gas of the caller account it creates, among them), or when its own frame halts — a first frame whose value the sender, its mint credited, cannot fund included.
  A failed deposit MUST bump its sender's nonce, MUST credit its mint to its sender, MUST use its whole gas limit, the reservoir included, and MUST apply nothing else: every other change its execution made is taken back.

SATIN-DEP-005.text:
- `SATIN-DEP-005` A failed deposit MUST report its whole gas limit as regular gas, and no state gas and no history gas, on the transaction's ledgers and on the block's.
  The caller account it creates for a sender that was empty under EIP-161 (`SATIN-STATE-011`) carries no state gas, unlike the one a deposit that runs to a success or a revert creates, and it MUST still count as one unit of state growth, on the transaction's reported usage and on the block's counter.

SATIN-DEP-006.text: - `SATIN-DEP-006` A failed deposit MUST keep the data size of its body and of the Oracle hints it admitted (see [Oracle](../system-contracts/oracle.md)), and MUST return no withheld gas, no unspent gas and no reservoir to its sender.

SATIN-DEP-007.section: Specification > What a deposit pays and is held to
SATIN-DEP-007.text: - `SATIN-DEP-007` That a deposit whose own frame succeeds, reverts or is stopped by a limit settles as an ordinary transaction, a stop being a revert and not a failed deposit, is the rule `SATIN-STOP-010` with `SATIN-OUT-014` (see [Halts, Reverts and Stops](../evm/outcomes.md)).

SATIN-DEP-008.text:
- `SATIN-DEP-008` A deposit whose caller is the live system address MUST be a failed deposit (see [Mega System Transactions](../system-contracts/system-tx.md), `SATIN-MST-003`), and so MUST one handed to the node already carrying the promotion's source hash from that address.
  A deposit that carries the base layer's system-transaction flag, which the base layer refuses from Regolith on, MUST be a failed deposit too.

SATIN-DEP-009.section: Specification > What a deposit pays and is held to
SATIN-DEP-009.text: - `SATIN-DEP-009` That a deposit pays nothing for its gas, and that where the [EIP-7623](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7623) floor binds its gas used only its receipt's gas used and the block's figures move, is the rule `SATIN-HIST-017` (see [History Gas](../evm/history-gas.md)).

SATIN-DEP-010.section: Specification > What a deposit pays and is held to
SATIN-DEP-010.text:
- `SATIN-DEP-010` A deposit that creates a contract from a sender whose nonce is `MAX_NONCE`, which cannot be bumped, and whose balance, its mint credited, funds the deposit's value, MUST succeed with nothing created and nothing counted for the creation: no account at the address the creation would derive, no state gas for it, no record and no state growth, the gas of its first frame untouched.
  The value is checked first: a sender at `MAX_NONCE` that cannot fund the value makes the deposit a failed deposit (`SATIN-DEP-004`), before the nonce is considered.

SATIN-DEP-011.text: - `SATIN-DEP-011` A state in which a deposit's sender's balance plus the deposit's mint exceeds `MAX_BALANCE` when the deposit is executed is an invalid prestate: the execution of such a deposit, whether it would succeed or fail, lies outside this specification.

SATIN-DEP-012.text:
- `SATIN-DEP-012` A deposit that fails before its first frame MUST make no load for its first frame's start: nothing of its recipient, nor of the account its creation would create, beyond what it loads in another role (its sender, when the recipient is the sender, is loaded all the same); it MUST load its sender's code only once its intrinsic gas and floor checks have passed, so a deposit that fails one of them loads none of it.
  What a deposit that fails loads otherwise is what [The Stateless Witness](stateless-witness.md) specifies for every transaction.

SATIN-DEP-013.text: - `SATIN-DEP-013` A deposit has no gas price: an envelope that presents itself as a deposit and carries a gas price is malformed, and its execution lies outside this specification.

SATIN-DET-002.text: - `SATIN-DET-002` `BLOBHASH` MUST NOT be a volatile read: it reads the transaction's own blob hashes.

SATIN-DET-003.text:
- `SATIN-DET-003` A read MUST be marked where its opcode loads the value, and only once the opcode completed; a load that fails, and a read whose opcode then fails, MUST mark nothing.
  An Oracle read is the exception: it MUST be marked when it is made, before its cold access is charged, and the mark MUST stand for the rest of the transaction though the `SLOAD` then runs out of gas or is stopped ([Oracle](../system-contracts/oracle.md), `SATIN-ORCL-004`), its `compute_at_read` the compute before that charge.
  A call opcode's read of the beneficiary's account — as the call's target or as the EIP-7702 delegate it follows — completes when the start is decided: it MUST be marked after the opcode's charges and its forward, before the child runs its first instruction, and not when the call returns.
  Its `compute_at_read` (`SATIN-DET-012`) MUST NOT include the regular gas the call forwards: the caller's compute at that point is its regular gas spent less that forward, as `SATIN-DET-009` counts a suspended caller.
  A transaction's read of `SATIN-DET-008` is marked before its first frame, at compute zero: the charges made before the first frame are not compute (`SATIN-DET-009`), so the limit it sets is the cap.

SATIN-DET-004.text: - `SATIN-DET-004` Every `BLOCKHASH` MUST be a read of the block environment, whatever its operand: the opcode loads the block number before it decides whether its operand is in range, so one of the current block, of a future block or of a block outside the last 256 is a read, and one in range reads the hash as well.

SATIN-DET-005.text:
- `SATIN-DET-005` A call to the EIP-2935 history contract MUST be a read of the block environment only when, and where, the contract's code completes a `NUMBER`, by `SATIN-DET-001` and `SATIN-DET-003`; the call itself MUST NOT be marked.
  The contract's `get` path executes `NUMBER` before it loads the slot, so a call that reaches the load is a read; a call that fails before its `NUMBER` — forwarded too little gas to reach it, or refused by the contract's input check that comes first — marks nothing.
  An `SLOAD` of the storage the EIP-2935 and EIP-4788 pre-block calls write MUST NOT be a volatile read: it is state committed before the block's first transaction.

SATIN-DET-006.text:
- `SATIN-DET-006` A `CREATE` or `CREATE2` MUST NOT be marked as a read, and MUST NOT be refused in a frame whose volatile-data access is off ([MegaAccessControl](../system-contracts/mega-access-control.md)), also when its creator or its created address is the block beneficiary: its loads of them — the creator's, to check its balance and nonce, and the created address's, to decide the created account's state gas — are the creation's own checks.
  A creation transaction is not detained from its start because its created address is the block beneficiary.

SATIN-DET-007.text: - `SATIN-DET-007` A frame running as the beneficiary MUST mark the beneficiary's account by its own `SELFBALANCE`, `SELFDESTRUCT` and the other reads of `SATIN-DET-001`, and with access off is refused them ([MegaAccessControl](../system-contracts/mega-access-control.md)).

SATIN-DET-008.text: - `SATIN-DET-008` A transaction whose sender, call recipient or applied EIP-7702 authority is the block beneficiary MUST be detained from its start, as a read of the beneficiary's account made before its first frame.

SATIN-DET-009.text: - `SATIN-DET-009` A transaction's compute MUST be every regular charge its frames make, whoever funds it: the running frame's regular gas spent, plus every suspended caller's, each less the regular gas it forwarded to its child, less the state and history gas its regular gas paid — a legacy share (`SATIN-STATE-012`) or a part the reservoir could not pay —, also when that charge is later given back into a reservoir by a take-back or a rollback, and less what halting frames burned (`SATIN-DET-011`).

SATIN-DET-010.text:
- `SATIN-DET-010` A value call's `CALL_STIPEND` is not forwarded gas: what the callee runs on it MUST count as compute, as the rest of what it runs does.
  The stipend MUST NOT lower compute either: when a value call returns, what the callee left of the stipend comes back to its caller with the rest of the callee's gas, and compute MUST NOT fall with the caller's spent regular gas.
  Compute can therefore exceed the transaction's regular ledger by the stipends of its value calls.

SATIN-DET-011.text:
- `SATIN-DET-011` What a halting frame burns — the regular gas it had left when it halted — MUST NOT count as compute, whatever it could not pay: a dynamic charge, an opcode's static gas, a cold access, or state or history gas its regular gas had to pay.
  A precompile that runs out of gas MUST count nothing of its forward as compute: it burns the forward, a value call's stipend included, unless it is the crossing (`SATIN-DET-021`), and then the forward returns to its caller.
  A precompile that halts (out of gas, or on a check it makes after its gas charge, a ModExp input over EIP-7823's bound among them) burns its whole forward, its charged price and a value call's stipend included, and MUST count none of it as compute; only a precompile that is the crossing (`SATIN-DET-021`) returns its forward.

SATIN-DET-012.text:
- `SATIN-DET-012` A volatile read MUST set `limit = compute_at_read + cap` when it lowers the transaction's limit, and the limit MUST only go down, so the most restrictive read binds:
  - `compute_at_read` — the transaction's compute when the read is marked.
  - `cap` — `BLOCK_ENV_ACCESS_COMPUTE_GAS` for a read of the block environment or of the beneficiary's account, and `ORACLE_ACCESS_COMPUTE_GAS` for a read of the Oracle's storage.

SATIN-DET-013.text:
- `SATIN-DET-013` The caps are protocol values fixed by the spec with the other limits (`SATIN-LIM-017`), and MUST NOT be taken from configuration.
  Both are below `MAX_TX_COMPUTE_GAS`, `EXECUTION_CAP − TX_BASE_COST − WARM_STORAGE_READ_COST`: the execution cap less the base cost every transaction pays and the least a frame pays for the code it runs, the most regular gas a transaction's frames can spend from its regular budget net of the stipends that come back to their callers.
  It is not a bound on compute: a transaction's compute can exceed it by the stipends of its value calls (`SATIN-DET-010`), as 18,000 value calls of 1 wei that each forward no gas to an account with no code spend 163,800,000 net regular gas and count at least 205,200,000 of compute.
  That the caps are below it means only that either cap can be reached within a transaction's regular budget.

SATIN-DET-014.text:
- `SATIN-DET-014` Once a limit is set, every frame's regular gas MUST be split into a spendable part, held at what the limit leaves the transaction (`limit − compute`, or zero once compute has reached the limit), and a withheld part, the rest of the frame's regular gas.
  The split MUST be applied when the read's opcode completes and when a frame starts or resumes; no give-back raises a frame's regular gas within the frame (`SATIN-HIST-012`), so nothing else can move it.

SATIN-DET-015.text:
- `SATIN-DET-015` Only a regular charge MUST be limited to the spendable part.
  Every other reader of the frame's gas MUST see both parts: `GAS`, the forward of [Gas Forwarding](gas-forwarding.md) and the clamp of an explicit call gas, the `SSTORE` minimum-gas check, the checks that decide whether a cold load is attempted, the gas a child returns, and the settlement at the end of the transaction.

SATIN-DET-016.text:
- `SATIN-DET-016` At the settlement the withheld part MUST be unspent gas: it returns to the sender with the rest of the unspent gas, and it is not part of the gas used that caps the EIP-3529 refund.
  A failed deposit returns none of it, as it returns no unspent gas and no reservoir ([Deposit Transactions](../block/deposits.md)).

SATIN-DET-017.text: - `SATIN-DET-017` A forward, and the part of a state or history charge that regular gas pays — its legacy share, and what the reservoir cannot pay — MUST draw the withheld part first.

SATIN-DET-018.text:
- `SATIN-DET-018` A regular charge that the spendable part cannot pay but the frame's whole regular gas can is the crossing: the charge MUST NOT be made, the frame's gas MUST be put back to what it was before the charge, and the frame MUST be stopped with `MegaLimitExceeded(2, limit)` ([Limit Stops](limit-stops.md)).
  What the frame spent before the crossing charge stays spent, and its caller MUST get back everything the frame had, the withheld part included.
  For a call refused at its target's EIP-7702 delegate, the restoration and the charges of `SATIN-MAC-004` MUST be applied before this rule decides the crossing: the call's gas is restored to what it held at the opcode, its static cost and its memory expansion are charged again, and only its cold surcharge, charged last, can cross, so the value-transfer cost the restoration gave back is not among what stays spent ([MegaAccessControl](../system-contracts/mega-access-control.md), `SATIN-MAC-007`).
  In general, each part an inherited opcode deducts from regular gas MUST be one charge, held to the spendable part where the opcode deducts it, in the opcode's order: its static cost (`SATIN-SCHED-002`), then each dynamic part it deducts on its own, as the base layer has them (`SATIN-BASE-001`).
  The first part the spendable part cannot pay decides, against the regular gas the frame holds at that part: it is the crossing when the frame's whole regular gas can pay it and an out-of-gas when it cannot (`SATIN-DET-020`), whatever the parts after it would cost.
  The charges stated as one are the exceptions: an Oracle read's cold access (`SATIN-ORCL-004`) and an interceptor's answer (`SATIN-DET-025`).
  A `BALANCE` of an account that is not warm, in a frame with 50 of spendable gas and 1,000 of regular gas in all, is stopped at its static cost of `WARM_STORAGE_READ_COST`, which the 1,000 can pay; it does not run out of gas on the 3,000 the access costs in all.

SATIN-DET-019.text:
- `SATIN-DET-019` At the crossing the transaction's compute is at most the limit and less than the crossing charge short of it; a caller the stop returns into MUST resume held to what the limit leaves the transaction, so any regular charge of its own past that is a crossing too.
  What a halting frame burns adds nothing to compute, while its paid work before the halt still counts, so no halt takes the transaction's compute past the limit: the compute since a read is at most its cap.

SATIN-DET-020.text: - `SATIN-DET-020` A regular charge beyond the frame's whole regular gas, and every other out-of-gas, MUST halt as it would without the read.

SATIN-DET-022.text:
- `SATIN-DET-022` The call's value has not moved when the price is consulted, so a call that is the crossing MUST be held to the price alone: the stop is kind 2, whatever records and state growth its value transfer would have made.
  A value call to a precompile whose account the state does not hold, or holds empty under EIP-161 (`SATIN-STATE-011`), pays that account's new-account state gas in the opcode, before its forward is computed and before the price is consulted (`SATIN-HIST-010`, `SATIN-HIST-023`); when the call is the crossing, the account is not created, and that charge, its legacy share included, MUST be given back into the caller's reservoir when the stop returns (`SATIN-POOL-015`).

SATIN-DET-024.text:
- `SATIN-DET-024` An input priced between the allowance and the forward that would fail a check the precompile makes after its gas charge — a ModExp input over EIP-7823's bound among them — is the crossing too.
  A call refused on its caller's account — a value the caller cannot fund — runs no precompile and MUST be answered as without the read.

SATIN-DET-025.text:
- `SATIN-DET-025` A system contract's intercepted answer ([Call Interception](../system-contracts/interception.md)) that spent more regular gas than the frame's allowance, state and history gas its regular gas paid not counted, MUST be the crossing.
  The answer's whole regular spend MUST be treated as the one charge that crossed: none of it is billed, the part within the allowance included, so the stop's compute is the transaction's compute when the frame started.

SATIN-DET-026.text:
- `SATIN-DET-026` A system-originated transaction and a system call MUST NOT be detained, whatever they read ([Mega System Transactions and the Protocol's Own Transactions](../system-contracts/system-tx.md)).
  A deposit that is not system-originated is detained as any transaction.

SATIN-DET-027.text: - `SATIN-DET-027` Gas detention MUST price exactly the precompiles of the precompile set (`SATIN-PCMP-001`); a precompile a node adds or replaces is outside that set and outside this specification.

SATIN-FWD-001.text:
- `SATIN-FWD-001` `CALL`, `CALLCODE`, `DELEGATECALL`, `STATICCALL`, `CREATE` and `CREATE2` MUST cap the regular gas they forward at

  `forwarded_gas_cap = parent_remaining_gas − parent_remaining_gas × GAS_RETAINED_NUMERATOR / GAS_RETAINED_DENOMINATOR`

  - `parent_remaining_gas` — the caller's regular gas at the point of `SATIN-FWD-002`.
  - The division is integer division, truncating toward zero.

  This cap applies in place of EIP-150's 63/64 rule.

SATIN-FWD-002.text:
- `SATIN-FWD-002` `parent_remaining_gas` MUST be the caller's remaining regular gas after every charge the opcode makes before the forward ([History Gas and the History Allowance](history-gas.md) orders them).
  For a value-transferring `CALL` or `CALLCODE` those charges include the value-transfer cost of `VALUE_TRANSFER_COST`, which already contains the `CALL_STIPEND`, so the stipend is not taken from `parent_remaining_gas` again.

SATIN-FWD-003.text:
- `SATIN-FWD-003` The child's regular gas MUST be `min(requested_gas, forwarded_gas_cap)`, plus `CALL_STIPEND` for a value-transferring `CALL` or `CALLCODE` and for no other opcode.
  - `requested_gas` — the gas operand of the call.

  The stipend MUST be added to the child after the cap and MUST NOT be taken from the caller's remaining regular gas; `requested_gas` MUST NOT raise the forwarded portion above `forwarded_gas_cap`.
  A value-transferring `CALL` whose caller has 10,000 regular gas left after the value-transfer charge forwards a cap of 9,800: the child receives 12,100 and the caller keeps 200.
  The history allowance a value call grants ([History Gas and the History Allowance](history-gas.md)) is not part of the child's gas.

SATIN-FWD-004.text:
- `SATIN-FWD-004` `CREATE` and `CREATE2` have no gas operand: each MUST forward `forwarded_gas_cap` and MUST add no stipend.
  The regular-gas forward of a keyless deployment's creation is specified on [KeylessDeploy](../system-contracts/keyless-deploy.md).

SATIN-FWD-005.text:
- `SATIN-FWD-005` The reservoir MUST NOT be part of `forwarded_gas_cap` or of `requested_gas`.
  A child MUST receive the reservoir share of `SATIN-POOL-011` ([Two-Pool Gas](gas-model.md)), the transaction's own frame and a system call's outermost frame the whole reservoir (`SATIN-POOL-010`), whatever regular gas the start forwards: a call that forwards no regular gas still forwards the share.

SATIN-FWD-006.text:
- `SATIN-FWD-006` The reservoir share and the forward cap MUST be computed by the subtraction of `SATIN-FWD-001` and `SATIN-POOL-011`, which a node MUST NOT replace by the frame-budget multiplication `remaining × FRAME_DATA_SHARE_NUMERATOR / FRAME_DATA_SHARE_DENOMINATOR` of [Resource Limits](resource-limits.md); the two give different integers.
  The subtraction gives a child 98 of a remaining 99, and the whole remaining value whenever that value is below 50, so a remaining 1 gives the child 1 and the caller 0; the multiplication gives 97 of 99 and 0 of 1.

SATIN-FWD-007.text: - `SATIN-FWD-007` A system-originated transaction and a system call MUST apply the reservoir split of `SATIN-POOL-011` like any other execution: their exemption from the per-transaction limits ([Mega System Transactions and the Protocol's Own Transactions](../system-contracts/system-tx.md)) does not exempt them from it.

SATIN-HIST-001.section: Specification > The price and the byte table
SATIN-HIST-001.text: - `SATIN-HIST-001` History gas MUST be `COST_PER_HISTORY_BYTE` gas per byte of the byte table, and MUST NOT be scaled by SALT.

SATIN-HIST-002.section: Specification > The price and the byte table
SATIN-HIST-002.text:
- `SATIN-HIST-002` The bytes MUST be those of this table, which is also the table the data-size limit counts ([Resource Accounting](resource-accounting.md)), so an item's history bytes are its own data size:

  | Item                                      | Bytes                                                              |
  | ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
  | Transaction body                          | `TX_BODY_SIZE`                                                     |
  | Calldata (a creation's initcode included) | 1 per byte, zero or non-zero                                       |
  | Access-list address                       | `ACCESS_LIST_ADDRESS_SIZE`                                         |
  | Access-list storage key                   | `ACCESS_LIST_SLOT_SIZE`                                            |
  | EIP-7702 authorization                    | `AUTHORIZATION_SIZE`                                               |
  | Log                                       | `LOG_BASE_SIZE`, plus `LOG_TOPIC_SIZE` per topic, plus its data length |
  | Write record                              | `WRITE_RECORD_SIZE`                                                |
  | Deployed code                             | 1 per byte                                                         |

SATIN-HIST-003.section: Specification > The price and the byte table
SATIN-HIST-003.text:
- `SATIN-HIST-003` `TX_BODY_SIZE` MUST be `TX_BASE_SIZE` for the envelope plus `TX_FIXED_WRITE_RECORDS` write records of `WRITE_RECORD_SIZE` bytes: the sender's account, and the settlement writes of the four accounts a transaction's fees are credited to (the block beneficiary, the L1 fee vault, the base fee vault and the operator fee vault).
  It is an upper bound, charged whether or not every fee account is written.
  It covers every account write to the sender, and of the fee accounts only the fee credits; a storage write to the sender's slots, and a write execution makes to a fee account that is not the sender, are records of their own ([Resource Accounting](resource-accounting.md)).
  The five fixed records are bytes of the body alone: they MUST count as data size and pay history gas with the body, and MUST NOT count as KV updates, so a transaction that keeps no write of its own reports zero KV updates, and the body takes nothing of the transaction's KV-update limit ([Resource Accounting](resource-accounting.md)).

SATIN-HIST-004.section: Specification > When each charge is made
SATIN-HIST-004.text:
- `SATIN-HIST-004` The body — `TX_BODY_SIZE`, the calldata, the access list and the authorization entries — MUST be charged before execution as the intrinsic state gas ([Two-Pool Gas](gas-model.md)): the reservoir pays it first and the regular budget its excess.
  It MUST NOT be part of the intrinsic regular gas the execution cap is validated against, a gas limit that cannot cover it makes the transaction invalid ([Transaction Validation and Refusals](../block/transaction-validation.md)), and it MUST NOT be reported on the state ledger.

SATIN-HIST-005.section: Specification > When each charge is made
SATIN-HIST-005.text:
- `SATIN-HIST-005` The records of the applied EIP-7702 authorities, and the record the transaction's own frame makes at its start (its value's recipient or its created account), MUST be charged before the first frame.
  A list the KV or state-growth limit skips has no authority records, and that history is not charged ([EIP-7702 Authorizations Before the First Frame](authorizations.md)).
  The authorities' records are the transaction's own: their history MUST be kept when the first frame fails or is stopped.
  The first frame's record is that frame's: its history gas MUST come back, into the transaction's reservoir, when that frame reverts or is stopped; when that frame halts, the part the reservoir paid MUST return to the reservoir and the part regular gas paid MUST be consumed with the frame's regular gas.
  Of the two, the reservoir MUST pay the authorities' records first and the first frame's record with what they leave it, the regular budget paying the rest (`SATIN-POOL-024`): the part of the first frame's record the reservoir paid is the reservoir left after the authorities' records, up to the record's price.
  When the destruction table takes that record back inside a first frame that then succeeds, the charge has already come back with the table, and the settlement MUST NOT give it back a second time; when that first frame then fails, the table's give-back is discarded with the table, and the settlement MUST give the charge back once.
  A transaction that runs out of gas before its first frame keeps neither ([Gas Schedule and Intrinsic Gas](gas-schedule.md)).

SATIN-HIST-006.section: Specification > When each charge is made
SATIN-HIST-006.text:
- `SATIN-HIST-006` A log, a storage write's record, and the records of a `SELFDESTRUCT` (the account it clears and its beneficiary) MUST be charged by the opcode once it completed.
  A record the opcode takes back — a slot written back to its original value, an account a `SELFDESTRUCT` returns to what the transaction loaded, each part the destruction table takes back — MUST be given back by the opcode then, before what it makes is charged.

SATIN-HIST-007.section: Specification > When each charge is made
SATIN-HIST-007.text:
- `SATIN-HIST-007` A part the destruction table takes back is given back to the destroying frame (`SATIN-SD-005`, `SATIN-SD-007`, `SATIN-SD-010`, [SELFDESTRUCT and the Destruction Table](selfdestruct.md)).
  Every other give-back of history gas, and every give-back of state gas but the destruction table's, MUST go into the reservoir of the frame that makes it, at the price the record or the state was charged, by the rule of `SATIN-HIST-012`, whichever frame paid the charge: a slot written back to its original value, and an account a `SELFDESTRUCT` returns to what the transaction loaded, give back to the frame running the opcode; an account a value transfer returns to what the transaction loaded gives back to the caller of that start once the frame returned with its start kept (`SATIN-HIST-009`); a start's records and state gas that a failed or stopped child discards give back to its caller when the child returns (`SATIN-HIST-014`, `SATIN-POOL-015`).
  A failed frame's own charges, its records and logs among them, are given back by its rollback, which undoes with them the give-backs the frame received (`SATIN-POOL-014`, `SATIN-TAKE-004`).
  The frame that makes a give-back decides only whose reservoir holds it: a frame can pay state and history charges, while it runs, with gas an ancestor paid for records or state the frame takes back, at most the price of those records and that state, but it cannot compute with that gas (`SATIN-POOL-007`, `SATIN-POOL-009`); what it does not spend returns up the chain with its reservoir when it succeeds.

SATIN-HIST-008.section: Specification > When each charge is made
SATIN-HIST-008.text:
- `SATIN-HIST-008` An opcode that fails after its write was observed — an `SSTORE` or a `SELFDESTRUCT` that cannot pay a regular charge it makes after its load — MUST keep nothing and MUST be charged no history.
  A `LOG` observes its write after every regular charge of the inherited opcode, so only the limits and its history charge can fail it after its write was observed.

SATIN-HIST-009.section: Specification > When each charge is made
SATIN-HIST-009.text:
- `SATIN-HIST-009` A `CALL`, `CALLCODE`, `CREATE` or `CREATE2` MUST charge its own frame for the records the frame it starts makes — the accounts a value transfer changes from what the transaction loaded; a creation's created account, unless the transaction changed it already, and the creator's nonce record when the bump changes the creator's account from what the transaction loaded ([Resource Accounting](resource-accounting.md)) — after the regular gas it forwards is computed, so the forward is not reduced by them.
  A caller that cannot pay MUST halt out of gas: the frame MUST NOT start, and none of the start's decisions is made (`SATIN-HIST-023`).
  The price of a record the start takes back — an account the transfer returns to what the transaction loaded — MUST be given back to the caller once the frame returned with its start kept.

SATIN-HIST-010.section: Specification > When each charge is made

SATIN-HIST-011.section: Specification > When each charge is made
SATIN-HIST-011.text: - `SATIN-HIST-011` A `CREATE` or `CREATE2` MUST charge the created account's state gas, its legacy share included (`SATIN-STATE-012`), when the account at the created address is empty under EIP-161 (no account, or nonce zero, zero balance and no code), before it computes the forward, and MUST give the creation its reservoir share after the history of the start's records, as a call does.

SATIN-HIST-012.text:
- `SATIN-HIST-012` Every give-back of state gas or of history gas — a refill (a slot written back, an account returned to what the transaction loaded, a record taken back), the destruction table's, a start's charge given back when the start fails or is refused, a failed frame's rollback — MUST credit the reservoir of the frame that receives it (`SATIN-HIST-007`, `SATIN-SD-005`, `SATIN-POOL-015`, `SATIN-POOL-014`) and MUST NOT credit its regular gas, whichever pool paid the charge, a legacy share included.
  A frame's regular gas MUST NOT rise within the frame except by the unused regular gas a child returns (`SATIN-POOL-012`); a give-back of a charge regular gas paid leaves that gas spent and puts its price into the reservoir, where it can pay later state and history charges, and what is left of it returns to the sender at the settlement (`SATIN-POOL-017`).
  An exceptional halt consumes the halting frame's regular gas, with the part of its charges that regular gas paid, and restores its reservoir to what it received (`SATIN-POOL-014`).
  A give-back of state or history gas MUST NOT be an EIP-3529 refund: it is credited at once, is not capped, and does not change the refund counter.

SATIN-HIST-013.section: Specification > When each charge is made
SATIN-HIST-013.text:
- `SATIN-HIST-013` A record an opcode commits — a storage write, a log, a `SELFDESTRUCT`'s records — MUST be held to the limits ([Resource Limits](resource-limits.md)) before its history is charged, so a record a limit refuses is not charged.
  A frame that cannot pay that history charge MUST halt out of gas, keeping neither the record nor its bytes.

SATIN-HIST-014.section: Specification > When each charge is made
SATIN-HIST-014.text: - `SATIN-HIST-014` At a frame start the order is the reverse of an opcode's: the calling opcode MUST pay for the start's records before the frame starts, and they are then held to the limits, so a caller that cannot pay runs out of gas first; the charge for a start a limit stops MUST be given back when the stopped frame returns.

SATIN-HIST-015.section: Specification > When each charge is made
SATIN-HIST-015.text:
- `SATIN-HIST-015` The opcode MUST charge the records a start makes as the state stands when it runs: a value the caller cannot fund makes no record and is charged no history; a creation its opcode refuses (`SATIN-HIST-023`) starts no frame and is charged no history and no state gas, the creation opcode refusing it before it charges for the start and before it reads the created address.
  The opcode reads the state and no decision that follows its charges: what a value call its caller can fund is charged, and given back when its start does not happen, is `SATIN-HIST-023`'s.
  The new account's state gas of a value `CALL` to an account empty under EIP-161 does not wait for the funds check either: it is charged at step 2 of `SATIN-HIST-010`, and given back when the start is refused (`SATIN-POOL-015`).

SATIN-HIST-017.text:
- `SATIN-HIST-017` The EIP-7623 floor MUST still be computed and validated for every transaction ([Gas Schedule and Intrinsic Gas](gas-schedule.md)).
  It can raise the gas used of a transaction whose history gas is small, and it bounds the figure a block counts on its execution ledger, `max(regular, floor)` (`SATIN-POOL-020`).
  Where it binds, the gas used is the floor, drawn from the whole gas limit, the reservoir included (`SATIN-POOL-018`); a deposit, which paid nothing, MUST be charged nothing either way, and only its receipt's and the block's figures move.

SATIN-HIST-018.text:
- `SATIN-HIST-018` A value-transferring `CALL` or `CALLCODE` below the transaction's own frame MUST grant the frame it starts a history allowance of `HISTORY_ALLOWANCE_BYTES × COST_PER_HISTORY_BYTE` gas.
  No other start grants one: not the transaction's own frame, a `DELEGATECALL`, a `STATICCALL`, a creation, or a call without value.

SATIN-HIST-019.text:
- `SATIN-HIST-019` A log's history charge in that frame MUST draw `min(history_charge, allowance_left)` from the allowance first, and the frame's gas MUST pay the rest; the allowance MUST be reduced by what it paid.
  - `history_charge` — the log's history gas (`SATIN-HIST-002`).
  - `allowance_left` — what the frame's allowance has left before the log.

  Only a log's history charge draws on the allowance: a write record's history charge MUST NOT draw on it.
  A value call whose child has only the stipend and no reservoir, and whose child emits an empty `LOG0` (2,816 gas of history), therefore pays that log from the allowance and succeeds.

SATIN-HIST-020.text:
- `SATIN-HIST-020` The allowance MUST NOT enter the frame's gas: it MUST NOT pay for computation or state, it is never returned as gas, and what it pays for is on no gas ledger.
  The history bytes it pays for still count as bytes the transaction appended, and as data size.

SATIN-HIST-021.text: - `SATIN-HIST-021` The transfer log of the value that granted the allowance MUST NOT draw on it ([EIP-7708 Transfer Logs](transfer-logs.md)).

SATIN-HIST-022.section: Specification > The history bytes a transaction reports
SATIN-HIST-022.text:
- `SATIN-HIST-022` The history bytes a transaction reports, which the block counts ([Block Limits and Packing](../block/block-limits.md)), MUST be the bytes of the byte table (`SATIN-HIST-002`) the transaction keeps — its body, its kept write records, its kept logs and its deposited code — whether history gas or a history allowance paid them, net of every take-back.
  A system call, exempt from history gas by `SATIN-HIST-016`, MUST report zero history bytes; a deposit and a system-originated transaction report theirs as any transaction does.
  EIP-7708 transfer logs and Oracle hint payloads are not history bytes.
  A deposit with empty calldata that makes no write reports 310 bytes of data size and 310 history bytes, its body; an ordinary transaction whose value call's child emits a `LOG0` the allowance pays reports that log's 32 bytes among its history bytes.

SATIN-HIST-023.section: Specification > When each charge is made
SATIN-HIST-023.text:
- `SATIN-HIST-023` The order around a frame start follows one principle, which the rules it cites apply case by case: the opcode charges first, the start is decided next, and a start that does not happen gives back what was charged for it.
  A `CALL`, `CALLCODE`, `DELEGATECALL`, `STATICCALL`, `CREATE` or `CREATE2` MUST make every charge of its own in the opcode, before any decision about the start: its regular charges, a new or created account's state gas, the forward, and the history of the records its start would make as the state stands (`SATIN-HIST-009`, `SATIN-HIST-010`, `SATIN-HIST-011`, `SATIN-HIST-015`).
  Only then MUST the start be decided: a call by the depth gate, then by interception, then by the frame start with its funds check, in the order of `SATIN-ICPT-007` ([Call Interception](../system-contracts/interception.md)); a creation by its frame start, the creation opcode having refused, before it charged anything for the start, a creation whose creator's nonce cannot be bumped, whose endowment the creator cannot fund, or which is past the call-depth limit (`SATIN-HIST-015`).
  No charge is skipped for a decision that would follow it: a frame that cannot pay one of these charges MUST halt out of gas at it, or be stopped at it when it is gas detention's crossing (`SATIN-DET-018`), and none of the decisions is then made: no interceptor answers, no hint is admitted or forwarded, and no frame starts.
  A value call its caller can fund whose start does not happen (a call an interceptor answers, a `sendHint` its data-size check stops, a call refused past the call-depth limit) MUST be given back the history the opcode charged for its records, into the caller's reservoir when the call returns (`SATIN-HIST-012`), as a start that a failed or stopped child discards is (`SATIN-HIST-014`).
  A call or a creation past the call-depth limit is reached by no execution under the current rules and constants: every calling or creating opcode forwards at most 98/100 of its frame's regular gas, so of the `EXECUTION_CAP` that bounds a transaction's regular gas less than one unit is left at depth 1,024 ([Gas Forwarding](gas-forwarding.md)); the case is stated here so that it has an answer if they change.
  The principle keeps `SATIN-HIST-015`: a value its caller cannot fund makes no record as the state stands, so the opcode charges no history for it and nothing is given back, whether the call is then answered, stopped or refused at its frame start; a new account's state gas charged before a refusal is given back by `SATIN-POOL-015`.
  The opcode's regular charges MUST stay spent, and every start that does not happen, a call refused for a value its caller cannot fund included, MUST return the child's whole regular gas, a value call's `CALL_STIPEND` included, less only what an interceptor's answer itself charges, together with the child's reservoir share (`SATIN-FWD-003`, `SATIN-POOL-012`, `SATIN-ICPT-004`).
  The transaction's own frame follows the same principle, the charges made before the first frame standing in the opcode's place (`SATIN-SCHED-008`, `SATIN-HIST-005`).

SATIN-HPTS-001.text:
- `SATIN-HPTS-001` The High-Precision Timestamp MUST be the account at `HIGH_PRECISION_TIMESTAMP_ADDRESS` holding the code `HIGH_PRECISION_TIMESTAMP_CODE_HASH` (see [System Contracts](overview.md)); it has no interceptor, and its interface, storage allocation and service are the following.
  - **Interface.**
    `timestamp() returns (uint256)` returns the value at Oracle slot `TIMESTAMP_BASE_SLOT`, read through the Oracle's `getSlot`, as a number of microseconds since the Unix epoch.
    `update(uint256 ts)` forwards to the Oracle's `setSlot`, which authorizes its immediate caller — the timestamp contract itself — and so commits only when the live system address is `HIGH_PRECISION_TIMESTAMP_ADDRESS`, and otherwise reverts.
    `ORACLE_CONTRACT_ADDRESS()` returns `ORACLE_CONTRACT_ADDRESS`, `ALLOCATION_START()` returns `TIMESTAMP_BASE_SLOT`, and `ALLOCATION_SIZE()` returns `TIMESTAMP_MAX_SLOTS` as a `uint32`.
  - **Storage allocation.** Of the Oracle's storage, slot `TIMESTAMP_BASE_SLOT` holds the current timestamp in microseconds, and the following slots up to `TIMESTAMP_BASE_SLOT + TIMESTAMP_MAX_SLOTS − 1` are reserved.
  - **Service.** For a transaction that reads the timestamp, the value the timestamp service gives is a per-transaction snapshot, and it MUST be:
    - expressed in microseconds;
    - at most `block.timestamp × MICROSECONDS_PER_SECOND`;
    - above `parent.timestamp × MICROSECONDS_PER_SECOND`, the parent block's timestamp in microseconds, when the block's timestamp is above its parent's, and `block.timestamp × MICROSECONDS_PER_SECOND` when the two timestamps are equal;
    - the same for every read the transaction makes;
    - at least the snapshot any earlier transaction was given, of the same block or of an earlier one.

    The snapshot MUST be persisted before the transaction that read it unless that transaction's own write explains it (see [Oracle](oracle.md), `SATIN-ORCL-012`), and the protocol MUST NOT require a timestamp write for a transaction that does not read the timestamp.
    A read made where the service is not asked (`SATIN-ORCL-005`) pushes the slot's value.

SATIN-HPTS-002.text: - `SATIN-HPTS-002` The wrapper's reads of the Oracle's storage are Oracle reads: an `SLOAD` in the Oracle's own frame, reached through `getSlot`, MUST be answered by the oracle service, charged as a cold access and held to gas detention as [Oracle](oracle.md) and [Gas Detention](../evm/gas-detention.md) specify, and a frame whose volatile-data access is off MUST be refused it (see [MegaAccessControl](mega-access-control.md)).

SATIN-ICPT-001.text:
- `SATIN-ICPT-001` A node MUST answer a call itself, before a frame is built for it, when and only when the call is a `CALL` or a `STATICCALL`, its target is a system contract that has an interceptor, and the first four bytes of its input are the selector of one of that contract's intercepted methods.
  The intercepted methods are those the table below lists; the matching is on the address, then on the four-byte selector alone, whatever bytes follow it, and an input shorter than four bytes names no selector.
  A `DELEGATECALL` or `CALLCODE` of any of these contracts, a call to a selector the contract does not intercept, and a call to a system contract that has no interceptor MUST run the contract's bytecode.
  A transaction whose recipient is a system contract is a `CALL` at depth 0 and MUST be intercepted all the same, though no opcode initiated it.
  A `CREATE` or `CREATE2` is never intercepted.

| Contract                                     | Intercepted methods                                                                          | Answer                                                                 |
| -------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [Oracle](oracle.md)                          | `sendHint(bytes32,bytes)`                                                                    | Forwards the hint, then the call runs the bytecode (see the page)      |
| [MegaAccessControl](mega-access-control.md)  | `disableVolatileDataAccess()`, `enableVolatileDataAccess()`, `isVolatileDataAccessDisabled()` | The node's answer; the bytecode does not run                           |
| [MegaLimitControl](mega-limit-control.md)    | `remainingComputeGas()`                                                                      | The node's answer; the bytecode does not run                           |

SATIN-ICPT-002.text:
- `SATIN-ICPT-002` A call whose frame would be deeper than `CALL_STACK_LIMIT` MUST NOT reach any interceptor, nor the `keylessDeploy` recognition.
  It MUST be answered as any call past the call-stack limit is, with the depth failure, which returns and gives back to the caller what `SATIN-HIST-023` states for a start that does not happen; no interceptor effect is made and no hint forwarded or counted.
  The depth gate comes before every other decision about the call, a limit included: a call past the depth limit counts no start toward any limit and cannot be stopped by one.

SATIN-ICPT-003.text:
- `SATIN-ICPT-003` An intercepted method of MegaAccessControl or MegaLimitControl called with a non-zero value MUST be answered with a revert whose data is `NonZeroTransfer()`, before any value moves and before the funds check (`SATIN-ICPT-007`); the method's own answer is not made.
  The policy applies once the selector matched: a call carrying value to a selector the contract does not intercept runs the bytecode.
