  A `sendHint` carrying value is not answered by this policy: it is admitted as any hint is (`SATIN-ORCL-006`).

SATIN-ICPT-004.text:
- `SATIN-ICPT-004` An interceptor's answer MUST return to the caller as the result of a frame that ran on the child's regular gas, the forward plus a value call's `CALL_STIPEND` (`SATIN-FWD-003`): the call opcode's regular charges, made before the call reached the interceptor, stay charged; the history the opcode charged for the records of a value call its caller can fund is given back into the caller's reservoir, since an answer moves no value (`SATIN-HIST-023`); the answer itself charges nothing unless its contract's page says otherwise; the child's regular gas returns to the caller untouched, the stipend included, and the reservoir share the caller gave the call returns to it by the child-merge rule of [Two-Pool Gas](../evm/gas-model.md) (`SATIN-POOL-012`).
  A successful answer's output is the method's ABI-encoded return value; a refusal's is the error's ABI encoding, returned with a revert.
  An answer writes no account, no storage and no log, and moves no value.

SATIN-ICPT-005.text: - `SATIN-ICPT-005` Under [gas detention](../evm/gas-detention.md), an answer whose regular spend exceeds the calling frame's allowance — state and history gas that regular gas paid not counted — MUST be the crossing: the answer's whole regular spend is treated as the one charge that crossed, none of it billed, the part within the allowance included, and the call is stopped as [Limit Stops](../evm/limit-stops.md) specifies, with the effect the answer would have made not made.

SATIN-ICPT-007.section: Specification > The order of a call's decisions
SATIN-ICPT-007.text:
- `SATIN-ICPT-007` Once the call opcode has made every charge of its own (its regular charges, a new account's state gas, the forward, and the history of the records its start would make as the state stands, steps 1 to 4 of `SATIN-HIST-010`), as the principle of `SATIN-HIST-023` orders it, a `CALL` or `STATICCALL` MUST be decided in this order: first the depth gate (`SATIN-ICPT-002`); then interception, which is every interceptor's answer, its value policy included (`SATIN-ICPT-003`), the admission of a `sendHint` and the data-size check of its input ([Oracle](oracle.md)), and the `keylessDeploy` recognition (`SATIN-ICPT-006`) with steps 1 and 2 of the deployment ([KeylessDeploy](keyless-deploy.md)); and only then the frame start, where the caller's funds are checked and the value moves ([Resource Limits](../evm/resource-limits.md), `SATIN-LIM-013`, `SATIN-LIM-015`).
  Interception therefore comes before the funds check, and whether the caller can fund the call's value changes nothing interception does: not the admission of a `sendHint` or the data-size stop of its input (`SATIN-ORCL-006`, `SATIN-ORCL-010`), not the value policy's `NonZeroTransfer()` (`SATIN-ICPT-003`), and not steps 1 and 2 of a recognized `keylessDeploy` call (`SATIN-KEY-018`).

  The charges come before all three decisions, so a caller that cannot pay one of them halts out of gas before the depth gate: no answer is made and no hint is admitted.
  A value call its caller can fund that interception answers or stops was charged the history of the records its transfer would make, and MUST be given it back into the caller's reservoir when the answer returns (`SATIN-HIST-023`); a value its caller cannot fund makes no record, so nothing was charged for it and nothing is given back (`SATIN-HIST-015`).
  A transaction's own frame that its authorization list stops before it runs (`SATIN-AUTH-010`) is stopped before any of these, and reaches no interceptor.

SATIN-KEY-002.text: - `SATIN-KEY-002` A `keylessDeploy(bytes,uint256)` call recognized as the transaction's own frame (see [Call Interception](interception.md), `SATIN-ICPT-006`) MUST deploy the creation its first argument carries as an ordinary creation frame, a child of the call, by the steps below; no code runs in the call's own frame.

SATIN-KEY-003.text: - `SATIN-KEY-003` A `keylessDeploy` call that a contract makes MUST run KeylessDeploy's bytecode: without value it reverts with `NotIntercepted()`, and with value it reverts with empty data, the method not being payable.

SATIN-KEY-004.text:
- `SATIN-KEY-004` A deployment MUST make the charges and checks of the table below.
  A step's refusal MUST revert the call with the error the table names: the state and history gas the call was charged MUST be given back into the call's reservoir (`SATIN-HIST-012`), and the regular gas it spent stays spent.
  A step that cannot pay its charge MUST halt the call out of gas, consuming the call's regular gas.

SATIN-KEY-005.text:
- `SATIN-KEY-005` The steps, in this order:

| Step | Check or charge | Refusal |
| ---- | --------------- | ------- |
| step-1 | Charge `KEYLESS_DEPLOY_OVERHEAD_GAS` of regular gas | Out of gas |
| step-2 | The call carries no value | `NoEtherTransfer()`, answered before the call's frame is built (see `SATIN-KEY-018`): no value moves |
| step-3 | The first argument — the `bytes` the call's arguments held when it was recognized, the length bytes after the length word that `SATIN-ICPT-006`'s offset points at, unpadded — decodes as a signed legacy transaction that is a creation (`to` empty), carries no chain id, and is followed by no trailing byte | In this order: `MalformedEncoding()` for an RLP encoding that does not decode or has trailing bytes, then `NotContractCreation()` for a transaction with `to` set, then `NotPreEIP155()` for one with a chain id |
| step-4 | The carried transaction's nonce is 0 | `NonZeroTxNonce(uint64)` |
| step-5 | The initcode is at most `MAX_INITCODE_SIZE` bytes | `InitCodeTooLarge(uint64,uint64)` |
| step-6 | `gasLimitOverride` (read as `MAX_UINT64` when larger) is at least the signed gas limit | `GasLimitTooLow(uint64,uint64)` |
| step-7 | The signer can be recovered from the signature, whether its `s` value is low or high: EIP-2's bound on `s` does not apply | `InvalidSignature()` |
| step-8 | The signer's nonce is at most 1 | `SignerNonceTooHigh(uint64)` |
| step-9 | Unless the node's configuration disables EIP-3607, the signer's code is empty or an EIP-7702 delegation indicator; with EIP-3607 disabled the step checks nothing | `SignerHasCode()` |
| step-10 | If the signer's account is empty (EIP-161), charge the state gas of a new account at the signer's bucket, with its legacy share | Out of gas |
| step-11 | `min(gasLimitOverride, available gas)` is at least the signed gas limit | `GasLimitTooLow(uint64,uint64)` |
| step-12 | The deploy address `keccak256(rlp([signer, 0]))[12:]` holds no code | `ContractAlreadyExists()` |
| step-13 | The signer's balance is at least the carried value | `InsufficientBalance()` |
| step-14 | Charge what a `CREATE` charges its frame for the start: `CREATE_GAS` plus EIP-3860's initcode cost of regular gas; the state gas of the created account at the deploy address's bucket if the deploy address is empty, with its legacy share; the history gas of the created account's write record, unless the transaction changed the deploy address's account already; and the history gas of the signer's nonce record, unless the transaction changed the signer's account already, the transaction's sender among such accounts | Out of gas |
| step-15 | `min(gasLimitOverride, available gas)` is still at least the signed gas limit | `GasLimitTooLow(uint64,uint64)` |

  "Available gas" is the call's regular gas a `CREATE` could forward, its withheld part included (see [Gas Detention](../evm/gas-detention.md)).
  The state charges of steps 10 and 14 are made as every state charge is, their legacy shares first from regular gas — 25,000 for the signer's new account and 20,000 for the created account at the current prices (`SATIN-STATE-012`) — then the reservoir, then the rest from regular gas (see [Two-Pool Gas](../evm/gas-model.md)), priced as [State Gas and SALT Pricing](../evm/state-gas.md) specifies; the history charge of step 14 is priced as [History Gas](../evm/history-gas.md) specifies.

SATIN-KEY-006.text: - `SATIN-KEY-006` A call that more than one of steps 3 to 13 would refuse MUST be refused with the error of the first of them in the table's order, and a call that step 3 refuses for more than one reason with the first error in step 3's own order: a carried transaction with `to` set and a chain id is refused with `NotContractCreation()`.

SATIN-KEY-007.text:
- `SATIN-KEY-007` The read of the signer's account that steps 8 to 10 and 13 check MUST load the account into the transaction's state as an account access loads it, warm: with its code, unless the node's configuration disables EIP-3607, in which case without it, so that a deployment with EIP-3607 disabled loads no signer code and makes no signer-code refusal.
  The read of step 12 MUST load the deploy address's account warm, without its code.
  Neither read is charged, and no charge the call or its creation makes depends on either account's warmth: the creation loads both accounts again when it starts, as a creation loads its creator and the address it creates.

SATIN-KEY-008.text:
- `SATIN-KEY-008` Step 12 MUST check the deploy address's code alone.
  An address that holds a nonce other than zero but no code passes it, and the creation then collides there, as any creation onto an address with a nonce does (`SATIN-SD-016`), and fails; the call answers `ExecutionHalted` with the creation's whole forward spent, and the signer's nonce is kept or taken back as `SATIN-KEY-013` says.
  An address that holds only a balance — nonce zero and no code — passes it and is not a collision: the creation lands there and keeps that balance; the address is not empty under EIP-161 (`SATIN-STATE-011`), so step 14 charges no created-account state gas for it and the creation counts no rise for it.

SATIN-KEY-009.text:
- `SATIN-KEY-009` A creation at the deploy address whose constructor returns empty code MUST be refused its empty code deposit and MUST revert, its state, logs and records taken back as for a creation that reverted, so that the address stays deployable; the call answers `EmptyCodeDeployed`.
  A constructor that destroyed the account it was creating leaves no code either, and the call answers `EmptyCodeDeployed` for it too.
  The rule concerns the deploy address alone: a creation the constructor itself makes may return empty code.

SATIN-KEY-010.text: - `SATIN-KEY-010` A signer that is the block beneficiary MUST be detained as a read of the beneficiary's account, made when the signer's account is read, after step 7 recovered the signer and before step 8's check; the read's compute is the call's `KEYLESS_DEPLOY_OVERHEAD_GAS` of step 1, so the limit it sets is that plus the cap, unless an earlier read set a lower limit (see [Gas Detention](../evm/gas-detention.md)).

SATIN-KEY-011.text:
- `SATIN-KEY-011` Once step 15 passed, the creation MUST start as a creation by the signer at the deploy address, one call level below the call, carrying the signed initcode and value, forwarding `min(gasLimitOverride, available gas)` of regular gas, drawn from the call's withheld gas first.
  The 98/100 forwarding cap of [Gas Forwarding](../evm/gas-forwarding.md) MUST NOT apply to that forward.
  The creation MUST receive the reservoir share of [Gas Forwarding](../evm/gas-forwarding.md) of the reservoir the call has left after step 14, the call keeping the rest, and, in data size, KV updates and state growth, the child share of the frame budgets the call has left (see [Resource Limits](../evm/resource-limits.md)).
  From its start it is an ordinary creation frame: priced, limited, detained and logged as any creation is, and its start bumps the signer's nonce as a creation bumps its creator's.
  `ORIGIN` and `GASPRICE` in the initcode MUST be the transaction's own.

SATIN-KEY-012.text: - `SATIN-KEY-012` The signer's nonce record, and the signer's unit of state growth when the creation's nonce bump creates the signer's account, MUST be counted on the call when the creation has returned, once the nonce rule below has been applied.

SATIN-KEY-013.text:
- `SATIN-KEY-013` The signer's nonce:
  - a deployment from signer nonce 0 MUST keep the creation's bump;
  - a deployment from signer nonce 1 MUST take the bump back, setting the nonce to 1, when the creation's bump is the last change of the signer's nonce the deployment made, whether the deployment succeeded or failed;
  - a signer whose own code spent a nonce during the creation, a change that survives the creation, MUST keep every bump.

  The signer's write record MUST be counted after that rule: when the nonce set back leaves the signer's account as the transaction loaded it, no record stands, and the history gas step 14 charged for it MUST be given back into the call's reservoir; a signer's account another write changed — value a creation that returned without a revert or a halt moved out of it, or into it — keeps its record.
  When the signer's nonce stands where it was and step 10 charged state gas for the signer's account, that state gas MUST be given back into the call's reservoir.
  That last case is reached by no execution under the current rules and constants: step 10 charges only a signer empty under EIP-161, whose nonce is zero, and once steps 11 to 15 have passed the creation always bumps that nonce, which a deployment from nonce zero keeps.

SATIN-KEY-015.text:
- `SATIN-KEY-015` `gasUsed` MUST be what the creation spent from both pools taken together, without intrinsic gas and before the EIP-3529 refund: the regular gas and the reservoir the creation was given, less the regular gas and the reservoir it returned — its regular charges plus the state and history gas it kept, net of every give-back within the creation of a charge the creation made — a slot written back to its original value, a record taken back, the upfront state gas of a frame it started that failed, and the state and history gas a same-transaction destruction gives back, the deployed code's history gas included.
  The call's own charges of steps 1 and 14 are not part of it, and a give-back is not an EIP-3529 refund.
  A give-back the creation receives for a charge it did not make MUST NOT lower `gasUsed`, and MUST be added back to what the creation returned: the one such give-back is the destruction table's for the account being created, when a destruction of it — the constructor's `SELFDESTRUCT`, or one a frame the constructor calls makes in its context — stands when the creation ends, and step 14's state gas of the created account and history gas of its write record come back within the creation (`SATIN-SD-005`, `SATIN-SD-007`).
  So `gasUsed` is `(regular given − regular returned) + (reservoir given − reservoir returned) + the give-backs of step 14's charges the creation received`.
  The two pools MUST be netted together, not each clipped at zero: a creation that pays state from regular gas and reverts returns that state as reservoir, which lowers `gasUsed` by it; a creation whose constructor writes a fresh slot at `m = 1` from regular gas alone and reverts reports 12,109 for its regular charges, not 113,549.
  A constructor `ORIGIN; SELFDESTRUCT` (`0x32ff`) at `m = 1`, given 500,000 of regular gas and no reservoir, with a zero balance and the warm sender as beneficiary, spends 2 + 5,000 and receives step 14's 183,600 of state gas and 3,520 of history gas back into its reservoir; it returns 494,998 of regular gas and 187,120 of reservoir, and `gasUsed` is 5,002 + (0 − 187,120) + 187,120 = 5,002, not −182,118; the call answers `EmptyCodeDeployed(5002)` (`SATIN-KEY-009`).
  `gasUsed` is never less than the creation's regular charges, the regular gas it spent on anything but state and history: every give-back left in it is of a charge the creation made.

SATIN-KEY-016.text:
- `SATIN-KEY-016` A limit the creation crosses — its frame budget in data size, KV updates or state growth, the transaction's limit in one of those dimensions, or gas detention's compute limit, at the creation's start or in its initcode — MUST stop the creation (see [Limit Stops](../evm/limit-stops.md)); the call then answers `ExecutionReverted` with the stop's revert data as `output`.
  The creation keeps only what an ordinary failed creation keeps on its creator's side, under the nonce rule above: the deploy address's account, the value moved, the transfer log and the deploy address's write record are taken back.
  A limit the call's own charges cross — gas detention's compute limit, for one — MUST stop the call: it reverts with the stop, and the deployment, the signer's nonce included, is taken back.
  The signer's nonce record counted on the call at its settlement can cross the call's frame budget in data size and KV updates, its state-growth budget when the bump created the signer, and the transaction's data-size limit once Oracle hints the creation sent used what the transaction had left; when it does, the call MUST revert with that stop, and the deployment, the nonce included, is taken back.
  The call is the transaction's own frame, so a stop of the call is the transaction's result.

SATIN-KEY-017.text:
- `SATIN-KEY-017` The node MUST NOT produce the errors `ParentBudgetExceeded(uint8,uint64,uint64)`, `InvalidTransaction()`, `InsufficientComputeGas(uint64,uint64)` or `InternalError()`, which the interface no longer declares: a read the node fails to make is a fault (`SATIN-VAL-010`, see [Transaction Validation and Refusals](../block/transaction-validation.md)).
  `AddressMismatch()` and `NoContractCreated()` remain the answers to a creation reported at another address or at none, a case reached by no execution under the current rules and constants.

SATIN-KEY-018.text:
- `SATIN-KEY-018` A call that carries value MUST first be held to gas detention for step 1's charge: when that charge is the crossing, the call is stopped with `MegaLimitExceeded(2, limit)` and none of it is billed; otherwise the charge is made (or halts the call out of gas) and the call reverts with `NoEtherTransfer()` before any value moves and before any frame is built.
  Steps 1 and 2 are part of interception, which comes before the frame start where the funds are checked (`SATIN-ICPT-007`).

SATIN-LIM-001.text:
- `SATIN-LIM-001` A node MUST limit every transaction in three dimensions, each with a transaction limit and a frame budget:

  | Dimension    | Counted in                                                     | Kind | Transaction limit       | Frame budget |
  | ------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ---- | ----------------------- | ------------ |
  | Data size    | Bytes of the data-size items ([Resource Accounting](resource-accounting.md)) | 0    | `TX_DATA_LIMIT`         | Yes          |
  | KV updates   | [Write records](../../glossary.md#write-record)                | 1    | `TX_KV_UPDATE_LIMIT`    | Yes          |
  | State growth | New accounts and new storage slots                             | 3    | `TX_STATE_GROWTH_LIMIT` | Yes          |

  The kind is the discriminant a stop in that dimension carries ([Limit Stops](limit-stops.md)).
  Compute is not a fourth limit: it is regular gas, bounded by the execution cap ([Two-Pool Gas](gas-model.md)) and by [gas detention](gas-detention.md), whose stops carry kind 2.
  A system-originated transaction and a system call are not held to these limits, and still have their usage counted ([Mega System Transactions and the Protocol's Own Transactions](../system-contracts/system-tx.md)).

SATIN-LIM-002.text:
- `SATIN-LIM-002` The transaction's own frame MUST receive, in each dimension, what the transaction has left once the body and the counts made before the first frame are counted (`SATIN-LIM-005`).
  A creation transaction's own frame is that frame, not a child: it receives the whole of what the transaction has left.

SATIN-LIM-003.text:
- `SATIN-LIM-003` Every child frame MUST receive, in each dimension,

  `budget = parent_remaining × FRAME_DATA_SHARE_NUMERATOR / FRAME_DATA_SHARE_DENOMINATOR`

  - `parent_remaining` — what the parent has left in that dimension (`SATIN-LIM-004`); the three dimensions share one definition of it.
  - The division rounds down.

  A `CREATE` or `CREATE2` MUST take that share of what the creator has left at the opcode, before the creator's nonce record of `SATIN-LIM-008` is counted.
  A creator that has 1,000 of state growth left, and whose nonce bump adds none, gives the creation a state-growth budget of 980.

SATIN-LIM-004.text:
- `SATIN-LIM-004` A frame's net in a dimension MUST be signed: what it added, minus what it gave back, plus the nets its successful children merged in.
  A fall of state growth, a write record taken back, or data size given back can make the net negative.
  The frame's remaining MUST be `min(budget, max(0, budget − net))`: it stays inside the budget the frame was given when the net is negative, so a negative net never raises what the frame passes to a child.
  A frame with a state-growth budget of 1,000 that has added 100 has 900 left, and the child it starts receives 882; if that child removes those 100, its net is −100 and its remaining stays 882, so the frame it starts receives 864.
  The remaining is the base a child's share is taken from (`SATIN-LIM-003`), not the room a rise of the frame's own is held to: a rise of the frame's own MUST cross the frame budget only when it takes the frame's signed net past the budget, `net + rise > budget` (`SATIN-ACCT-019`), so a frame whose net is negative can keep a rise larger than its remaining.
  A child with a data-size budget of 1,000 bytes whose net is −400, because it took back ten write records its caller made, keeps a log of 1,200 bytes, its net becoming 800, although its remaining is 1,000.

SATIN-LIM-005.text:
- `SATIN-LIM-005` The transaction's net in a dimension MUST be what is counted on no frame — the body, the applied authorities' records ([EIP-7702 Authorizations Before the First Frame](authorizations.md)), the caller account a deposit creates ([Deposit Transactions](../block/deposits.md)), and every admitted Oracle hint ([Oracle](../system-contracts/oracle.md)) — plus the net of every frame on the stack, a frame's net including a child's only once that child succeeded and merged.
  The transaction's remaining MUST be `min(limit, max(0, limit − net))`, with `limit` the transaction limit of the dimension; it is the base the transaction's own frame is given, and a rise crosses the transaction limit only when it takes the transaction's signed net past `limit` (`SATIN-ACCT-019`).

SATIN-LIM-006.text:
- `SATIN-LIM-006` When a frame succeeds, its signed net MUST merge into its caller's net, and the caller's remaining MUST be computed again from the caller's own budget; the merge can raise the caller's remaining up to that budget.
  After the child of `SATIN-LIM-004` succeeds, its caller's net is 0 and its remaining is again 1,000, so a later child receives 980.
  When a frame fails, its net MUST be discarded and its caller's net is unchanged; the credits inside the failed frame are discarded with it, the state-gas refill, the write-record takeback and the code's data size and history gas of a same-transaction destruction included ([SELFDESTRUCT and the Destruction Table](selfdestruct.md)).
  A fall with no earlier rise leaves the frame's remaining at its budget; later rises may consume that fall, and the kept net still cannot pass the budget.

SATIN-LIM-007.text: - `SATIN-LIM-007` The KV-update and state-growth counts a transaction reports MUST each be `max(net, 0)` of the transaction's net in that dimension at its end.

SATIN-LIM-008.text:
- `SATIN-LIM-008` A creator's nonce record, and the creator's state growth when the bump creates the creator's account (as a keyless signer's bump can), MUST be counted on the creator once the creation returned with the nonce bumped, MUST be held to the creator's budget and not the creation's, and MUST survive the creation's failure.
  The created account's write record and its state growth are the creation's own, held to the creation's budget.

SATIN-LIM-009.text: - `SATIN-LIM-009` A node MUST NOT hold a frame to any per-frame cap other than its frame budgets in these three dimensions and the regular gas it was forwarded.

SATIN-LIM-010.text:
- `SATIN-LIM-010` At a completed write or a decided frame start, an operation that crosses more than one of data size (kind 0), KV updates (kind 1) and state growth (kind 3) MUST stop on the first of those three, in that order.
  Compute (kind 2) MUST be decided at the regular charge, before the write is counted: a regular charge that crosses gas detention means the opcode does not complete, so its data size, KV updates and state growth are not counted, and kind 2 is the stop.
  A call to a precompile whose price crosses gas detention is decided from the price before its value moves, and is held to the price alone (`SATIN-DET-022`, [Gas Detention](gas-detention.md)).

SATIN-LIM-011.text:
- `SATIN-LIM-011` Within one dimension the frame budget MUST be tested before the transaction limit.
  When the frame budget is crossed, the stop MUST name that budget, its `limit` being that budget, also when the transaction limit of the same dimension is crossed too.
  When the frame budget is not crossed — no budget applies, or the frame's own budget still holds the write — a crossing of the transaction limit MUST name that limit, its `limit` being the transaction limit.

SATIN-LIM-012.text:
- `SATIN-LIM-012` A node MUST NOT hold an Oracle hint's bytes, which are counted on the transaction and on no frame, or the authorization list, which is decided before the first frame, to any frame budget.
  A framed write can therefore cross the transaction's data-size limit alone, after hints used what the transaction had left, while its frame's budget still holds it; the stop then names the transaction limit, and the admitted hint bytes stay counted.
  A framed write of KV updates or of state growth cannot cross the transaction limit without crossing its frame budget, since once a frame runs those dimensions have no usage that sits on no frame.

SATIN-LIM-013.text:
- `SATIN-LIM-013` A frame start MUST be held to the limits once it is decided — once the value moved and, for a creation, the creator's nonce was bumped and the created account made — and MUST be held to what the start kept: the write records, the state growth and the transfer log of the accounts it changed ([Resource Accounting](resource-accounting.md), [EIP-7708 Transfer Logs](transfer-logs.md)).
  What the start kept MUST be held first to the started frame's own budget — for a child, its share of the caller's remaining (`SATIN-LIM-003`) — and then to the transaction limit, so a crossing of that budget names it (`SATIN-LIM-011`); the creator's nonce record is the exception, held to the creator's budget (`SATIN-LIM-008`).
  A start that crosses is stopped before the frame runs an instruction ([Limit Stops](limit-stops.md)).

SATIN-LIM-014.text: - `SATIN-LIM-014` A start answered with a failure — a precompile that fails after its value moved — kept nothing, its failure taking back the value and the transfer log: it MUST count nothing and MUST NOT be stopped by a limit, and its result is the precompile's failure, which consumes the gas forwarded to it.

SATIN-LIM-015.text:
- `SATIN-LIM-015` A start the caller's account refuses — a value the caller cannot fund, a creation whose creator nonce cannot be bumped — MUST count nothing, MUST make no start record, and MUST NOT be stopped by a limit for anything that start would have counted; it is charged no history for start records (`SATIN-HIST-015`).
  Interception comes before the start, and what it did is not the start's (`SATIN-ICPT-007`): an admitted `sendHint` stays counted on the transaction (`SATIN-ORCL-009`), and a call an interceptor answers never reaches the start.
  What the opcode charged before the refusal, and what of it is given back, is `SATIN-HIST-023`'s.
  A creation transaction whose sender's nonce cannot be bumped MUST likewise create nothing: its own frame starts no creation, counts nothing, is stopped by no limit, and the transaction succeeds without a created account ([Deposit Transactions](../block/deposits.md) for a deposit).

SATIN-LIM-016.text:
- `SATIN-LIM-016` A creation onto an occupied address ([SELFDESTRUCT and the Destruction Table](selfdestruct.md)) fails on the collision after its creator's nonce was bumped, and MUST NOT be stopped for what its start would count: its failure discards the created account's record and its transfer log, and the creator's nonce record, which survives it, MUST be counted on the creator when the creation returns (`SATIN-LIM-008`).
  The created account was not new, so the collision adds no state growth.

SATIN-LIM-017.section: Specification > The limits are protocol values
SATIN-LIM-017.text:
- `SATIN-LIM-017` The transaction limits of `SATIN-LIM-001`, the frame share of `SATIN-LIM-003`, the detention caps ([Gas Detention](gas-detention.md)) and the block's data-size, KV and state-growth limits ([Block Limits and Packing](../block/block-limits.md)) are protocol values of the spec, the same on every chain.
  A node MUST hold every transaction and block it executes or validates to them, and MUST NOT take them from a chain configuration or from values handed with a block.
  How a node executes a call, a gas estimate or a simulation outside a block is outside this specification.

SATIN-LIM-018.text: - `SATIN-LIM-018` Retired: removed. The expectation that an execution outside a block uses the same limits and caps is node documentation, not a rule of block execution.

SATIN-LOG-001.text:
- `SATIN-LOG-001` A node MUST apply EIP-7708's transfer log: every movement of value to another account — the transaction's value, a value `CALL`, a creation's endowment, a `SELFDESTRUCT` that moves a balance to another account — MUST emit `Transfer(address indexed from, address indexed to, uint256 value)` from `TRANSFER_LOG_ADDRESS`, with `TRANSFER_TOPIC` as its first topic, `from` and `to` as its second and third, and `value` as its data.
  The transfer log MUST be that of EIP-7708 as of [commit `f7230c46a7`](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/commit/f7230c46a743313957d8f38a159bda934cc735b2) (10 July 2026), the revision current when the EIP-8037 profile was frozen (`SATIN-POOL-004`), as this page restates it.

SATIN-LOG-002.text: - `SATIN-LOG-002` The log MUST appear in the receipt in execution order among the contracts' own logs, where the value moves; a failed frame's transfer logs MUST be discarded with the rest of its logs.

SATIN-LOG-003.text: - `SATIN-LOG-003` A `CALLCODE`, a call to the calling account itself, and a transaction's value sent to its own sender move nothing to another account and MUST NOT log.

SATIN-LOG-004.text: - `SATIN-LOG-004` A deposit's value MUST be logged; its mint MUST NOT be.

SATIN-LOG-005.text:
- `SATIN-LOG-005` A node MUST NOT emit any other log any revision of EIP-7708 defines, a `Burn` log included, and MUST NOT apply [EIP-8246](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8246): a balance can still be burned, and a burn MUST NOT log.
  Two burns remain, both silent: a `SELFDESTRUCT` to itself of an account created in the same transaction burns the balance at once, and an account destroyed in the transaction is removed at its end with whatever balance it then holds, a value it received after its destruction included, whose `CALL` logged the transfer ([SELFDESTRUCT and the Destruction Table](selfdestruct.md)).

SATIN-LOG-006.text: - `SATIN-LOG-006` A transfer log MUST count `TRANSFER_LOG_SIZE` bytes of data size where the value moves — with the start of the frame that moves it, held to the limits with the start's records (`SATIN-LIM-013`), or with the `SELFDESTRUCT` that moves it — and MUST NOT be a write record, MUST NOT pay history gas, and MUST NOT draw on a history allowance ([History Gas and the History Allowance](history-gas.md)).

SATIN-LOG-007.text: - `SATIN-LOG-007` A frame start that the caller's account refuses (`SATIN-LIM-015`, `SATIN-HIST-023`), and a creation with an endowment onto an occupied address, which fails on the collision before the endowment moves (`SATIN-LIM-016`), move nothing and MUST log nothing.

SATIN-MAC-001.section: Specification > The contract and its methods

SATIN-MAC-002.section: Specification > The contract and its methods
SATIN-MAC-002.text: - `SATIN-MAC-002` `disableVolatileDataAccess()` MUST switch access off only once its answer is settled; an answer that gas detention turns into the compute stop (see [Call Interception](interception.md), `SATIN-ICPT-005`) MUST leave the switch as it was.

SATIN-MAC-003.text:
- `SATIN-MAC-003` In a frame whose volatile-data access is off, every volatile read (see [Gas Detention](../evm/gas-detention.md)) MUST be refused:
  - an opcode that is volatile whatever its operands — `NUMBER`, `TIMESTAMP`, `COINBASE`, `PREVRANDAO`, `GASLIMIT`, `BASEFEE`, `BLOBBASEFEE`, `SLOTNUM` and `BLOCKHASH` — MUST be refused before its operands are checked and before any of its gas is charged, so a `BLOCKHASH` on an empty stack is refused rather than halting on the underflow;
  - an opcode that is volatile only for the account or the storage it reads — `BALANCE`, `SELFBALANCE`, `EXTCODESIZE`, `EXTCODECOPY`, `EXTCODEHASH`, the four call opcodes, `SELFDESTRUCT`, and `SLOAD` of the Oracle's storage — MUST first have every operand it takes on the stack: such an opcode that fails on its operands — a stack underflow, for example — MUST fail as it would with access on.
    Once its operands are there, it MUST be refused when what it reads is the beneficiary's account or the Oracle's storage, as its operands and its frame show it: the target operand of `BALANCE`, `EXTCODESIZE`, `EXTCODECOPY`, `EXTCODEHASH` or a call opcode; the executing frame's own address for `SELFBALANCE`, and for `SELFDESTRUCT`, whose target operand is checked too; the frame's storage for an `SLOAD`.
    The refusal MUST come before the opcode charges anything and before any other check its body makes — a memory expansion, a copy, a static-context check, a value transfer, a state charge — so an `EXTCODECOPY` of the beneficiary with a large length, or a call to it the frame could not fund, is refused rather than running out of gas;
  - a call opcode whose target operand is not the block beneficiary MUST be refused when its target's one-hop EIP-7702 delegate is the beneficiary, at the load of that delegate and not before the call's own steps, as `SATIN-MAC-007` specifies.

  Every refusal comes before the opcode pushes a result, so a read on a full stack MUST be refused rather than overflow the stack.
  A `BLOCKHASH` MUST be refused as `BLOCKHASH`, access type 7, whatever its operand.

SATIN-MAC-004.text:
- `SATIN-MAC-004` A refused read MUST revert the frame with `VolatileDataAccessDisabled(accessType)`, unless it is a call refused at its target's EIP-7702 delegate (`SATIN-MAC-007`) whose cold surcharge is gas detention's crossing, which MUST stop the frame with `MegaLimitExceeded(2, limit)` instead ([Limit Stops](../evm/limit-stops.md)).
  A read refused before the opcode's body, by the first two items of `SATIN-MAC-003`, MUST NOT consume any gas: neither the opcode's static gas nor any dynamic cost (a cold access, a copy's memory, a call's memory or value transfer).
  Such a frame MUST revert on the gas it held when the opcode was reached, nothing having been charged, and a frame whose regular gas is below the opcode's static gas, or below what the opcode's body would charge, MUST be refused all the same and MUST NOT run out of gas.
  A call refused at its target's delegate has made its earlier steps and read its target's account and code, which is not a volatile read; it MUST pay its target's access (its cold surcharge unless that is gas detention's crossing) and its memory expansion, and nothing else:
  - its regular gas, the spendable and the withheld part, MUST be restored to what it held when the opcode was reached;
  - it MUST then be charged, as regular charges and in this order: its static cost, `WARM_STORAGE_READ_COST`; its memory expansion; and, when the target was not warm, its cold surcharge, `COLD_ACCOUNT_ACCESS − WARM_STORAGE_READ_COST`, last;
  - its memory expansion is this opcode's own growth of memory for its input and output ranges together, at the base layer's price, and nothing for a range already within the frame's memory; it is not the frame's whole memory cost.

  The first two charges leave the call's gas as it was just after its memory expansion, so the static cost and the memory expansion remain charged and count as compute once (`SATIN-DET-009`); the value-transfer cost of a call that carries value is given back by the restoration and is not compute, and the refused delegate's access is never charged.
  The cold surcharge MUST come last: when it is gas detention's crossing, the gas is put back to what it was just before it (`SATIN-DET-018`), so the memory expansion stays charged at the stop as well.
  Nothing before the delegate's load draws on the reservoir, so the restoration and the charges leave it as the opcode found it; the frame's end then rolls back its own state and history charges as any revert or stop does (`SATIN-POOL-014`).
  A refused read marks nothing for gas detention and asks no oracle service.

SATIN-MAC-005.text:
- `SATIN-MAC-005` The error's argument MUST be ABI-encoded as a `uint8`, with the value of the table below.
  Values 3 and 9 MUST NOT be produced.
  Value 12 is outside the contract's `VolatileDataAccessType` enum.

| `accessType` | Read refused                     |
| ------------ | -------------------------------- |
| 0            | `NUMBER`                         |
| 1            | `TIMESTAMP`                      |
| 2            | `COINBASE`                       |
| 4            | `GASLIMIT`                       |
| 5            | `BASEFEE`                        |
| 6            | `PREVRANDAO` (`0x44`)            |
| 7            | `BLOCKHASH`                      |
| 8            | `BLOBBASEFEE`                    |
| 10           | The block beneficiary's account  |
| 11           | The Oracle's storage             |
| 12           | `SLOTNUM`                        |

SATIN-MAC-006.text: - `SATIN-MAC-006` A `CREATE` or `CREATE2` MUST NOT be refused in a frame whose access is off, even when its creator or its created address is the block beneficiary: its loads of them are the creation's own checks, not volatile reads.

SATIN-MAC-007.text:
- `SATIN-MAC-007` In a frame whose volatile-data access is off, a call opcode (`CALL`, `CALLCODE`, `DELEGATECALL` or `STATICCALL`) whose target operand is not the block beneficiary MUST read its target only at the target's load, after the steps before it, and MUST make the steps that come before its delegate's load as it would with access on:
  - its static cost, `WARM_STORAGE_READ_COST`, and the static-context check of a `CALL` that carries value;
  - its memory expansion (`SATIN-MAC-004`), and the value-transfer cost of a `CALL` or `CALLCODE` that carries value ([Gas Schedule and Intrinsic Gas](../evm/gas-schedule.md), `SATIN-SCHED-003`);
  - the load of its target's account and code, skipped with an out-of-gas halt when the target is not warm and the regular gas left, both parts counted (`SATIN-DET-015`), is below the cold surcharge, `COLD_ACCOUNT_ACCESS − WARM_STORAGE_READ_COST`;
  - when the target holds an EIP-7702 delegation indicator, the delegation guard, which halts the call out of gas unless the regular gas left, both parts counted, covers the target's cold surcharge, not yet deducted (the surcharge for a target that was not warm, zero for one that was), plus `WARM_STORAGE_READ_COST` for the delegate's access; the static cost the call has paid is not counted again.

  A call that fails at one of these steps, or is stopped at one as gas detention's crossing (`SATIN-DET-018`), has not reached its delegate's load and MUST end as it would with access on; it has read its target's account and code exactly when it made the target's load, which a cold load skipped for its surcharge does not make.
  When the call reaches its delegate's load and that one-hop delegate is the block beneficiary, the load MUST be refused as the beneficiary's account (type 10) before anything else on the call's path: before the target's cold surcharge is deducted, before any new-account state gas, the forward and the start's history gas, and before any frame starts.
  The beneficiary's account MUST NOT be loaded, and the call's gas MUST be settled as `SATIN-MAC-004` states.
  For these rules the target was warm when it was among EIP-2929's accessed addresses as they stood when the call reached the target's load: the addresses warm from the transaction's start (`SATIN-SCHED-012`, `SATIN-SCHED-014`), and every address an earlier access warmed that no rollback has taken back, the authorities the authorization list's application warmed included (`SATIN-AUTH-014`); the call's own load of the target does not count.
  No charge of that settlement can run out of gas: the static cost and the memory expansion were paid from the same gas before the delegate's load, and the delegation guard held the regular gas left after them and after the value-transfer cost to at least the cold surcharge plus `WARM_STORAGE_READ_COST`.
  The cold surcharge MUST therefore be paid, or be gas detention's crossing when the spendable part cannot pay it (`SATIN-DET-018`), and MUST NOT halt the frame out of gas.
  The frame's end, the revert or the stop, MUST leave the target's account and code in the transaction's read set (`SATIN-WIT-002`, `SATIN-WIT-012`), and MUST roll EIP-2929's accessed addresses back to the ending frame's checkpoint, taken when that frame started: the warming the frame took, its warming of the target included, is undone, and a warmth from before the frame started stays.
  Whenever the call makes its target's load, the load is a required read: a failed read of the target's account or code MUST be reported as `SATIN-VAL-010` classifies a failed read of the transaction's execution, and MUST NOT be taken as a target without a delegate ([Transaction Validation and Refusals](../block/transaction-validation.md)).

SATIN-MLC-003.text: - `SATIN-MLC-003` The answer MUST count regular gas only: the reservoir is not part of it, so a transaction whose gas limit is above the execution cap hears at most the regular gas the execution cap leaves it.

SATIN-MLC-004.text: - `SATIN-MLC-004` A transaction that calls the contract directly has no calling frame: `own` is the gas its own frame was given, so it MUST hear its own frame's regular gas, or less when it is detained from its start (its sender is the block beneficiary, or an EIP-7702 authority it applies is).

SATIN-MST-001.text: - `SATIN-MST-001` A transaction MUST be taken to have the system shape when, judged on its own fields alone, it is of type `0x0` (legacy) and is a call — not a creation — to an address on `MEGA_SYSTEM_TX_WHITELIST`.

SATIN-MST-002.text: - `SATIN-MST-002` A transaction of the system shape whose caller is the live system address (see [SequencerRegistry](sequencer-registry.md), `SATIN-REG-002`) MUST be a Mega System Transaction.

SATIN-MST-003.text: - `SATIN-MST-003` A transaction whose caller is the live system address and that does not have the system shape MUST be invalid, whatever its type: a transaction other than a deposit MUST be rejected (see [Transaction Validation and Refusals](../block/transaction-validation.md)), and a deposit, which never has the system shape, MUST be included as a failed deposit, which runs no call (see [Deposit Transactions](../block/deposits.md)); that includes a deposit handed to the node already carrying the promotion's source hash.

SATIN-MST-004.text: - `SATIN-MST-004` A transaction whose caller is any other address MUST NOT be a Mega System Transaction, and MUST be validated and charged as a user's: that includes a transaction from an address a rotation retired, which is no longer the live system address.

SATIN-MST-005.text:
- `SATIN-MST-005` A Mega System Transaction MUST be validated before it is promoted to a deposit, and a failure MUST be a rejection: it MUST carry a chain id, equal to the chain's; its nonce MUST equal the system address's nonce; and the system address MUST hold no code other than an EIP-7702 delegation indicator, as [EIP-3607](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-3607) requires of any sender.
  The chain-id check MUST be made whatever the node's configuration says (`SATIN-VAL-006`); the nonce and EIP-3607 checks are those every sender is held to, and a configuration that switches either off for a user's transaction switches it off for a Mega System Transaction too.
  Once it passes them, the transaction MUST be executed as a deposit from the system address to its recipient, with its value, gas limit and input, no mint, and the gas price zero: no signature, nonce, fee or balance-for-fee check of its own is made, no fee is charged and no fee recipient is credited, the caller its recipient sees is the system address, and the system address's nonce is bumped as a deposit's sender's is.
  A check the deposit then fails, or a first frame that halts, makes it a failed deposit (see [Deposit Transactions](../block/deposits.md)).

SATIN-MST-006.text: - `SATIN-MST-006` The promotion MUST stamp the deposit with the source hash `MEGA_SYSTEM_TRANSACTION_SOURCE_HASH`.

SATIN-MST-007.text:
- `SATIN-MST-007` A transaction MUST be system-originated when it is a Mega System Transaction, before or after its promotion; when its caller is `SYSTEM_CALLER`, the caller of the pre-block calls; or when it is a deposit carrying `MEGA_SYSTEM_TRANSACTION_SOURCE_HASH`, whoever its caller.
  The test MUST be made on the transaction's own fields, in a block as outside one: a transaction of any type from `SYSTEM_CALLER`, or a deposit carrying that source hash, is the protocol's wherever it is executed, a call or a simulation included.
  Only a deposit carries a source hash: a transaction handed to a node with one is a deposit, and is executed as one, whatever type its other fields name.
  A deposit carrying that source hash from the live system address is system-originated and, by `SATIN-MST-003`, a failed deposit.
  A system call — a pre-block call (see [System Calls and the Pre-Block Sequence](../block/system-calls.md)) — is the protocol's own work as well.

SATIN-MST-009.text: - `SATIN-MST-009` A system-originated transaction's usage MUST be reported, and MUST count toward the block's counters; a Mega System Transaction is held to the block's packing budgets as any other non-deposit transaction is (see [Block Limits and Packing](../block/block-limits.md), `SATIN-BLK-007`); a pre-block call's usage MUST count toward neither the block's counters nor its limits.

SATIN-MST-010.text: - `SATIN-MST-010` A user's deposit is not system-originated: it MUST be priced by bucket, held to every per-transaction limit and frame budget, and detained, and it pays history gas as any transaction does (see [Deposit Transactions](../block/deposits.md)).

SATIN-ORCL-001.text:
- `SATIN-ORCL-001` The Oracle MUST be the account at `ORACLE_CONTRACT_ADDRESS` holding the code of version 2.0.0 (`ORACLE_CODE_HASH`, see [System Contracts](overview.md)), whose interface and behaviour are the following.
  - **Storage.** The contract's storage is a flat map from a `uint256` slot to a `bytes32` value; each service that uses it is allotted a range of slots (the [High-Precision Timestamp](high-precision-timestamp.md)'s is slots 0 to 7).
  - **Reads.** `getSlot(uint256 slot) returns (bytes32 value)` returns the value at `slot`; `getSlots(uint256[] slots) returns (bytes32[] values)` returns the values at `slots`, in order. Both read by `SLOAD` in the Oracle's own frame.
  - **Restricted writes.** `setSlot(uint256 slot, bytes32 value)`, `setSlots(uint256[] slots, bytes32[] values)`, `emitLog(bytes32 topic, bytes data)` and `emitLogs(bytes32 topic, bytes[] dataVector)` write the slots or emit the logs, and then revert with `NotSystemAddress()` unless the immediate caller is the address `SequencerRegistry.currentSystemAddress()` returns (see [SequencerRegistry](sequencer-registry.md)). The body — every `SSTORE`, `LOG` and loop iteration — runs before that check and is charged as it runs; the revert takes back every write and log. `setSlots` with arrays of different lengths reverts with `InvalidLength(uint256 slotsLength, uint256 valuesLength)` before any `SSTORE` and before the check.
  - **Auxiliary.** `multiCall(bytes[] data) returns (bytes[] results)` executes each payload by `DELEGATECALL` into the Oracle and returns the results in order; at the first payload that fails it reverts with that payload's revert data when the data are not empty, and with `Error(string)` carrying `"Multicall: call failed"` when they are empty; `sendHint(bytes32 topic, bytes data)` is a no-op `view` method at the bytecode level.

SATIN-ORCL-002.text:
- `SATIN-ORCL-002` An `SLOAD` executed in the Oracle's own frame — a frame whose storage is the Oracle's: a frame running at the Oracle's address, the frames of `multiCall`'s `DELEGATECALL`s of the Oracle into itself included, and not a `DELEGATECALL` from another account into the Oracle's code, which runs on that account's storage — MUST load the slot from the state through the transaction's journal, then, unless the read is made during a system call, a deposit or a Mega System Transaction (see below), ask the node's oracle service for the slot, and push the service's value when the service gives one and the loaded value otherwise.
  The service's value MUST win over whatever the slot holds at the read, a value the Oracle's own frame wrote earlier in the transaction included; with no value from the service the read MUST push the slot's present value, that write included.

SATIN-ORCL-003.text:
- `SATIN-ORCL-003` Every such read MUST be charged as a cold storage access, `COLD_SLOAD_COST`, however often the slot was read before, and the slot MUST be loaded whichever source answers, so that a later access finds it warm and a stateless witness carries it.
  The read is a read of volatile data for [gas detention](../evm/gas-detention.md), under the Oracle's cap.

SATIN-ORCL-004.text:
- `SATIN-ORCL-004` The read MUST be made before the cold access is charged: the slot is loaded, the service asked when the read is one that asks it, and the read marked for gas detention (`SATIN-DET-003`), and only then is `COLD_SLOAD_COST` charged, as one charge, its warm base of 100 included: no part of the `SLOAD`'s gas is charged before the read.
  A frame whose regular gas, its withheld part included, cannot pay the cold access — whether it holds fewer than the 100 of the warm base or from 100 to 2,099 — MUST therefore load the slot, ask the service where it is asked, and mark the read, and then run out of gas at the `SLOAD`; the mark MUST stand for the rest of the transaction, though the frame halts.
  When the charge is gas detention's crossing (`SATIN-DET-018`) — the spendable part cannot pay it but the whole regular gas can — the frame is stopped and the `SLOAD` does not complete, and the slot stays loaded and the read marked all the same.
  A read refused because the frame's volatile-data access is off (see [MegaAccessControl](mega-access-control.md)) MUST NOT ask the service, and marks nothing.

SATIN-ORCL-005.text:
- `SATIN-ORCL-005` During a system call, a deposit or a Mega System Transaction the node MUST NOT ask the oracle service for a value: an `SLOAD` in the Oracle's own frame MUST push the slot's value on the chain — its present value, a write made earlier in the same call or transaction included (`SATIN-ORCL-002`) — and MUST be loaded, priced and marked as any Oracle read is (`SATIN-ORCL-003`, `SATIN-ORCL-004`).
  Only the reads of a transaction that is neither a deposit nor a Mega System Transaction ask the service; the rule holds for the whole of the system call or transaction it covers and ends with it.
  The rule concerns reads: a `sendHint` call made in such a call or transaction is admitted, forwarded and counted by the rules of Hints below, as in any transaction, and asks the service for no value.
  It follows that no read of the block in which Satin activates asks the service: that block admits only deposits (see [Base Layer](../base-layer.md), `SATIN-BASE-006`, `SATIN-BASE-008`).

SATIN-ORCL-006.text:
- `SATIN-ORCL-006` A `sendHint` call MUST be admitted, and its hint forwarded to the oracle service synchronously, when it is called, before the call returns, only when both of the following hold: the call's gas limit is more than zero, and the frame that makes it has its volatile-data access on (see [MegaAccessControl](mega-access-control.md)); whether the call carries value does not matter.
  The gas limit is the regular gas the call's frame starts with, a value call's stipend included, as Rex6 judges it: for a call opcode the gas `SATIN-FWD-003` gives the child (see [Gas Forwarding](../evm/gas-forwarding.md)), so a value-transferring `CALL` that requests no gas starts its frame on the stipend, and its hint is admitted and counted.
  A `sendHint` that is the transaction's own call, a deposit's included, has no stipend (`SATIN-FWD-003` adds `CALL_STIPEND` only for the opcodes) and is judged on its first frame's whole regular gas: it is admitted whenever that gas is more than zero, whether or not the transaction carries value.
  A call that fails either condition MUST drop the hint and count nothing.
  Whether admitted or not, the call then reaches its frame start and runs the Oracle's bytecode, unless the rule `SATIN-ORCL-010` below answers it first.
  Admission comes before the frame start, where the caller's funds are checked (`SATIN-ICPT-007`): a `sendHint` carrying a value its caller cannot fund is admitted, forwarded and counted as any hint is, and its frame start then refuses the call, which fails with empty return data and runs no bytecode (`SATIN-OUT-010`); the hint stays counted (`SATIN-ORCL-009`).

SATIN-ORCL-007.text: - `SATIN-ORCL-007` The service MUST be handed the hint's `topic`, its `data`, and the address of the frame that made the call: the transaction's sender for a `sendHint` that is the transaction's own call.

SATIN-ORCL-008.text:
- `SATIN-ORCL-008` Only a `CALL` or a `STATICCALL` whose target is the Oracle and whose input's first four bytes are the selector of `sendHint(bytes32,bytes)` is a `sendHint` call.
  A `CALLCODE` or `DELEGATECALL` of the method — `multiCall`'s payloads among them — runs the Oracle's bytecode in a frame of the caller's own context, MUST NOT reach the service and MUST count nothing.

SATIN-ORCL-009.text:
- `SATIN-ORCL-009` An admitted call MUST count its whole input length as data size on the transaction, before the input is decoded, on no frame's budget, and MUST pay no history gas.
  A `sendHint` that is the transaction's own call MUST count its input twice: once as calldata in the transaction's body, and once as the hint.
  An admitted input MUST stay counted whatever the calling frame or the transaction does afterwards — a revert, a halt, a later stop, a failed deposit — and that includes an input that does not decode as `sendHint(bytes32,bytes)`, which reaches no service.

SATIN-ORCL-010.text:
- `SATIN-ORCL-010` A `sendHint` call whose input length would take the transaction's data size over its data-size limit (see [Resource Limits](../evm/resource-limits.md)) MUST NOT be forwarded and MUST NOT be counted.
  The call MUST be answered with the data-size stop, `MegaLimitExceeded(0, limit)` (see [Limit Stops](../evm/limit-stops.md)), without running the Oracle's bytecode: the check is made at admission, before the frame start and its funds check (`SATIN-ICPT-007`); the stop is the call's, which its caller can catch, and when the call is the transaction's own frame, the stop the transaction reports counts the data size the hint would have reached as used.
  The data size the transaction keeps, which the block's data-size budget counts, holds none of the hint's bytes.
  The check is against the transaction's limit alone: a hint's bytes are on no frame's budget.

SATIN-ORCL-011.text:
- `SATIN-ORCL-011` A restricted write MUST be authorized as the Oracle's bytecode authorizes it, and by no further rule of the node's: once the body has run, the write stands when the immediate caller of the Oracle's frame is the address `SequencerRegistry.currentSystemAddress()` returns, and the call reverts with `NotSystemAddress()` otherwise, whatever sent the transaction and whatever the transaction's type.
  The sequencer writes the Oracle through Mega System Transactions (see [Mega System Transactions](system-tx.md)); code running at the live system address writes it as well — the [High-Precision Timestamp](high-precision-timestamp.md)'s `update` while that contract is the live system address (`SATIN-HPTS-001`), or the code an EIP-7702 delegation of the system address runs, a deposit's call among them — since the registry accepts any non-zero address as the system address (`SATIN-REG-001`).

SATIN-ORCL-012.text:
- `SATIN-ORCL-012` For a transaction the block includes, the sequencer MUST persist on-chain every value of the oracle service that one of its Oracle reads pushed, unless the transaction's own writes explain it, by inserting a [Mega System Transaction](system-tx.md) that calls `setSlot` or `setSlots`, ordered before that transaction, so that every node replaying the block observes the same storage state.
  The sequencer MAY persist in the same way a value the service gave a read that pushed nothing — a read made before its charge whose frame then ran out of gas at the `SLOAD`, or was stopped at gas detention's crossing (`SATIN-ORCL-004`) — and need not: the replay of that read pushes nothing either, whatever the slot holds; a value so persisted MUST leave the slot holding, when the transaction starts, a value that still reproduces its reads (`SATIN-ORCL-013`).
  A system call, a deposit and a Mega System Transaction are given no value by the service (`SATIN-ORCL-005`), so nothing is persisted for them.
  The transaction's own writes explain a served value when the slot's present value at the read is one the transaction itself wrote to the slot earlier in it — by a restricted write the Oracle authorized (`SATIN-ORCL-011`) and no revert has taken back — and that value is the value served: the replay of the read pushes that write, and nothing written before the transaction need hold the value.
  A node that validates or replays a block runs no oracle service: each Oracle read it makes has no value from the service and pushes the slot's present value (`SATIN-ORCL-002`), which the Mega System Transactions before the reading transaction wrote, or, after a write of the transaction's own to the slot, that write.
  A transaction is therefore not included when a value this rule requires for it cannot be persisted before it in the block, its Mega System Transaction being skipped or refused.

SATIN-ORCL-013.text:
- `SATIN-ORCL-013` A transaction MUST NOT be included in a block when an Oracle slot it reads has no value that, written before the transaction, would make the transaction's replay push, at each of its reads of that slot that pushed a value, the value that read pushed, the replay's read pushing the slot's present value, a write the transaction made to the slot earlier in it included (`SATIN-ORCL-002`); a read that pushed nothing — its frame out of gas or stopped at the `SLOAD` (`SATIN-ORCL-004`) — asks nothing of the slot's value.
  A transaction is left out by this rule only then: one for which such a value exists for every slot it reads is not.
  A deposit or a Mega System Transaction is never left out by it, since the service gives none of its reads a value (`SATIN-ORCL-005`): each pushes the slot's present value, as its replay does.
  A transaction that reads a slot the service answers, then sends a hint that has the service fetch another value, and then reads the slot again, answered that other value, with no write of its own to the slot between, is left out: one slot answers it two values, and no single value written before it reproduces both.
  A transaction that reads a slot the service answers 7, writes 8 to it by a restricted write the Oracle authorizes, and reads it again, answered 8, is not: the value 7 written before it reproduces the first read, and the second pushes the transaction's own write, which explains the value 8 (`SATIN-ORCL-012`).

SATIN-OUT-002.text:
- `SATIN-OUT-002` Every resource limit and gas detention's compute limit MUST revert only the frame that crosses it, and its caller MAY catch the stop; no limit halts a frame or a transaction.
  What the stop reverts, keeps and reports is [Limit Stops](limit-stops.md); which limits exist is [Resource Limits](resource-limits.md) and [Gas Detention](gas-detention.md).

SATIN-OUT-003.text: - `SATIN-OUT-003` Initcode over `MAX_INITCODE_SIZE` and deployed code over `MAX_CONTRACT_SIZE` MUST end as [Contract Size Limits](contract-limits.md) specifies (`SATIN-SIZE-003`, `SATIN-SIZE-004`): a rejection of a creation transaction, a halt at a creation opcode or of a creation, a refusal of a keyless deployment.

SATIN-OUT-004.text: - `SATIN-OUT-004` An input over an OP precompile's size limit MUST fail the call as [Precompiles](precompiles.md) specifies (`SATIN-PCMP-005`): a halt of the call.

SATIN-OUT-005.text: - `SATIN-OUT-005` A failed deposit MUST use its whole gas limit and report no stop ([Deposit Transactions](../block/deposits.md)).

SATIN-OUT-006.text: - `SATIN-OUT-006` A charge made before the first frame that the transaction cannot pay MUST end the transaction out of gas without running a frame, as `SATIN-SCHED-009` and `SATIN-SCHED-010` specify ([Gas Schedule and Intrinsic Gas](gas-schedule.md)): a non-deposit is included out of gas, and a deposit becomes a failed deposit.

SATIN-OUT-007.text:
- `SATIN-OUT-007` A real out-of-gas, a precompile given less than its price, an invalid opcode, and every other exceptional halt of the base layer ([Base Layer](../base-layer.md)) MUST halt and consume the halting frame's regular gas (`SATIN-POOL-014`).
  So do a regular charge beyond the frame's whole regular gas under gas detention (`SATIN-DET-020`) and a code-deposit charge a creation cannot pay (`SATIN-SCHED-011`).

SATIN-OUT-008.text: - `SATIN-OUT-008` A refused volatile read MUST revert its frame with `VolatileDataAccessDisabled(uint8)`, as [MegaAccessControl](../system-contracts/mega-access-control.md) specifies, with one exception: a call refused at its target's EIP-7702 delegate whose cold surcharge is gas detention's crossing MUST stop its frame with `MegaLimitExceeded(2, limit)`, a limit stop (`SATIN-MAC-004`, `SATIN-MAC-007`).

SATIN-OUT-009.text: - `SATIN-OUT-009` A system contract's own refusal (for example `NonZeroTransfer()` or `NotIntercepted()`) MUST revert with its own error ([Call Interception](../system-contracts/interception.md)); a keyless deployment's step refuses or halts as `SATIN-KEY-004` states ([KeylessDeploy](../system-contracts/keyless-deploy.md)).

SATIN-OUT-010.text:
- `SATIN-OUT-010` A call refused at the depth gate, or at its frame start for a value its caller cannot fund, MUST fail with empty return data and count nothing for the refused start (`SATIN-LIM-015`); it is neither a halt of the caller nor a stop.
  Interception's answers, stops and admissions keep their own results and counts (`SATIN-ICPT-007`, `SATIN-ORCL-006`).

SATIN-OUT-011.text: - `SATIN-OUT-011` A precompile that fails MUST consume all the gas forwarded to it ([Precompiles](precompiles.md)), and a start answered with that failure is not replaced by a stop (`SATIN-LIM-014`).

SATIN-OUT-012.text: - `SATIN-OUT-012` A creation opcode in a static frame, or short of its operands, MUST halt its frame, unless a charge it makes before the failing check is gas detention's crossing (`SATIN-SIZE-006`).

SATIN-OUT-013.section: Specification > How the transaction's own frame ends
SATIN-OUT-013.text: - `SATIN-OUT-013` A halt of the transaction's own frame ends the transaction as `SATIN-POOL-017` settles it, with a failed receipt; for a deposit it is a failed deposit (`SATIN-DEP-004`, [Deposit Transactions](../block/deposits.md)).

SATIN-OUT-014.section: Specification > How the transaction's own frame ends
SATIN-OUT-014.text: - `SATIN-OUT-014` A revert of the transaction's own frame ends the transaction with a failed receipt, as `SATIN-POOL-017` settles it, and a limit stop of that frame as `SATIN-STOP-009` settles it; for a deposit either is a revert, not a failed deposit (`SATIN-STOP-010`).

SATIN-OUT-015.text: - `SATIN-OUT-015` A failed bucket-capacity read (`SATIN-STATE-007`) or a failed database read MUST NOT be an outcome of the transaction, for a deposit as for any transaction: the transaction is not settled, and the node reports the fault as `SATIN-VAL-010` classifies it ([Transaction Validation and Refusals](../block/transaction-validation.md)).

SATIN-OUT-016.section: Specification > How the transaction's own frame ends
SATIN-OUT-016.text: - `SATIN-OUT-016` A transaction that fails validation MUST report no stop (`SATIN-STOP-003`): a non-deposit is rejected, a Mega System Transaction that fails its own checks among them, and a deposit is included as a failed deposit (`SATIN-VAL-008`, `SATIN-DEP-004`).

SATIN-OUT-017.text: - `SATIN-OUT-017` What a tracer or inspector is shown of an execution is outside this specification, and a node MAY show it any frames — for a transaction whose first frame cannot pay a charge made before it runs, one halted root frame or none; two nodes that agree on every outcome, gas figure, state change, log and read set conform whatever they show a tracer.

SATIN-OUT-018.text:
- `SATIN-OUT-018` This specification names no halt reason: a halt is identified only as a halt, and a node MAY label a halt with any reason, which is part of no receipt, state or witness.
  In particular the label of a failed `DUP`, `DUPN`, `SWAPN` or `EXCHANGE` (a stack underflow, a stack overflow or an invalid immediate) is not specified.

SATIN-PBLK-001.section: Specification > The gas of a system call
SATIN-PBLK-001.text:
- `SATIN-PBLK-001` A system call MUST run on at most `SYSTEM_CALL_REGULAR_GAS_LIMIT` of regular gas, the rest of its gas limit being its state-gas reservoir, as [EIP-8037](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8037) specifies for system calls; `GAS` inside a system call MUST read at most `SYSTEM_CALL_REGULAR_GAS_LIMIT`.
  A transaction is not a system call, a Mega System Transaction included: every transaction's gas is split by the execution cap (see [Two-Pool Gas](../evm/gas-model.md)).
  A system call is the protocol's own work and is exempt as [Mega System Transactions](../system-contracts/system-tx.md) (`SATIN-MST-008`) specifies.

SATIN-PBLK-002.section: Specification > The gas of a system call
SATIN-PBLK-002.text:
- `SATIN-PBLK-002` Each pre-block call MUST run from `SYSTEM_CALLER` on `PRE_BLOCK_CALL_GAS_LIMIT` of gas, whatever the block's gas limit: `SYSTEM_CALL_REGULAR_GAS_LIMIT` of regular gas and a reservoir of `PRE_BLOCK_CALL_GAS_LIMIT − SYSTEM_CALL_REGULAR_GAS_LIMIT`, the state gas of `SYSTEM_CALL_RESERVOIR_SLOTS` new storage slots at `m = 1`.
  A state charge MUST draw the call's pools as any frame's does: its legacy share, for a fresh slot, from the regular gas, then the reservoir, then the rest from the regular gas (see [Two-Pool Gas](../evm/gas-model.md), [State Gas and SALT Pricing](../evm/state-gas.md)).
  A pre-block call does not draw on the block's gas limit.

SATIN-PBLK-004.text:
- `SATIN-PBLK-004` A role change MUST be due in the block when the SequencerRegistry's account exists and, for the system-address role (pending address in slot 7, activation block in slot 8) or for the sequencer role (pending address in slot 9, activation block in slot 10), the pending address slot holds a non-zero value and the activation block slot holds a value at most the block's number.
  The read MUST load the registry's account and, for each role, its pending address slot, and its activation block slot only when the pending address is non-zero; an absent registry has no change due and MUST be recorded as absent.
  The read writes nothing; its loads are a read-only state of the pre-block phase (see [The Stateless Witness](stateless-witness.md)).

SATIN-PBLK-005.text: - `SATIN-PBLK-005` Retired, merged into `SATIN-ORCL-005` (see [Oracle](../system-contracts/oracle.md)): an Oracle read during a system call asks no oracle service.

SATIN-PBLK-006.text:
- `SATIN-PBLK-006` A pre-block call that does not succeed MUST make the block invalid, before its state is used.
  A database error the node's database declares fatal is an internal error of the node, not a verdict on the block; any other failure of a pre-block call — a database error not declared fatal, another execution error, a result that is not a success — MUST make the block invalid.
  A database error in the factory check, in a deployment, in the due-change read or in the resolution of the live system address is always an internal error of the node: a node whose database cannot serve them cannot execute the block, whatever its transactions.
  A registry the deployment cannot migrate (`SATIN-REG-008`), and one the resolution finds absent, holding other code or naming no system address (`SATIN-REG-004`), MUST make the block invalid.

SATIN-PCMP-001.text:
- `SATIN-PCMP-001` The precompile set MUST be Optimism Karst's, with KZG point evaluation (`0x0A`) at a fixed `KZG_POINT_EVALUATION_GAS`:

  | Precompile             | Address | Rule                                                            |
  | ---------------------- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | KZG point evaluation   | `0x0A`  | Fixed `KZG_POINT_EVALUATION_GAS`                                |
  | ModExp                 | `0x05`  | Osaka schedule (`SATIN-PCMP-002`)                               |
  | `P256VERIFY`           | `0x100` | `P256VERIFY_GAS` (`SATIN-PCMP-003`)                             |
  | BN254 pairing          | `0x08`  | Input of at most `BN254_PAIRING_MAX_INPUT_SIZE` bytes            |
  | BLS12-381 G1 MSM       | `0x0C`  | Input of at most `BLS12_G1_MSM_MAX_INPUT_SIZE` bytes             |
  | BLS12-381 G2 MSM       | `0x0E`  | Input of at most `BLS12_G2_MSM_MAX_INPUT_SIZE` bytes             |
  | BLS12-381 pairing      | `0x0F`  | Input of at most `BLS12_PAIRING_MAX_INPUT_SIZE` bytes            |
  | Every other precompile | Any     | As Karst defines it                                             |

  The system contracts are not precompiles ([System Contracts](../system-contracts/overview.md)).

SATIN-PCMP-002.text: - `SATIN-PCMP-002` ModExp (`0x05`) MUST run on the Osaka schedule: [EIP-7823](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7823)'s bound of `MODEXP_MAX_INPUT_SIZE` bytes on each of its three lengths, and [EIP-7883](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7883)'s pricing with its minimum of `MODEXP_MIN_GAS`.

SATIN-PCMP-003.text:
- `SATIN-PCMP-003` `P256VERIFY` (`0x100`) MUST cost `P256VERIFY_GAS` ([EIP-7951](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7951)).
  The precompile MUST be that of EIP-7951 as of [commit `b55cdb0ee7`](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/commit/b55cdb0ee78a696327cf76d1c5cf8088d73499ca) (21 January 2026), the revision current when the EIP-8037 profile was frozen (`SATIN-POOL-004`).

SATIN-PCMP-004.text: - `SATIN-PCMP-004` The OP precompiles' input size limits MUST be those the table of `SATIN-PCMP-001` gives BN254 pairing (`0x08`) and BLS12-381 G1 MSM (`0x0C`), G2 MSM (`0x0E`) and pairing (`0x0F`).

SATIN-PCMP-005.text: - `SATIN-PCMP-005` An input over one of those size limits MUST fail the call before any gas check, as the Optimism specification of the limit has it, a call forwarded no gas included, and MUST consume all the gas forwarded to it, as every precompile call that fails does.

SATIN-PCMP-006.text: - `SATIN-PCMP-006` A KZG point evaluation call given less than `KZG_POINT_EVALUATION_GAS` MUST fail out of gas before any verification runs; a successful call MUST be charged exactly `KZG_POINT_EVALUATION_GAS`; and a call given at least `KZG_POINT_EVALUATION_GAS` that fails otherwise — an input of the wrong length, a versioned hash that does not match the commitment, a proof that does not verify — MUST consume all the gas forwarded to it.

SATIN-PCMP-007.text:
- `SATIN-PCMP-007` ModExp MUST charge and check its input in this order: its `MODEXP_MIN_GAS` minimum, a call that cannot pay it failing before the lengths are read; then the rest of its formula price; then EIP-7823's bound, an input over it failing after its whole formula price is charged; then its computation.
  Lengths too large to price are priced past any gas a call can hold.

SATIN-PCMP-008.text:
- `SATIN-PCMP-008` A call that reaches precompile dispatch and whose address is a precompile's MUST run that precompile, and MUST be priced by it for gas detention ([Gas Detention](gas-detention.md)), whatever code the state holds at the address, an EIP-7702 delegation indicator included.
  The rule does not exempt the call from the call opcode's earlier charges, checks or refusal: in a frame whose volatile-data access is off, a call to a precompile address whose indicator names the block beneficiary ends at or before the delegate's load and never reaches dispatch ([MegaAccessControl](../system-contracts/mega-access-control.md), `SATIN-MAC-007`).

SATIN-POOL-001.text:
- `SATIN-POOL-001` A node MUST apply [EIP-8037](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8037) as of [commit `c406bdb2ff`](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/commit/c406bdb2ffbf2fbf9d85698e97b3b2e8b6e79112) (4 September 2026), with the parameters this page and [State Gas and SALT Pricing](state-gas.md) set: the execution cap, and the cost per state byte scaled by the bucket multiplier.
  The rules of the EIP a transaction's outcome depends on are stated on this page and on the pages it links; the EIP is cited for their provenance.

SATIN-POOL-002.text: - `SATIN-POOL-002` A node MUST apply these later changes to EIP-8037: the collision rule of [commit `dbc6d457cb`](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/commit/dbc6d457cbf90d5f9d55552f3fd91d58b88cc898) (18 September 2026), under which a creation does not collide on storage, as [SELFDESTRUCT and the Destruction Table](selfdestruct.md) states it; and, of the child-merge return of [commit `3ff5cff17a`](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/commit/3ff5cff17a11ab31273ee14ebea0df8bbc4f4aef) (4 September 2026) and the failure outcome of [commit `9dcd72754f`](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/commit/9dcd72754f3fe4b48a4dbeffee669dc4c60f7ec5) (14 September 2026), what the give-back rule of `SATIN-POOL-022` leaves of them: a returned reservoir joins the reservoir its caller kept and never draws it (`SATIN-POOL-012`), and a failure of the transaction's own frame returns no reservoir that a charge made before that frame drew (`SATIN-POOL-024`).

SATIN-POOL-003.text:
- `SATIN-POOL-003` A node MUST NOT apply the transaction gas cap of [commit `d7087803ca`](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/commit/d7087803ca236498c73f64665df0ddac7d621950) (14 September 2026): a transaction's gas limit is not capped at `TX_MAX_TOTAL_GAS_LIMIT` and stays bounded by the block's gas limit (see [Base Layer](../base-layer.md)).
  A node MUST NOT apply the commit of the pre-execution spill of [commit `9dcd72754f`](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/commit/9dcd72754f3fe4b48a4dbeffee669dc4c60f7ec5) as a rule of its own: under the give-back rule of `SATIN-POOL-022` the part of any charge that regular gas paid stays spent, a charge made before the first frame included (`SATIN-POOL-024`).

SATIN-POOL-004.text:
- `SATIN-POOL-004` The profile of EIP-8037 a node applies MUST be the one `SATIN-POOL-001` to `SATIN-POOL-003` and `SATIN-POOL-022` define, frozen at [commit `dbc6d457cb`](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/commit/dbc6d457cbf90d5f9d55552f3fd91d58b88cc898) (18 September 2026).
  The give-back rule and the legacy share of `SATIN-POOL-022` are departures from that commit, made in Satin's own words, and not the adoption of a later revision.
  A node MUST NOT apply a change made to EIP-8037 after that commit, whatever the EIP's status becomes; the removal of an unused counter ([commit `052029f362`](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/commit/052029f3625328d6f51dec8e62a7090201e66f17)), the co-author lines and the move to Last Call change no rule a transaction executes.

SATIN-POOL-005.text:
- `SATIN-POOL-005` At the start of a transaction's execution a node MUST split its gas limit into a regular budget and a reservoir:

  ```
  regular_budget = min(gas_limit, EXECUTION_CAP) − intrinsic_regular_gas
  reservoir      = max(0, gas_limit − EXECUTION_CAP)
  ```

  - `gas_limit` — the transaction's gas limit.
  - `EXECUTION_CAP` — the execution cap, the most regular gas one transaction can hold.
  - `intrinsic_regular_gas` — the regular part of the transaction's intrinsic gas ([Gas Schedule and Intrinsic Gas](gas-schedule.md)).

  Validation guarantees that `intrinsic_regular_gas` does not exceed `min(gas_limit, EXECUTION_CAP)` ([Transaction Validation and Refusals](../block/transaction-validation.md)).

SATIN-POOL-006.text:
- `SATIN-POOL-006` The intrinsic state gas, which is the history gas of the transaction's body ([History Gas and the History Allowance](history-gas.md)), MUST be taken from the reservoir first and only its excess from the regular budget, before the first frame starts.
  The excess taken from the regular budget is spent, as every part of a state or history charge that regular gas pays is (`SATIN-POOL-008`).

SATIN-POOL-007.text:
- `SATIN-POOL-007` A regular charge — every inherited opcode cost, static or dynamic, and every regular part of the intrinsic gas — MUST draw only the regular gas of the frame that makes it.
  A regular charge the frame's regular gas cannot pay is an out-of-gas of that frame.

SATIN-POOL-008.text:
- `SATIN-POOL-008` A state charge ([State Gas and SALT Pricing](state-gas.md)) and a history charge ([History Gas and the History Allowance](history-gas.md)) MUST draw the pools of the frame that makes it in this order: first the charge's legacy share, which only the state charges `SATIN-STATE-012` lists have — for a fresh slot, a new account or a created account, made by an opcode in any frame, a system call's included ([System Calls](../block/system-calls.md)), or by a keyless deployment's step 10 or 14 ([KeylessDeploy](../system-contracts/keyless-deploy.md)) — from the frame's regular gas; then the frame's reservoir, until it is zero; then the rest, the spill, from the frame's regular gas.
  A frame whose regular gas cannot pay the legacy share, or the spill, MUST run out of gas, whatever its reservoir holds.
  The part of a state or history charge that regular gas pays is spent, and no give-back credits it to regular gas again (`SATIN-HIST-012`).

SATIN-POOL-009.text: - `SATIN-POOL-009` `GAS` MUST push the regular gas the frame has left, and MUST NOT include the reservoir.

SATIN-POOL-010.text: - `SATIN-POOL-010` The transaction's own frame MUST receive the whole reservoir left once the intrinsic state gas and the charges made before the first frame are paid, and a system call's outermost frame MUST receive the whole reservoir of the system call ([System Calls and the Pre-Block Sequence](../block/system-calls.md)).

SATIN-POOL-011.text:
