- `SATIN-POOL-011` A child frame started by `CALL`, `CALLCODE`, `DELEGATECALL`, `STATICCALL`, `CREATE` or `CREATE2`, and the creation a keyless deployment starts ([KeylessDeploy](../system-contracts/keyless-deploy.md)), MUST receive

  `reservoir_share = remaining − remaining × GAS_RETAINED_NUMERATOR / GAS_RETAINED_DENOMINATOR`

  - `remaining` — the reservoir the caller has left after every charge the caller makes for that start, the history of the start's records included ([History Gas and the History Allowance](history-gas.md)).
  - The division is integer division, truncating toward zero.

  The caller MUST keep `remaining − reservoir_share`.
  The regular gas the caller asks to forward MUST NOT bound `reservoir_share`: a start that forwards no regular gas still receives the share ([Gas Forwarding](gas-forwarding.md)).

SATIN-POOL-012.text:
- `SATIN-POOL-012` When a start returns — whether it was answered without building a frame (a precompile, a call to an account with no code, an interceptor's answer, a refused start) or a built frame returned — the reservoir the child returns MUST join the reservoir the caller kept at the start, `remaining − reservoir_share` (`SATIN-POOL-011`), and the caller's regular gas MUST rise by the regular gas the child returns and by nothing else: the child's unused regular gas after a success, a revert, a stop or a refusal, and none after an exceptional halt.
  The child's regular gas is that of `SATIN-FWD-003`, a value call's `CALL_STIPEND` included: a refused start uses none of it and MUST return all of it, as an interceptor's answer that charges nothing does (`SATIN-HIST-023`).
  The returned reservoir — the reservoir the child holds when it returns, after its own rollback when it failed (`SATIN-POOL-014`) — MUST NOT be credited to the caller's regular gas.
  A caller with 100 reservoir after the start's charges keeps 2 and gives the child 98; a child that returns all 98 leaves the caller 100, whatever regular gas the caller paid for state before.

SATIN-POOL-013.text: - `SATIN-POOL-013` Retired: removed. A child's state and history charges are no longer tracked by the pool that paid them, and a returned reservoir joins its caller's without crediting regular gas (`SATIN-POOL-012`).

SATIN-POOL-014.text:
- `SATIN-POOL-014` When a frame reverts, or is stopped by a limit, the state and history charges it made, and those its successful children merged into it, net of the give-backs it and they received (`SATIN-HIST-007`), MUST be given back into its own reservoir by this formula, which is the one definition of a frame's reservoir after a revert or a stop:

  `reservoir = reservoir + net_charged`

  - `reservoir` (right-hand side) — the frame's reservoir when it fails: what it kept of the reservoir it received and of what its successful children returned, every give-back it holds, and the reservoir its failed children returned after their own rollback.
  - `net_charged` — the state and history gas charged since the frame started, by the frame and by the children that succeeded and merged into it, legacy shares included, less every give-back they received; it is negative for a frame that took back more than it charged; a failed child's charges are not part of it, that child's rollback having already returned them.

  Every state and history charge the revert undoes therefore ends in the frame's reservoir, whichever pool paid it, the reservoir a failed child returned stays there, and the frame's unspent regular gas, which none of it reaches, returns to its caller (`SATIN-POOL-012`).
  When a frame halts exceptionally, its reservoir MUST become the reservoir it received when it started, and its regular gas, with the part of its charges regular gas paid, is consumed; reservoir its failed children returned to it is consumed with it.
  A failed frame's charges therefore never return to regular gas.

SATIN-POOL-015.text:
- `SATIN-POOL-015` When a start for which the caller charged an account leaf's state gas — a value `CALL` to an account that is empty under EIP-161, or a `CREATE` or `CREATE2` onto an address empty under EIP-161 — returns without that leaf added, because the child failed, because a limit stopped the start (an answer replaced by the stop included), or, for a `CALL`, because the start did not happen after the charge (`SATIN-HIST-023`), a value the caller cannot fund among the reasons, the caller MUST be given that charge back, its legacy share included, into its reservoir, after the reservoir the child returns joined it (`SATIN-POOL-012`, [History Gas and the History Allowance](history-gas.md)).
  The new-account or created-account state gas charged for the transaction's own frame before it starts (`SATIN-SCHED-008` step 4) MUST likewise be given back into the transaction's reservoir, after that frame's rollback, when that frame reverts or is stopped.
  When that frame halts, the part of that charge the reservoir paid MUST return to the transaction's reservoir, and the part regular gas paid MUST be consumed with the frame's regular gas: nothing of it returns to the sender at the settlement.

SATIN-POOL-016.text: - `SATIN-POOL-016` Retired: replaced by `SATIN-POOL-024`. Charges made before the first frame are no longer unwound by the reservoir the first frame returns.

SATIN-POOL-017.text:
- `SATIN-POOL-017` When a transaction ends, the reservoir left MUST return to the sender, and so MUST the unspent regular gas unless the transaction's own frame halted; this holds when the transaction's own frame reverted and when it was stopped by a limit ([Limit Stops](limit-stops.md)).
  A failed deposit is the exception: it uses its whole gas limit, the reservoir included, and nothing returns ([Deposit Transactions](../block/deposits.md)).

SATIN-POOL-018.text:
- `SATIN-POOL-018` The receipt's gas used MUST be what the transaction spent from both pools — regular, state and history gas together — after the inherited EIP-3529 refund and the floor rule of `SATIN-POOL-020`.
  When that spend less the refund is below the floor, the gas used MUST be the floor and no refund MUST be made: the sender is returned its gas limit less the floor, the floor's excess over the spend being drawn from the unspent regular gas and the reservoir alike.

SATIN-POOL-019.text:
- `SATIN-POOL-019` A node MUST split a transaction's gas used into three ledgers, all paid from the two pools:

  | Ledger      | Value                                                     |
  | ----------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
  | Regular gas | `total − state − history`                                 |
  | State gas   | The state charges the transaction kept                    |
  | History gas | The history charges the transaction kept, its body's included |

  - `total` — what the transaction spent from both pools, the intrinsic gas included, before the EIP-3529 refund and before the floor of `SATIN-POOL-020`; it is not the receipt's gas used of `SATIN-POOL-018`, which is that spend less the refund and at least the floor.
  - `state`, `history` — the state and history charges kept, net of every give-back.

  The EIP-3529 refund MUST NOT lower any ledger, and the floor MUST NOT raise one: the receipt's gas used and the three ledgers are separate figures.
  State or history gas that regular gas paid, a legacy share or a spill, MUST stay on its own ledger.
  The ledgers of a failed deposit are specified on [Deposit Transactions](../block/deposits.md).

SATIN-POOL-020.text:
- `SATIN-POOL-020` The EIP-7623 floor, as EIP-7976 and EIP-7981 amend it, MUST be computed and validated as the Amsterdam schedule computes it, from the base and per-byte costs of [Gas Schedule and Intrinsic Gas](gas-schedule.md).
  The figure a block counts on its execution ledger for a transaction MUST be `max(regular, floor)`, with `regular` the transaction's regular-gas ledger, from which history gas is taken out before the floor applies ([Block Limits and Packing](../block/block-limits.md)).
  The floor MUST be that of EIP-7623 as of [commit `451cd9e1ec`](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/commit/451cd9e1ecb30b19be1c02199760a70d6248e604) (15 May 2025), amended by EIP-7976 and EIP-7981 at the commits of `SATIN-SCHED-001`.

SATIN-POOL-021.text:
- `SATIN-POOL-021` A node MUST NOT keep a separate compute-gas limit or ledger.
  Computation is paid in regular gas, bounded by the execution cap and, once a transaction read volatile data, by [gas detention](gas-detention.md).

SATIN-POOL-024.text:
- `SATIN-POOL-024` A state or history charge made before the first frame — the caller a deposit creates, an authorization's charges ([EIP-7702 Authorizations Before the First Frame](authorizations.md)), the history of the records made outside a frame, the state gas of the first frame's recipient or created account ([Gas Schedule and Intrinsic Gas](gas-schedule.md)) — has no legacy share: it MUST draw the reservoir first and the regular budget for the rest, and the first frame receives the reservoir it left (`SATIN-POOL-010`).
  The part the regular budget pays MUST NOT be credited back to regular gas, and a halt of the first frame consumes it.
  The first frame's rollback MUST NOT return such a charge: it is not part of that frame's `net_charged` (`SATIN-POOL-014`); each such charge is kept or given back by its own rule — the authorities' charges kept (`SATIN-AUTH-016`), the first frame's start record (`SATIN-HIST-005`) and its recipient's or created account's state gas (`SATIN-POOL-015`) given back on a revert or a stop, and on a halt only for the part the reservoir paid.

SATIN-REG-002.text:
- `SATIN-REG-002` Once per block, after every other pre-block step (see [System Calls and the Pre-Block Sequence](../block/system-calls.md)), the node MUST resolve the block's live system address from the registry: it loads the registry's account and slot 0 (`_currentSystemAddress`) from the state those steps left, compares the account's code hash with `SEQUENCER_REGISTRY_CODE_HASH`, and takes the address the slot holds.
  The read MUST compare the code hash and MUST NOT load or run the registry's code; it is not charged, writes nothing, and is committed as a read-only state of the pre-block phase, after the other steps (see [The Stateless Witness](../block/stateless-witness.md)).
  Every transaction of the block MUST be classified against that address; no transaction reads the registry, or finds its account or slot warm, for its classification.

SATIN-REG-003.text: - `SATIN-REG-003` Retired, removed: no transaction reads the registry, or finds its account or slot warm, for its classification; the block resolves the live system address once (`SATIN-REG-002`).

SATIN-REG-004.text: - `SATIN-REG-004` A registry that is absent, holds other code, or whose slot 0 is zero when the block resolves the live system address MUST make the block invalid.

SATIN-REG-005.text:
- `SATIN-REG-005` A role change takes effect only in a later block than the one that scheduled it, and only through that block's pre-block call to `applyPendingChanges()` (see [System Calls and the Pre-Block Sequence](../block/system-calls.md)).
  So every transaction of a block is classified against the address the block resolved after its pre-block steps (`SATIN-REG-002`), and a call to `applyPendingChanges()` inside a block finds no change due that the pre-block step did not apply.

SATIN-REG-006.text: - `SATIN-REG-006` The registry's roles MUST be what its storage holds: a node writes them only when it deploys the registry new (`SATIN-REG-008`), from the bootstrap values of the chain configuration (`SATIN-REG-009`), and MUST NOT otherwise seed, overwrite or derive them.

SATIN-REG-007.text: - `SATIN-REG-007` A registry read the node fails to make — in the resolution, in the due-change read of the pre-block sequence, or in the registry's deployment — MUST be reported as an internal error of the node, never as an invalid block or as a result of a transaction (see [System Calls and the Pre-Block Sequence](../block/system-calls.md)).

SATIN-REG-009.text:
- `SATIN-REG-009` A chain configuration that schedules Satin MUST carry the registry's bootstrap values, under the keys the Rex era introduced: `rex5InitialSequencer` and `rex5InitialAdmin`, each a non-zero address, and `rex6MinRotationDelay`, a non-zero number of blocks.
  A node MUST refuse a configuration that lacks one of them or gives one as zero.
  The values are read only by the deployment of `SATIN-REG-008`, every block; once the registry holds its roles, its storage, not the configuration, decides them.

SATIN-SCHED-001.text:
- `SATIN-SCHED-001` The gas schedule MUST be Amsterdam's — including [EIP-8038](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8038)'s state-access prices, [EIP-2780](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-2780)'s decomposition of the intrinsic cost, [EIP-7976](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7976)'s calldata floor and [EIP-7981](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7981)'s access-list floor — with exactly three changes:
  - the EIP-8037 state-gas entries MUST be rebuilt at `COST_PER_STATE_BYTE` ([State Gas and SALT Pricing](state-gas.md));
  - the history gas of deposited code MUST be `COST_PER_HISTORY_BYTE` per byte ([History Gas and the History Allowance](history-gas.md)), where Amsterdam prices it at zero;
  - the forwarding reduction of a call or a creation MUST be the 98/100 cap of [Gas Forwarding](gas-forwarding.md) (`SATIN-FWD-001`), where Amsterdam keeps EIP-150's 63/64: a caller keeps `remaining × 2 / 100` of its regular gas instead of `remaining / 64`, so 1,000 regular gas forwards 980, not 985.

  Every other entry MUST be Amsterdam's: every regular-gas entry, the regular code-deposit cost, the EIP-7702 entries, and the entries Amsterdam introduced for EIP-8037, EIP-2780, EIP-7976 and EIP-7981.
  The regular gas of creating state is therefore the access and the write EIP-8038 prices, and the new state itself is paid in state gas alone.
  A node MUST apply EIP-8038 as of [commit `4c7e2487e4`](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/commit/4c7e2487e4da3131bcadc7399f8b153f5344c0b7) (18 September 2026), EIP-2780 as of [commit `7243c92ba8`](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/commit/7243c92ba812437c64bae9fc6524ee269b29daa9) (4 September 2026), EIP-7976 as of [commit `c998ef94eb`](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/commit/c998ef94eb16a6af8a9b8e2084f947b17ea14865) (7 July 2026) and EIP-7981 as of [commit `747b78c0ed`](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/commit/747b78c0edfdf04e9e2933ad1bec592d3318e1d9) (7 July 2026), each the revision current when the EIP-8037 profile was frozen (`SATIN-POOL-004`); every value of them a transaction's outcome depends on is restated on this page, so the pins are their provenance.

SATIN-SCHED-002.text: - `SATIN-SCHED-002` The static gas every opcode pays before its dynamic cost MUST be Amsterdam's: `EXTCODESIZE` and `EXTCODECOPY` pay `WARM_STORAGE_READ_COST` twice, one access for the account and one for its code, and every other opcode's static gas is the same in Osaka and Amsterdam.

SATIN-SCHED-003.text:
- `SATIN-SCHED-003` The regular-gas, state-gas and history-gas entries below MUST have the values in the Value column; each differs from Osaka, or is one EIP-8038 restates at its Osaka value:

  | ---------------------------------------------------- | ------ | ------- |

  | `SSTORE` of a fresh slot, before the load cost       | 19,900 | 10,000  |
  | `SSTORE` reset, before the cold load                 | 2,800  | 10,000  |
  | `SSTORE` refund of a restored fresh slot             | 19,900 | 10,000  |
  | `SSTORE` refund of a restored reset                  | 2,800  | 10,000  |
  | `SSTORE` refund of a cleared slot                    | 4,800  | 11,616  |
  | `CREATE` and `CREATE2`                               | 32,000 | 12,000  |
  | `EXTCODESIZE` and `EXTCODECOPY`, static gas          | 100    | 200     |
  | Creation transaction (unused under EIP-2780)         | 32,000 | 12,000  |
  | Access-list address, with its 20 bytes at 64 gas     | 2,400  | 4,180   |
  | Access-list storage key, with its 32 bytes at 64 gas | 1,900  | 4,048   |
  | Code deposit, regular gas per byte                   | 200    | 0       |
  | Code deposit, state gas per byte                     | 0      | 1,530   |
  | Code deposit, history gas per byte                   | 0      | 88      |
  | Fresh-slot `SSTORE`, state gas                       | 0      | 97,920  |
  | New account, state gas                               | 0      | 183,600 |
  | Created account, state gas                           | 0      | 183,600 |
  | EIP-7702 delegation indicator, state gas             | 0      | 35,190  |
  | EIP-7702 authorization, intrinsic regular gas        | 25,000 | 7,816   |
  | EIP-7702 refund for an existing authority            | 12,500 | 0       |
  | Account write (EIP-2780)                             | 0      | 9,000   |

  The state-gas entries are the price at `m = 1`; a state charge is scaled by its bucket's multiplier ([State Gas and SALT Pricing](state-gas.md)).
  An opcode whose static gas is the warm read pays the additional cold account access for an account that is not warm; `SELFDESTRUCT`'s static gas holds no warm read, so a beneficiary that is not warm costs it the whole `COLD_ACCOUNT_ACCESS`, as EIP-2929 charges it.

SATIN-SCHED-004.text:
- `SATIN-SCHED-004` A cold `SSTORE` MUST pay `COLD_STORAGE_ACCESS` (2,100) for its access, its static cost included, as a cold `SLOAD` does: EIP-8038 folds the warm base into a cold slot's access.
  The static cost, `WARM_STORAGE_READ_COST`, MUST be a charge of its own, made before the slot is loaded; the rest of the access, `COLD_STORAGE_ACCESS − WARM_STORAGE_READ_COST`, MUST be charged after the load, in one charge with the cost of the write, so gas detention holds the two charges to the spendable part one after the other (`SATIN-DET-018`).

SATIN-SCHED-005.section: Specification > Intrinsic regular gas and the floor
SATIN-SCHED-005.text:
- `SATIN-SCHED-005` The floor's base MUST be the transaction's own decomposed base of `SATIN-SCHED-006` without its calldata, access-list, authorization and initcode costs: `TX_BASE_COST` for a transaction to its sender, `TX_BASE_COST + COLD_ACCOUNT_ACCESS` for a call to another account without value, `TX_BASE_COST + COLD_ACCOUNT_ACCESS + TX_VALUE_COST` for one with value, and `TX_BASE_COST + CREATE_ACCESS` for a creation.
  The floor MUST be that base plus `TOTAL_COST_FLOOR_PER_TOKEN × FLOOR_TOKENS_PER_BYTE` gas for every calldata byte, zero or non-zero, a creation's initcode included, and the same for every access-list byte, `ACCESS_LIST_ADDRESS_SIZE` bytes for an address and `ACCESS_LIST_SLOT_SIZE` for a storage key.
  How the floor sets the gas used is `SATIN-POOL-018` and `SATIN-POOL-020` ([Two-Pool Gas](gas-model.md)); how validation holds the gas limit to it is on [Transaction Validation and Refusals](../block/transaction-validation.md).

SATIN-SCHED-006.section: Specification > Intrinsic regular gas and the floor
SATIN-SCHED-006.text:
- `SATIN-SCHED-006` The intrinsic regular gas of a transaction MUST be `TX_BASE_COST`, plus, for a call to an account other than the sender, `COLD_ACCOUNT_ACCESS` for the recipient's access and `TX_VALUE_COST` more when it carries value; plus, for a creation, `CREATE_ACCESS` and EIP-3860's initcode cost; plus the calldata cost, the access-list entries of `SATIN-SCHED-003`, and `PER_AUTH_BASE_COST` per authorization entry.
  A transaction to its own sender MUST pay `TX_BASE_COST` alone for its base, with or without value.

SATIN-SCHED-007.section: Specification > Intrinsic regular gas and the floor
SATIN-SCHED-007.text: - `SATIN-SCHED-007` The `PER_AUTH_BASE_COST` of every authorization entry MUST be charged by the transaction's validation, as every intrinsic entry is, whether or not the authorization will apply; an authority that already exists MUST be refunded nothing when its authorization is applied.

SATIN-SCHED-008.section: Specification > Charges made at the start of execution

SATIN-SCHED-009.section: Specification > Charges made at the start of execution
SATIN-SCHED-009.text:
- `SATIN-SCHED-009` A transaction that cannot pay a charge of `SATIN-SCHED-008` — the account a deposit creates for its caller, an authorization's charges, the history of the records made outside a frame, the charge for the first frame's start, or a delegated recipient's delegate access — MUST run out of gas without running a frame.
  An authorization list the KV or state-growth limit skips is charged nothing ([EIP-7702 Authorizations Before the First Frame](authorizations.md)), and this path does not apply to it.

SATIN-SCHED-010.section: Specification > Charges made at the start of execution
SATIN-SCHED-010.text:
- `SATIN-SCHED-010` On that path everything applied before the first frame MUST be taken back, except what validation did to the sender's account (its fee and a call's nonce bump) and the account a deposit created for its caller: the applied EIP-7702 authorizations with their nonce and delegation writes, the sender's own authorization included, their state gas and their write records.
  The intrinsic gas and the body's history gas MUST stay charged, the rest of the regular budget MUST be consumed, and the reservoir left MUST return to the sender; the sender of a creation keeps the nonce bump the creation would have made.
  A deposit that runs out of gas this way is a failed deposit instead, which uses its whole gas limit, the reservoir included ([Deposit Transactions](../block/deposits.md)).

SATIN-SCHED-011.text:
- `SATIN-SCHED-011` Once a creation's returned code passed its checks ([Contract Size Limits](contract-limits.md)), deposited code MUST be charged in this order: the regular code-deposit cost per byte (zero), the hashing cost of the code at `KECCAK256_WORD_COST` per 32-byte word, the code's state gas (`SATIN-STATE-003`), and its history gas (`SATIN-HIST-002`).
  A creation that cannot pay any of the four MUST run out of gas, and no code is deposited.
  The data size of the code is counted after every deposit charge is made and before the creation commits ([Resource Accounting](resource-accounting.md)).

SATIN-SCHED-012.section: Specification > Addresses warm from the start
SATIN-SCHED-012.text: - `SATIN-SCHED-012` The addresses EIP-2929 and EIP-3651 make warm from the start of a transaction — the precompiles, the block beneficiary, and the addresses the transaction's access list names, those listed without storage keys included — MUST be charged as warm on every access, their first `CALL`-family access and their first access as a `SELFDESTRUCT` beneficiary included.

SATIN-SCHED-013.text: - `SATIN-SCHED-013` Retired, removed: no transaction finds the SequencerRegistry's account or slot 0 warm from its start; the block resolves the live system address once, outside every transaction ([SequencerRegistry](../system-contracts/sequencer-registry.md), `SATIN-REG-002`).

SATIN-SCHED-014.section: Specification > Addresses warm from the start
SATIN-SCHED-014.text: - `SATIN-SCHED-014` The sender, and the recipient of a call, MUST be warm from the start of the transaction, as EIP-2929 has them.

SATIN-SD-001.section: Specification > EIP-6780 and the first effective destruction
SATIN-SD-001.text: - `SATIN-SD-001` `SELFDESTRUCT` MUST follow [EIP-6780](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-6780): it moves the account's balance to its beneficiary, and it deletes the account only when the account was created in the same transaction.

SATIN-SD-002.section: Specification > EIP-6780 and the first effective destruction
SATIN-SD-002.text: - `SATIN-SD-002` The first effective `SELFDESTRUCT` of an account created in the same transaction MUST apply the table of `SATIN-SD-004` to every part of that account — its leaf, its deployed code and each of its slots — by the part's value at the transaction's start and its value before the destruction, and MUST mark the account as destroyed.

SATIN-SD-003.section: Specification > EIP-6780 and the first effective destruction
SATIN-SD-003.text:
- `SATIN-SD-003` A slot's value at the transaction's start MUST be its original value in the transaction, the value it held when the transaction first accessed it.
  A slot of the created account that the transaction first accesses after the creation reads zero, whatever the state held there, and so has an original of zero; a slot the transaction accessed before the creation keeps the value it held then as its original.

SATIN-SD-004.text:
- `SATIN-SD-004` The destruction MUST apply, to each part, the effect of its row:

  | Part          | At the transaction's start | Before   | Effect                                                                                                                                                         |
  | ------------- | -------------------------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | Account leaf  | absent                     | present  | Refill the leaf's state gas; state growth −1; take the account's write record back                                                                            |
  | Account leaf  | present                    | present  | Nothing: the leaf existed before the transaction, and its write record stands                                                                                  |
  | Deployed code | absent                     | present  | Refill the code's state gas; take back its data size and its history gas                                                                                       |
  | Deployed code | absent                     | absent   | Nothing                                                                                                                                                        |
  | Deployed code | present                    | present  | Not reached: non-empty code at the start collides with the creation (`SATIN-SD-016`)                                                                           |
  | Slot          | zero                       | non-zero | Refill the slot's state gas; state growth −1; take the slot's write record back                                                                                |
  | Slot          | zero                       | zero     | Nothing: the slot is already clear                                                                                                                             |
  | Slot          | non-zero                   | any      | Nothing of the refill or the fall; the write record of a slot the transaction loaded stands, and the deletion makes it when that slot still holds its original value; a slot the transaction did not load has no record |

  Every part is deleted with the account.

SATIN-SD-005.text:
- `SATIN-SD-005` A refill MUST be the price that part was charged — its schedule entry times the bucket multiplier of that charge ([State Gas and SALT Pricing](state-gas.md)), its legacy share included — and MUST go into the reservoir of the destroying frame, also when another frame paid it (`SATIN-HIST-012`).
  On the absent-leaf row the leaf's charge is the one this transaction made for that leaf: at the value transfer that funded the address, at a `SELFDESTRUCT` that paid it, at the transaction's own value, or at the creation when the created address was empty.

SATIN-SD-006.text:
- `SATIN-SD-006` State growth MUST fall for the absent leaf and for each slot on the zero-then-non-zero row, and for nothing else in the table.
  The fall of the absent leaf stands also when the creation itself added no rise, as when the transaction funded the address and then created onto it.
  An address that held a balance before the transaction is on the present-leaf row: the creation adds no rise for that leaf, the destruction subtracts none, and the write record the nonce bump made stands.

SATIN-SD-007.text:
- `SATIN-SD-007` A write record the table takes back MUST return its data size to the destroying frame's budget and its history gas into the destroying frame's reservoir, and the KV count falls by that record.
  When the destroying frame is the transaction's own frame and that frame succeeds, this return is the record's history gas once, and the settlement MUST NOT give that charge back again (`SATIN-HIST-005`).

SATIN-SD-008.text: - `SATIN-SD-008` Deployed code is neither a write record nor a unit of state growth; code on the absent-then-present row MUST return its data size and its history gas as a record taken back does.

SATIN-SD-009.text:
- `SATIN-SD-009` The give-back MUST follow the give-back rule of `SATIN-HIST-012`, as a slot written back to zero does.
  It MUST be credited with the completed write, after every charge the opcode makes: a charge the frame cannot pay halts the opcode first, and the give-back is not credited.
  It MUST NOT raise the destroying frame's remaining in any dimension above the budget the frame was given (`SATIN-LIM-004`).

SATIN-SD-010.text:
- `SATIN-SD-010` When the destroying frame succeeds, the give-back is reservoir of that frame and returns up the chain with its reservoir (`SATIN-POOL-012`).
  When the destroying frame fails, or a frame containing it fails, the mark and every effect of the table MUST be discarded: the charges stand, or come back by the ordinary rule for that failure, and a record the table took back stands again; the discarded give-back is not a further one.

SATIN-SD-011.text: - `SATIN-SD-011` A later `SELFDESTRUCT` of the same account while the mark stands MUST apply the table for nothing: it subtracts nothing, refills nothing and takes nothing back.

SATIN-SD-012.section: Specification > EIP-6780 and the first effective destruction
SATIN-SD-012.text: - `SATIN-SD-012` A `SELFDESTRUCT` of an account that was not created in the transaction MUST NOT apply the destruction table and MUST NOT mark the account: it subtracts nothing, refills nothing and takes nothing back, and EIP-6780 does not delete the account.

SATIN-SD-013.text:
- `SATIN-SD-013` From the first effective destruction until the end of the transaction, while the mark stands, the account MUST add nothing further to state growth and keep no further state gas: an `SSTORE` of one of its slots neither rises nor falls and neither charges nor refills fresh-slot state gas, its regular gas being unchanged.
  The mark MUST NOT change what such an `SSTORE` does to the EIP-3529 refund counter: a store that clears the slot or restores its original value moves the counter by the inherited `SSTORE` rules, on the slot's original, present and new values, as it would without the mark (`SATIN-TAKE-003`).
  A write to the account or to one of its slots makes no record.

SATIN-SD-014.text: - `SATIN-SD-014` Code deposited after a constructor destroyed its own account, on the absent-then-absent row, MUST NOT be charged state gas; its data size and history gas MUST be charged as any deposited code's, and no later destruction takes them back.

SATIN-SD-015.text:
- `SATIN-SD-015` Value sent to the marked account MUST NOT be a rise and MUST make no write record.
  The account still exists until the transaction ends, and MUST then be removed with the balance it holds ([EIP-7708 Transfer Logs](transfer-logs.md)); its logs and the transfer log of the balance moved stay counted and charged.
  The removal MUST NOT take a record back again, and MUST NOT take the code's data size or history gas back again.

SATIN-SD-016.text:
- `SATIN-SD-016` A creation MUST collide when the created address holds non-empty code or a nonce other than zero, and MUST NOT collide on storage alone: [EIP-7610](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7610) is not applied.
  A creation can therefore land on an address with nonce zero, empty code and storage.
  A slot of such an address that the transaction first accesses once the account is created reads zero and is on a zero row; a slot the state held that the transaction never accessed makes no record when the account is destroyed; a slot the transaction accessed before the creation keeps the value it held, and the destruction deletes it with the account as an ordinary deletion, which makes its write record while it still holds that value.

SATIN-SD-017.text:
- `SATIN-SD-017` An account that is empty under EIP-161 while its leaf is in the state the transaction loaded — nonce zero, balance zero, empty code, storage that is not empty — MUST be the present-leaf row: the creation charges new-account state gas and counts a rise, the address being empty under EIP-161 (`SATIN-STATE-004`, `SATIN-STATE-011`, `SATIN-ACCT-014`), and the destruction MUST NOT refill that charge or subtract that rise.
  An address the state holds no account for is absent, never an empty account.

SATIN-SD-018.section: Specification > The beneficiary and the order of a destruction
SATIN-SD-018.text:
- `SATIN-SD-018` A `SELFDESTRUCT` that moves a non-zero balance to a distinct account empty under EIP-161 (`SATIN-STATE-011`) MUST be a rise of state growth and MUST be charged new-account state gas, with its legacy share ([State Gas and SALT Pricing](state-gas.md), `SATIN-STATE-012`), a repeated destruction included; a zero balance creates no account and is not a rise.
  That rise MUST be held to the limits only after the operation's give-back, which cannot cross a limit.
  A frame exactly at its state-growth budget that destroys an account created in the transaction, with N new slots, while moving a non-zero balance to a new beneficiary, subtracts `1 + N` when the leaf was absent at the transaction's start and N when it was present, before it adds the beneficiary.

SATIN-SD-019.section: Specification > The beneficiary and the order of a destruction

SATIN-SD-020.section: Specification > The beneficiary and the order of a destruction
SATIN-SD-020.text: - `SATIN-SD-020` A `SELFDESTRUCT`'s volatile reads of either end — the destroyed account or the beneficiary being the block beneficiary ([Gas Detention](gas-detention.md)) — MUST be marked only after its last step that can fail.

SATIN-SIZE-001.text: - `SATIN-SIZE-001` Deployed code MUST be at most `MAX_CONTRACT_SIZE` bytes.

SATIN-SIZE-002.text: - `SATIN-SIZE-002` Initcode MUST be at most `MAX_INITCODE_SIZE` bytes, twice `MAX_CONTRACT_SIZE`.

SATIN-SIZE-003.text:
- `SATIN-SIZE-003` These are Ethereum's size checks at MegaETH's sizes, not resource limits: initcode over `MAX_INITCODE_SIZE` MUST halt the creating frame at the creation opcode, and deployed code over `MAX_CONTRACT_SIZE` MUST halt the creation, each consuming the halting frame's regular gas.
  Neither is a limit stop ([Halts, Reverts and Stops](outcomes.md)).

SATIN-SIZE-004.text:
- `SATIN-SIZE-004` A creation transaction other than a deposit whose initcode is over `MAX_INITCODE_SIZE` MUST be rejected at validation ([Transaction Validation and Refusals](../block/transaction-validation.md)); a deposit is never rejected, and one that fails this check is a failed deposit ([Deposit Transactions](../block/deposits.md)).
  A keyless deployment's initcode over the limit is refused by its own rule ([KeylessDeploy](../system-contracts/keyless-deploy.md)).

SATIN-SIZE-006.text:
- `SATIN-SIZE-006` A creation in a static frame therefore MUST fail before its operands are read, and a `CREATE2` short of its salt MUST pay the initcode cost and the memory before it fails on the missing operand.
  The halt consumes the frame's gas either way, but under gas detention one of those charges can be the crossing, which stops the frame with a revert where the stack underflow would have halted it ([Gas Detention](gas-detention.md)).

SATIN-STATE-001.section: Specification > The price of a state charge
SATIN-STATE-001.text:
- `SATIN-STATE-001` Every EIP-8037 state charge MUST be `entry × m`:
  - `entry` — the schedule's state-gas entry ([Gas Schedule and Intrinsic Gas](gas-schedule.md)): EIP-8037's byte count of the state times `COST_PER_STATE_BYTE`.
  - `m` — the multiplier of the SALT bucket the state lands in (`SATIN-STATE-002`).

SATIN-STATE-002.section: Specification > The price of a state charge
SATIN-STATE-002.text:
- `SATIN-STATE-002` The multiplier of a bucket MUST be `m = floor(bucket_capacity / MIN_BUCKET_SIZE)`.
  - `bucket_capacity` — the capacity SALT holds for the bucket in the state the block executes on.

rows: Fresh storage slot (SSTORE, original and present zero, new non-zero)
SATIN-STATE-003.section: Specification > The price of a state charge
SATIN-STATE-003.text:
- `SATIN-STATE-003` The states a state charge prices, their byte counts, and the bucket each lands in MUST be:

  | State                                                                  | Bytes                          | `entry` at `m = 1` | Bucket                |
  | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------ | ------------------ | --------------------- |
  | Fresh storage slot (`SSTORE`, original and present zero, new non-zero) | `SLOT_STATE_BYTES` = 64        | 97,920             | The slot's            |
  | New account                                                            | `ACCOUNT_STATE_BYTES` = 120    | 183,600            | The account's         |
  | Created contract account                                               | `ACCOUNT_STATE_BYTES` = 120    | 183,600            | The created account's |
  | Deployed code, per byte                                                | `CODE_STATE_BYTES` = 1         | 1,530              | The created account's |
  | EIP-7702 delegation indicator                                          | `DELEGATION_STATE_BYTES` = 23  | 35,190             | The authority's       |

SATIN-STATE-005.section: Specification > The price of a state charge
SATIN-STATE-005.text: - `SATIN-STATE-005` `m` MUST scale state gas and nothing else: regular gas and history gas are never scaled.

SATIN-STATE-006.text: - `SATIN-STATE-006` A node MUST read a bucket's capacity at most once per transaction: every later state charge, and every give-back, in that bucket during the transaction MUST use the same `m`, so a give-back cancels its charge exactly.

SATIN-STATE-007.text:
- `SATIN-STATE-007` A bucket capacity below `MIN_BUCKET_SIZE`, or one the node cannot read, is a fault of the node, for a deposit as for any transaction: the transaction MUST NOT be priced at any multiplier and MUST NOT be settled, and the node MUST report an internal error.
  The transaction then has no outcome ([Halts, Reverts and Stops](outcomes.md)).

SATIN-STATE-008.text:
- `SATIN-STATE-008` The only `SSTORE` that charges fresh-slot state gas MUST be one whose original value in the transaction is zero, whose present value is zero, and whose new value is not zero.
  The only `SSTORE` that gives it back MUST be one whose original value is zero, whose present value is not zero, and whose new value is zero, unless the slot's account is marked for deletion ([SELFDESTRUCT and the Destruction Table](selfdestruct.md)); the give-back is the price the slot was charged, credited as `SATIN-HIST-007` and `SATIN-HIST-012` state ([History Gas and the History Allowance](history-gas.md)).
  Every other `SSTORE` transition MUST charge no fresh-slot state gas and give none back.
  These are the same transitions as the state-growth change of an `SSTORE` ([Resource Accounting](resource-accounting.md)).

SATIN-STATE-009.text:
- `SATIN-STATE-009` A system-originated transaction and a system call ([Mega System Transactions and the Protocol's Own Transactions](../system-contracts/system-tx.md)) MUST be priced at `m = 1` and MUST NOT read a bucket capacity.
  A deposit that is not system-originated MUST be priced by its buckets; deposits and system-originated transactions pay history gas as any transaction does ([History Gas and the History Allowance](history-gas.md)).

SATIN-STATE-010.section: Specification > The price of a state charge
SATIN-STATE-010.text: - `SATIN-STATE-010` The SALT bucket an account or a storage slot lands in MUST be the bucket [SALT](https://github.com/megaeth-labs/salt)'s own definition assigns to its key: the mapping from an account or a slot to its bucket is an input to this specification, as the bucket capacities are, and is not restated here.

SATIN-STATE-011.text:
- `SATIN-STATE-011` Every new-account and created-account charge of `SATIN-STATE-004`, and the state-growth rise that goes with it ([Resource Accounting](resource-accounting.md)), MUST be decided, when the charge is decided, by one of two predicates:
  - **existence**, for the authority of an applied EIP-7702 authorization alone: the authority is new when the state holds no account at its address; an account whose leaf the state holds is not new, an account empty under EIP-161 included ([EIP-7702 Authorizations Before the First Frame](authorizations.md));
  - **EIP-161 emptiness**, for every other site — a deposit's or Mega System Transaction's caller, a value call's recipient, a transaction's value recipient, a `SELFDESTRUCT`'s beneficiary, a created address and a keyless deployment's signer: the account is new when the state holds no account at the address, or the account it holds has nonce zero, zero balance and no code.

  At a site decided by emptiness, an account whose leaf is in the state but is empty under EIP-161 is charged and counted as an absent one.
  Apart from an authority's charge, the distinction between no account and an empty leaf is made only by the witness ([The Stateless Witness](../block/stateless-witness.md)) and by the destruction table ([SELFDESTRUCT and the Destruction Table](selfdestruct.md)).

rows: Created account, by CREATE or CREATE2, or a keyless deployment's creation (step 14)
New account, by a SELFDESTRUCT's beneficiary
New account, by a value CALL, or a keyless deployment's signer (step 10)
SATIN-STATE-012.text:
- `SATIN-STATE-012` A state charge an opcode or a keyless deployment makes for one of the following MUST take its legacy share from the frame's regular gas before the reservoir pays any of it, and the rest as every state charge is paid (`SATIN-POOL-008`):

  `legacy_share = min(state_charge, max(0, PRE_FORK_COST − execution_charge))`

  - `state_charge` — the state charge, `entry × m` (`SATIN-STATE-001`).
  - `PRE_FORK_COST` and `execution_charge` — by the component that creates the state:

  | State charge | `PRE_FORK_COST` | `execution_charge` |
  | ------------ | --------------- | ------------------ |
  | Fresh storage slot, by `SSTORE` | `PRE_FORK_SSTORE_SET_COST` | `SSTORE_WRITE_COST` |
  | New account, by a value `CALL`, or a keyless deployment's signer (step 10) | `PRE_FORK_NEW_ACCOUNT_COST` | 0 |
  | New account, by a `SELFDESTRUCT`'s beneficiary | `PRE_FORK_NEW_ACCOUNT_COST` | `SELFDESTRUCT_NEW_ACCOUNT_COST` |
  | Created account, by `CREATE` or `CREATE2`, or a keyless deployment's creation (step 14) | `PRE_FORK_CREATE_COST` | `CREATE_ACCESS` |

  `PRE_FORK_COST` is a fixed pre-Satin price: it MUST NOT be scaled by the bucket multiplier and does not move when the schedule's prices do; `execution_charge` is the regular cost the schedule gives the component that creates the state ([Gas Schedule and Intrinsic Gas](gas-schedule.md)): the fresh slot's write, nothing for a value call's new account, the "new account of `SELFDESTRUCT`" entry for a `SELFDESTRUCT`'s beneficiary, and the creation's access.
  Every other state charge MUST have a legacy share of zero: deployed code, a delegation indicator, and every charge made before the first frame — the caller a deposit creates, an authorization's, the transaction's recipient or created account (`SATIN-POOL-024`); a history charge has none.
  The legacy share is state gas: it is counted on the state ledger, given back with the rest of its charge, into a reservoir (`SATIN-HIST-012`), and a frame whose regular gas cannot pay it runs out of gas whatever its reservoir holds.
  For a value `CALL` the new-account charge, with its share, is made before the forward is computed (`SATIN-HIST-010`), so the share is not forwarded.

  With the schedule's current prices the shares are 10,000 for a fresh slot (20,000 − 10,000), 25,000 for a value call's or a keyless signer's new account (25,000 − 0), 16,000 for a `SELFDESTRUCT`'s new beneficiary (25,000 − 9,000) and 20,000 for a created account (32,000 − 12,000), at every multiplier: a cold fresh slot written with a reservoir takes 22,100 of regular gas (2,100 access, 10,000 write, 10,000 share) and the rest of its 97,920 × `m` from the reservoir; a `SELFDESTRUCT` that moves a non-zero balance to a warm beneficiary empty under EIP-161 takes 30,000 of regular gas (5,000, the 9,000 entry and the 16,000 share), the pre-Satin 5,000 + 25,000, and the rest of its 183,600 × `m` from the reservoir.

SATIN-STOP-001.text: - `SATIN-STOP-001` Every limit — the transaction's data-size, KV-update and state-growth limits ([Resource Limits](resource-limits.md)), a frame's budget in those dimensions, and gas detention's compute limit ([Gas Detention](gas-detention.md)) — MUST stop the frame that crosses it with a revert, and MUST NOT halt.

SATIN-STOP-002.text:
- `SATIN-STOP-002` A limit stop MUST exist in exactly four dimensions: data size (kind 0), KV updates (kind 1), compute under gas detention (kind 2) and state growth (kind 3).
  Nothing else is a limit stop; the endings that are not are listed on [Halts, Reverts and Stops](outcomes.md).

SATIN-STOP-003.text:
- `SATIN-STOP-003` The stop MUST apply only to a transaction that passes validation and pays every charge made before its first frame.
  A transaction that fails validation, or cannot pay a charge made before its first frame ([Gas Schedule and Intrinsic Gas](gas-schedule.md)), MUST report no stop: a non-deposit is rejected or runs out of gas, and a deposit becomes a failed deposit ([Deposit Transactions](../block/deposits.md)), whose body stays counted as data size.

SATIN-STOP-004.text:
- `SATIN-STOP-004` The frame that crosses a limit MUST revert with `MegaLimitExceeded(uint8 kind, uint64 limit)` as its output, ABI-encoded as a Solidity custom error.
  The write or the charge that crossed MUST NOT be kept or made, and every write and log the frame made MUST be reverted, as a `REVERT` reverts them.

SATIN-STOP-005.text: - `SATIN-STOP-005` Its caller MUST resume as after any revert: the call fails, its return data is the stop's revert data, and the frame's regular gas MUST return to the caller — for gas detention's limit, the gas it had before the charge that crossed — with its reservoir, after the rollback of `SATIN-POOL-014` ([Two-Pool Gas](gas-model.md)).

SATIN-STOP-006.text:
- `SATIN-STOP-006` What the frame counted MUST be discarded with it, so the caller resumes within every limit, with one exception.
  A failed frame's discard puts back what the frames above it kept when it started, a record of theirs it took back included, while an Oracle hint it admitted stays counted (`SATIN-STOP-012`); a hint sent into room such a take-back freed leaves the transaction over its data-size limit once the frame fails.
  The frame it returns into MUST then return the stop of the transaction's data-size limit before it runs another instruction, whether the frame below reverted, halted or was itself stopped.

SATIN-STOP-007.text: - `SATIN-STOP-007` Otherwise a caller that carries on MUST be held to what the transaction has left, and a write or a charge of its own that crosses a limit again MUST stop the caller's frame in turn.

SATIN-STOP-008.text: - `SATIN-STOP-008` A caller that catches the stop MUST run on as after any failed call, unless `SATIN-STOP-006` stops it as it resumes; a transaction whose frames catch every stop below its own frame MAY succeed, keeping what its frames did and nothing of a frame that was stopped.

SATIN-STOP-009.section: Specification > A stop of the transaction's own frame
SATIN-STOP-009.text:
- `SATIN-STOP-009` A stop of the transaction's own frame is the transaction's result, and the transaction MUST settle like an EIP-8037 revert: every write and log its frames made MUST be reverted, the value its first frame carried and that frame's write record included; the sender pays the intrinsic gas, the body's history gas, the charges of what it keeps from before the first frame (`SATIN-STOP-011`), and what ran; the unspent regular gas and the reservoir return to the sender (`SATIN-POOL-017`).
  The transaction MUST be included with a failed receipt, and its usage counts toward the block's counters ([Block Limits and Packing](../block/block-limits.md)).

SATIN-STOP-010.section: Specification > A stop of the transaction's own frame
SATIN-STOP-010.text: - `SATIN-STOP-010` A deposit whose own frame is stopped MUST settle as `SATIN-STOP-009` states, as a revert: it is not a failed deposit, which only a deposit that fails validation, cannot pay a charge made before its first frame, or whose own frame halts becomes ([Deposit Transactions](../block/deposits.md)).

SATIN-STOP-011.section: Specification > A stop of the transaction's own frame
SATIN-STOP-011.text:
- `SATIN-STOP-011` A stop of the transaction's own frame MUST NOT revert what was applied before the first frame, as a revert of the first frame does not:
  - the sender's nonce and the fees it pays; for a deposit, its mint and the caller account it created, with that account's state gas;
  - the EIP-7702 authorizations admitted before the first frame ([EIP-7702 Authorizations Before the First Frame](authorizations.md)): their authorities' nonce and delegation writes, their state gas, their write records, and the history gas those records cost.
    A list the list rule skipped was not admitted, and the stop keeps nothing of it.

SATIN-STOP-012.section: Specification > A stop of the transaction's own frame
SATIN-STOP-012.text:
- `SATIN-STOP-012` An Oracle hint a frame admitted is not the frames' state: it MUST stay counted as data size through any stop, whether its payload reached the oracle service or failed to decode.
  A hint that would itself cross the data-size limit MUST be neither forwarded nor counted, and its call is answered with the stop ([Oracle](../system-contracts/oracle.md)).

SATIN-STOP-013.section: Specification > Enforcement before a frame runs
SATIN-STOP-013.text: - `SATIN-STOP-013` A frame whose start crosses a limit (`SATIN-LIM-013`) MUST be stopped before it runs an instruction, and what its start moved MUST be reverted with it: the value, the transfer log, a created account.

SATIN-STOP-014.section: Specification > Enforcement before a frame runs
SATIN-STOP-014.text:
- `SATIN-STOP-014` A frame answered with a success without running — a call to an account with no code, a precompile that answers — whose start crosses MUST have its answer replaced by the stop, on the child's whole regular gas, untouched: the forward and, for a value call, the `CALL_STIPEND` (`SATIN-FWD-003`, `SATIN-POOL-012`).
  A frame answered with a failure kept nothing, and its answer MUST NOT be replaced by a stop: a precompile that fails consumes the gas forwarded to it, as without a limit.
  A precompile whose price crosses gas detention moves nothing, and MUST be held to the price alone: its result is the compute stop, whatever records its value transfer would have made (`SATIN-DET-022`).

SATIN-STOP-015.section: Specification > Enforcement before a frame runs
SATIN-STOP-015.text: - `SATIN-STOP-015` A stopped creation MUST keep its creator's nonce bump, and that write's record MUST be counted on the creator when the creation returns: the creator MUST be held to its limits with it before it runs on, and be stopped if it crosses one (`SATIN-LIM-008`).

SATIN-STOP-016.text: - `SATIN-STOP-016` Retired, removed: no transaction reaches it. The answers gas detention rewrites to the stop have moved nothing when they are rewritten: a precompile's is decided from its price before its value moves (`SATIN-DET-021`, `SATIN-DET-022`, `SATIN-STOP-014`), and an interceptor's is made before the frame start (`SATIN-DET-025`, `SATIN-ICPT-007`), so neither has anything of its start to revert.

SATIN-STOP-017.section: Specification > Enforcement before a frame runs
SATIN-STOP-017.text:
- `SATIN-STOP-017` A node MUST NOT stop a transaction for data size counted before its first frame: validation's data-size check (`SATIN-VAL-003` step 1, [Transaction Validation and Refusals](../block/transaction-validation.md)) leaves nothing counted there that crosses the limit.
  KV updates and state growth can cross before the first frame only on the authorization list, which is then skipped ([EIP-7702 Authorizations Before the First Frame](authorizations.md)).

SATIN-STOP-018.text:
- `SATIN-STOP-018` The stop's `kind` and `limit` MUST be:

  | `kind` | Dimension               | `limit`                                                                                            |
  | ------ | ----------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | 0      | Data size               | The frame budget crossed, or the transaction limit when no frame budget was crossed, in bytes     |
  | 1      | KV updates              | The frame budget crossed, or the transaction limit when no frame budget was crossed, in write records |
  | 2      | Compute (gas detention) | The compute limit of the binding read: the transaction's compute at that read plus the cap, in gas |
  | 3      | State growth            | The frame budget crossed, or the transaction limit when no frame budget was crossed, in new accounts and new slots |

  Kinds 0, 1 and 3 MUST name the frame budget when that budget is crossed, also when the transaction limit of the same dimension is crossed too, and the transaction limit otherwise, whether or not a frame budget applies to the operation (`SATIN-LIM-011`).

SATIN-STOP-019.text: - `SATIN-STOP-019` A stop MUST carry the kind discriminant `SATIN-STOP-018` gives its dimension, and a node MUST NOT produce any other kind value.

SATIN-STOP-020.text:
- `SATIN-STOP-020` Among the refusals the protocol makes, only a limit stop MUST carry `MegaLimitExceeded`, and every limit stop MUST carry it.
  A refusal the protocol makes that is not a limit stop MUST NOT carry it: a refused volatile read whose charges are not gas detention's crossing reverts with `VolatileDataAccessDisabled(uint8)` ([MegaAccessControl](../system-contracts/mega-access-control.md), `SATIN-OUT-008`), the system contracts' and a keyless deployment's refusals carry their own errors ([KeylessDeploy](../system-contracts/keyless-deploy.md)), a call the depth gate or its frame start refuses fails with empty return data (`SATIN-OUT-010`), and a halt has no return data.
  What a contract returns is not a refusal the protocol makes: a `REVERT` whose data are the bytes of `MegaLimitExceeded`, a caller re-raising a stop it caught included, is an ordinary revert and is not a limit stop (`SATIN-STOP-021`).

SATIN-STOP-021.text:
- `SATIN-STOP-021` The revert data alone MUST NOT be taken to identify a stop: a contract can revert with the same bytes, and so can a caller that re-raises the stop a frame below returned.
  The stop of a transaction is the crossing that produced the result of its own frame, and execution MUST report it: the transaction's data-size, KV or state-growth limit, gas detention's compute limit, or that frame's own budget in data size, KV or state growth; it MUST report none when that result is not the stop's revert, a stop a caller caught included.

SATIN-SYSC-001.text:
- `SATIN-SYSC-001` A node MUST treat the six contracts of the table below, at their addresses, as MegaETH's system contracts, and no other account.

| Contract                                                | Address                            | Page                                                                 |
| ------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Oracle                                                  | `ORACLE_CONTRACT_ADDRESS`          | [Oracle](oracle.md)                                                  |
| High-Precision Timestamp                                | `HIGH_PRECISION_TIMESTAMP_ADDRESS` | [High-Precision Timestamp](high-precision-timestamp.md)              |
| KeylessDeploy                                           | `KEYLESS_DEPLOY_ADDRESS`           | [KeylessDeploy](keyless-deploy.md)                                   |
| MegaAccessControl                                       | `MEGA_ACCESS_CONTROL_ADDRESS`      | [MegaAccessControl](mega-access-control.md)                          |
| MegaLimitControl                                        | `MEGA_LIMIT_CONTROL_ADDRESS`       | [MegaLimitControl](mega-limit-control.md)                            |
| SequencerRegistry                                       | `SEQUENCER_REGISTRY_ADDRESS`       | [SequencerRegistry](sequencer-registry.md)                           |

SATIN-SYSC-002.text:
- `SATIN-SYSC-002` Each system contract's address MUST hold the code whose Keccak-256 code hash the table below names; that code hash is the normative identity of the contract's bytecode, and the bytecode defines every method a node does not intercept.
  The interface each contract page states is the ABI of that bytecode.
  The interface of KeylessDeploy no longer declares four errors (see [KeylessDeploy](keyless-deploy.md)); its bytecode is the one named below, which produces none of them.

| Contract                 | Version | Code hash                                                            |
| ------------------------ | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Oracle                   | 2.0.0   | `ORACLE_CODE_HASH`                                                   |
| High-Precision Timestamp | N/A     | `HIGH_PRECISION_TIMESTAMP_CODE_HASH`                                 |
| KeylessDeploy            | 1.0.0   | `KEYLESS_DEPLOY_CODE_HASH`                                           |
| MegaAccessControl        | 1.0.0   | `MEGA_ACCESS_CONTROL_CODE_HASH`                                      |
| MegaLimitControl         | 1.0.0   | `MEGA_LIMIT_CONTROL_CODE_HASH`                                       |
| SequencerRegistry        | 2.0.0   | `SEQUENCER_REGISTRY_CODE_HASH`                                       |

SATIN-SYSC-003.text:
- `SATIN-SYSC-003` Every block MUST deploy the system contracts before its first transaction, as steps of its pre-block sequence (see [System Calls and the Pre-Block Sequence](../block/system-calls.md)), on the state the earlier steps left:
  - the Oracle, the High-Precision Timestamp, KeylessDeploy, MegaAccessControl and MegaLimitControl, in that order, each by the same rule: an address with no account MUST be given an account holding the contract's code; an account whose code hash is not the one the table above names MUST have its code replaced by the contract's, its nonce, balance and storage kept; an account whose code hash is the table's MUST be left as it is;
  - then the SequencerRegistry, which holds roles and histories and so is deployed by its own rule: seeded when it is new, migrated in place from its earlier version, and never overwritten when it holds other code (see [SequencerRegistry](sequencer-registry.md), `SATIN-REG-008`).

  A deployment is charged nothing, counts toward none of the block's counters, and writes nothing but the account and the code it installs (and, for the registry, the slots `SATIN-REG-008` names); an account it leaves as it is MUST still be read, and recorded as a read-only entry of the step's state (see [The Stateless Witness](../block/stateless-witness.md)).
  No block installs code at a system-contract address, or writes a system contract's storage, other than by these steps, by the execution of its transactions and by its pre-block calls.

SATIN-SYSC-004.text:
- `SATIN-SYSC-004` A system contract MUST be executed as an account with code and storage, never as a precompile: it is read and written by `SLOAD`, `SSTORE`, `BALANCE` and every other account access as any account is, and a call to it runs its bytecode.
  The one exception is a call the node intercepts: a call to an intercepted method of a system contract is answered by the node, before a frame is built, as [Call Interception](interception.md) specifies, and every other call runs the contract's bytecode.
  A `keylessDeploy` call that is a transaction's own frame is a native creation rather than an interception (see [KeylessDeploy](keyless-deploy.md)).

SATIN-TAKE-001.section: Specification > The ledgers and the frame credited

SATIN-TAKE-002.section: Specification > The ledgers and the frame credited
SATIN-TAKE-002.text:
- `SATIN-TAKE-002` A give-back of state gas or history gas MUST credit a reservoir, as `SATIN-HIST-012` states, and the reservoir is that of the frame that makes it (`SATIN-HIST-007`): the frame running the opcode that takes the record or the state back, or the caller of a start when that start returns.
  The destruction table's give-back goes into the destroying frame's reservoir (`SATIN-SD-005`, `SATIN-SD-007`); the rollback of a failed frame gives the failed frame's own charges back into that frame's reservoir (`SATIN-POOL-014`); and a give-back made once the transaction's own frame has returned — the first frame's start record (`SATIN-HIST-005`), the state gas charged for its recipient or created account (`SATIN-POOL-015`) — is made by the settlement, into the transaction's reservoir.

SATIN-TAKE-003.section: Specification > The ledgers and the frame credited
SATIN-TAKE-003.text: - `SATIN-TAKE-003` A give-back of state or history gas is not an EIP-3529 refund (`SATIN-HIST-012`): the refund counter MUST change only by the inherited `SSTORE` rules, a frame's changes to it merging into its caller's when it succeeds and being discarded when it fails.

SATIN-TAKE-004.section: Specification > The ledgers and the frame credited
SATIN-TAKE-004.text:
- `SATIN-TAKE-004` Every count a frame makes, a fall and a take-back included, MUST be on that frame's own net: it merges into the caller's net when the frame succeeds and is discarded when it fails, and a record the failed frame took back stands again (`SATIN-ACCT-011`, `SATIN-LIM-006`).
  A count made outside every frame — the body, the applied authorities' records, the caller a deposit creates, an admitted Oracle hint — is on the transaction's net and is not discarded by a frame's failure (`SATIN-LIM-005`).
  The rollback of a failed frame MUST undo the give-backs the frame received together with the charges it made, as `SATIN-POOL-014` defines it: on a revert or a stop, `reservoir = reservoir + net_charged`, the reservoir it holds when it fails — a failed child's returned reservoir included — plus the net of its and its successful children's state and history charges, and its regular gas is what it has left, none of those charges returning to it; on an exceptional halt, its reservoir becomes the reservoir it received and its regular gas is consumed.

rows: ancestor: a write a descendant made and merged by succeeding, taken back by an ancestor (SATIN-HIST-007)

descendant: a write a frame made that another frame running on the same storage takes back — a descendant by DELEGATECALL, CALLCODE or a call back into the writing contract, or a frame started on that storage after the writer returned successfully (SATIN-HIST-007, SATIN-TAKE-002)
no-op: an SSTORE that writes the slot's present value, p → p, in any pattern (SATIN-ACCT-016)
refused: a write whose record crosses a limit (SATIN-HIST-013, SATIN-STOP-004)
rolled-back: a write discarded by the revert or halt of the writing frame or of a frame containing it (SATIN-POOL-014, SATIN-ACCT-011)
SATIN-TAKE-005.text:
- `SATIN-TAKE-005` A storage slot written by `SSTORE` and taken back MUST be accounted as this table states, for a slot of an account that is not marked for deletion (a marked account's slot is the marked row of `SATIN-TAKE-007`), each `SSTORE` in the order: the `SSTORE` minimum-gas check, the regular charge with the refund counter's change and the fresh-slot state charge or refill, then the limits on the record in the order data size, KV updates, state growth (`SATIN-LIM-010`), then the history give-back of a record taken back, then the history charge of a record made (`SATIN-HIST-006`, `SATIN-HIST-013`):

| Pattern | Regular gas and EIP-3529 refund | State gas | History gas | State growth | KV updates | Data size | Frame credited | Order |
| ------- | ------------------------------- | --------- | ----------- | ------------ | ---------- | --------- | -------------- | ----- |
| no-op: an `SSTORE` that writes the slot's present value, `p → p`, in any pattern (`SATIN-ACCT-016`) | `WARM_STORAGE_READ_COST`; the refund counter does not change | None | None | None | None | None | No give-back | The regular charge alone |
| zero-back: `0 → x → 0` (`SATIN-STATE-008`, `SATIN-ACCT-004`, `SATIN-ACCT-016`) | First write `WARM_STORAGE_READ_COST + SSTORE_WRITE_COST`; second `WARM_STORAGE_READ_COST` and refund `+SSTORE_RESTORE_REFUND` | `+SLOT_STATE_GAS × m` — its legacy share from regular gas, the rest from the reservoir first — then the refill `−SLOT_STATE_GAS × m`, into the reservoir | `+RECORD_HISTORY_GAS`, then `−RECORD_HISTORY_GAS` | +1, then −1 | +1, then −1 | `+WRITE_RECORD_SIZE`, then `−WRITE_RECORD_SIZE` | The frame running the second `SSTORE`, into its reservoir | Second `SSTORE`: its regular charge, refund and refill, then the limits, then the history give-back |
| restore: `x → y → x` (`SATIN-ACCT-004`, `SATIN-ACCT-016`) | First `WARM_STORAGE_READ_COST + SSTORE_WRITE_COST`; second `WARM_STORAGE_READ_COST` and refund `+SSTORE_RESTORE_REFUND` | None | `+RECORD_HISTORY_GAS`, then `−RECORD_HISTORY_GAS` | None | +1, then −1 | `+WRITE_RECORD_SIZE`, then `−WRITE_RECORD_SIZE` | The frame running the second `SSTORE`, into its reservoir | Second `SSTORE`: its regular charge and refund, then the limits, then the history give-back |
| clear-back: `x → 0 → x` (`SATIN-ACCT-004`, `SATIN-ACCT-016`) | First `WARM_STORAGE_READ_COST + SSTORE_WRITE_COST` and refund `+SSTORE_CLEAR_REFUND`; second `WARM_STORAGE_READ_COST` and refund `−SSTORE_CLEAR_REFUND + SSTORE_RESTORE_REFUND` | None | `+RECORD_HISTORY_GAS`, then `−RECORD_HISTORY_GAS` | None | +1, then −1 | `+WRITE_RECORD_SIZE`, then `−WRITE_RECORD_SIZE` | The frame running the second `SSTORE`, into its reservoir | Second `SSTORE`: its regular charge and refund, then the limits, then the history give-back |
| rewrite: `0 → x → y` (`SATIN-STATE-008`, `SATIN-ACCT-016`) | First `WARM_STORAGE_READ_COST + SSTORE_WRITE_COST`; second `WARM_STORAGE_READ_COST`, no refund | `+SLOT_STATE_GAS × m` once, its legacy share from regular gas first; the second write charges and refills nothing | `+RECORD_HISTORY_GAS` once | +1 once | +1 once | `+WRITE_RECORD_SIZE` once | No give-back | First `SSTORE`: its regular and state charges, then the limits, then the history charge |
| again: `0 → x → 0 → x` (`SATIN-STATE-008`, `SATIN-ACCT-016`) | `WARM_STORAGE_READ_COST + SSTORE_WRITE_COST`, `WARM_STORAGE_READ_COST` with refund `+SSTORE_RESTORE_REFUND`, `WARM_STORAGE_READ_COST + SSTORE_WRITE_COST`; the refund stays | Charged with its legacy share, refilled into the reservoir, charged with its legacy share again | Charged, given back into the reservoir, charged | +1, −1, +1 | +1, −1, +1 | `WRITE_RECORD_SIZE` added, taken back, added | The frame running the second `SSTORE`, for its give-backs | Each `SSTORE` in the order of zero-back or rewrite |
| rolled-back: a write discarded by the revert or halt of the writing frame or of a frame containing it (`SATIN-POOL-014`, `SATIN-ACCT-011`) | The `SSTORE`'s regular gas stays spent; a revert returns the failing frame's unspent regular gas to its caller, a halt consumes it; the failing frame's refund-counter changes, those merged into it included, are discarded | Given back by the rollback into the failing frame's reservoir — on a revert or a stop by `reservoir = reservoir + net_charged` (`SATIN-POOL-014`), on a halt the reservoir it received, what regular gas paid being consumed with it | As state gas | Discarded with the frame | Discarded; a record the frame took back stands again | Discarded | The failing frame, by its rollback | At the failing frame's end |
| descendant: a write a frame made that another frame running on the same storage takes back — a descendant by `DELEGATECALL`, `CALLCODE` or a call back into the writing contract, or a frame started on that storage after the writer returned successfully (`SATIN-HIST-007`, `SATIN-TAKE-002`) | The descendant pays `WARM_STORAGE_READ_COST`; its refund change, that of the value row of its write (zero-back, restore or clear-back), is on its own counter, which merges into its caller's when it succeeds and reaches the writer only when every frame between them succeeds (`SATIN-TAKE-003`) | A fresh slot (zero original): the writer paid the charge and the descendant receives the refill; a non-zero original: none | The writer paid the charge; the descendant receives the give-back | A fresh slot: −1 on the descendant's net, which can be negative; a non-zero original: none | −1 on the descendant's net | `−WRITE_RECORD_SIZE` on the descendant's net | The descendant, into its reservoir; when it fails, its give-backs are discarded, the record stands again and the writer's charges stay paid | In the descendant's `SSTORE`, as zero-back; merged or discarded at its return |
| ancestor: a write a descendant made and merged by succeeding, taken back by an ancestor (`SATIN-HIST-007`) | The ancestor's `SSTORE` and refund, as the value row of its write | A fresh slot: the ancestor receives the refill; a non-zero original: none | The ancestor receives the give-back | A fresh slot: −1 on the ancestor's net; a non-zero original: none | −1 on the ancestor's net | `−WRITE_RECORD_SIZE` on the ancestor's net | The ancestor, into its reservoir | In the ancestor's `SSTORE`, as zero-back |
| refused: a write whose record crosses a limit (`SATIN-HIST-013`, `SATIN-STOP-004`) | The regular charge stays spent; the frame is stopped and reverts with the gas it has left | A fresh-slot charge the write made before the limits is given back by the stopped frame's rollback | Not charged | Not counted | Not counted | Not counted | The stopped frame, by its rollback | The regular and state charges, then the limit that crosses; no history |

rows: destruct-back: an account a SELFDESTRUCT returns to what the transaction loaded, of an account not created in the transaction (SATIN-HIST-006, SATIN-SD-012)

failed-new: a value CALL to an account empty under EIP-161 that returns without that account added — such an account has no code, so this is a precompile at an empty address that fails, a start a limit stops, or a start refused after the charge (the precompile-failed, start-stopped, answer-stopped and refused rows of SATIN-TAKE-010) (SATIN-HIST-010, SATIN-POOL-015, SATIN-HIST-014)
keyless-back: a keyless deployment from signer nonce 1 whose creation's bump is set back (SATIN-KEY-013)
self: a value CALLCODE, or a value CALL to the calling account itself (SATIN-ACCT-007, SATIN-LOG-003)
sent-back: value sent from P to Q and sent back from Q to P, neither empty under EIP-161 (SATIN-ACCT-004, SATIN-ACCT-006, SATIN-HIST-009)
SATIN-TAKE-006.text:
- `SATIN-TAKE-006` An account's nonce, balance or code written and taken back MUST be accounted as this table states, an account's record existing while it differs from what the transaction loaded (`SATIN-ACCT-004`); the sender, whose account is a fixed record of the body, makes none (`SATIN-ACCT-008`):

| Pattern | Regular gas and EIP-3529 refund | State gas | History gas | State growth | KV updates | Data size | Frame credited | Order |
| ------- | ------------------------------- | --------- | ----------- | ------------ | ---------- | --------- | -------------- | ----- |
| sent-back: value sent from P to Q and sent back from Q to P, neither empty under EIP-161 (`SATIN-ACCT-004`, `SATIN-ACCT-006`, `SATIN-HIST-009`) | Each call's regular charges, `VALUE_TRANSFER_COST` among them; no refund | None | Each start, judged against what the transaction loaded: its caller pays `RECORD_HISTORY_GAS` after the forward for each record the start makes — an account the transfer changes that did not differ yet, never the sender (`SATIN-ACCT-008`) or a marked account — and is given back the price of each record the start takes back, an account the transfer returns to what was loaded; for P and Q unchanged before the round trip the first start makes two and the second takes both back, and for P and Q whose balances an earlier transfer between them already changed the first takes two back and the second makes two | None | On each start's frame, +1 for each record it makes and −1 for each it takes back | On each start's frame, `+WRITE_RECORD_SIZE` for each record it makes, `−WRITE_RECORD_SIZE` for each it takes back, and `+TRANSFER_LOG_SIZE`: both transfer logs stay while both starts are kept, a failing start's log being discarded with its frame | The caller of each start that takes records back, into its reservoir, once that start's frame returned with its start kept; if that frame fails, the records stand again and nothing is given back | Each start: its regular charges, the forward, then the history of the records it makes; the give-back of the records it takes back at its return, after the reservoir join of `SATIN-POOL-012` |
| destruct-back: an account a `SELFDESTRUCT` returns to what the transaction loaded, of an account not created in the transaction (`SATIN-HIST-006`, `SATIN-SD-012`) | The `SELFDESTRUCT`'s regular charge; no refund | None | `RECORD_HISTORY_GAS` given back for each record the move takes back — each account it returns to what was loaded that had a record, the sender having none (`SATIN-ACCT-008`) — before the history of a record the move makes is charged | None | −1 for each record taken back | `−WRITE_RECORD_SIZE` for each record taken back, `+TRANSFER_LOG_SIZE` for the move | The frame running the `SELFDESTRUCT`, into its reservoir | `SATIN-SD-019`: its charges, then the records it takes back, then its positive effects held to the limits, then the history of the records it makes |
| failed-new: a value `CALL` to an account empty under EIP-161 that returns without that account added — such an account has no code, so this is a precompile at an empty address that fails, a start a limit stops, or a start refused after the charge (the precompile-failed, start-stopped, answer-stopped and refused rows of `SATIN-TAKE-010`) (`SATIN-HIST-010`, `SATIN-POOL-015`, `SATIN-HIST-014`) | The call's regular charges stay spent | `+ACCOUNT_STATE_GAS × m` charged to the caller before the forward, its 25,000-gas legacy share from regular gas first, given back into the caller's reservoir, share included, after the reservoir the child returns was joined (`SATIN-POOL-012`) | The start's records charged to the caller after the forward, given back to the caller when the call returns without the account; a start refused for a value its caller cannot fund makes none and is charged none (`SATIN-HIST-015`) | +1 on the start, discarded; none for a refused start | The start's records, discarded; none for a refused start | The start's records and transfer log, discarded; none for a refused start | The caller, into its reservoir | `SATIN-HIST-010` at the call; at the return the reservoir join, then the state give-back, then the records' give-back |
| self: a value `CALLCODE`, or a value `CALL` to the calling account itself (`SATIN-ACCT-007`, `SATIN-LOG-003`) | The call's regular charges | None | None | None | None | None: no record and no transfer log | No give-back | None |
| keyless-back: a keyless deployment from signer nonce 1 whose creation's bump is set back (`SATIN-KEY-013`) | The call's regular charges | Step 10 charged nothing (the signer is not empty) | The history step 14 charged for the signer's record — none when the transaction had changed the signer's account already, the sender among such accounts — given back when the set-back leaves the signer as loaded | None | The signer's record: none when the set-back leaves the account as loaded | None for the signer's record | The keyless call, into its reservoir | At the creation's return, by the nonce rule of `SATIN-KEY-013`, before the call answers |

rows: absent-leaf: an account absent at the transaction's start, created and destroyed (SATIN-SD-004, SATIN-SD-005, SATIN-SD-006, SATIN-SD-007)
after-destroy: code deposited after the constructor destroyed its own account (SATIN-SD-014, SATIN-SD-015)
code: deployed code of the destroyed account (SATIN-SD-004, SATIN-SD-008)
collision: a creation onto an address with code or a nonce (SATIN-SD-016, SATIN-LIM-016)
discarded: the destroying frame, or a frame containing it, fails (SATIN-SD-010)
failed-create: a CREATE or CREATE2 whose child reverts or halts (SATIN-POOL-015, SATIN-HIST-014, SATIN-LIM-008)
first-frame: a creation transaction whose own frame destroys the created account (SATIN-HIST-005, SATIN-SD-007)
fresh-slot: a slot whose original value is zero, non-zero before the destruction (SATIN-SD-003, SATIN-SD-004)

funded-then-created: an address absent at the transaction's start that the transaction funded, then created onto and destroyed; an address that held a balance before the transaction is the present-leaf row (SATIN-SD-005, SATIN-SD-006)
loaded-slot: a slot whose original value is not zero, which only a slot loaded before the creation has (SATIN-SD-003, SATIN-SD-004, SATIN-SD-019)

marked: the marked account and its slots after the first effective destruction — a later SELFDESTRUCT of it, an SSTORE of one of its slots, value sent to it or from it, a bump of its nonce (SATIN-SD-011, SATIN-SD-013, SATIN-SD-015)
present-leaf: a leaf in the state at the transaction's start — funded before, or empty under EIP-161 with storage (SATIN-SD-006, SATIN-SD-017)
SATIN-TAKE-007.section: Specification > Created account and the destruction table
SATIN-TAKE-007.text:
- `SATIN-TAKE-007` An account created in the transaction and destroyed by its first effective `SELFDESTRUCT`, and a creation that fails, MUST be accounted as this table states, the destruction table's give-back going to the destroying frame whichever frame paid, and following `SATIN-SD-019`'s order: the opcode's charges, the table's give-back, the positive effects held to the limits, the history of the records the opcode makes:

| Pattern | Regular gas and EIP-3529 refund | State gas | History gas | State growth | KV updates | Data size | Frame credited | Order |
| ------- | ------------------------------- | --------- | ----------- | ------------ | ---------- | --------- | -------------- | ----- |
| absent-leaf: an account absent at the transaction's start, created and destroyed (`SATIN-SD-004`, `SATIN-SD-005`, `SATIN-SD-006`, `SATIN-SD-007`) | The `SELFDESTRUCT`'s regular charge; the refund counter is not touched by the table | Refill of the leaf's charge `ACCOUNT_STATE_GAS × m` | `RECORD_HISTORY_GAS` given back for the account's record | −1 | −1 | `−WRITE_RECORD_SIZE` | The destroying frame, into its reservoir | `SATIN-SD-019` step 2 |
